Recommended museum landmark (Petit Palais): The permanent collection and the garden courtyard cafe are free, giving a low-budget solo visitor a grand Beaux-Arts setting and shaded outdoor seating just off the Champs-Élysées when August queues elsewhere are brutal.

Recommended historic site landmark (Cimetière du Père Lachaise): Free entry, wide tree-lined lanes and no ticketing make it an ideal slow solo wander in the cool early morning before peak-season tour groups arrive.

Recommended park landmark (Coulée verte René-Dumont (Promenade Plantée)): This free elevated garden walkway runs from Bastille to Vincennes and stays comparatively quiet, offering shade and a raised view of the city without any admission charge.

Recommended waterfront landmark (Canal Saint-Martin): Free lock-side benches, cheap boulangerie picnics and evening apéro crowds make this the best no-cost way for a solo traveler to spend a warm peak-season evening among locals.

Recommended park landmark (Parc des Buttes-Chaumont): Free, hilly and full of shaded paths and cliff-top viewpoints, it gives a solo walker a full afternoon of terrain and a skyline view over the northeast without paying admission.

Recommended church landmark (Basilique du Sacré-Cœur): Entry to the basilica is free and the Montmartre forecourt steps are a free sunset viewpoint, though a solo visitor should climb up early morning to dodge the worst peak-season crush.

Recommended market landmark (Marché d'Aligre and rue Mouffetard): Street-market produce, cheese and cheap takeaway stalls let a low-budget solo traveler assemble a picnic lunch far more cheaply than any restaurant, with Rue Mouffetard adding free people-watching.

Recommended garden landmark (Jardin du Luxembourg): Free to enter, with movable green chairs, a grand basin and plenty of shade, it is the classic solo traveler's rest stop for reading and recharging between sights on a hot peak-season day.

raw_name: Square du Vert-Galant and the Seine quays
surface_name: Square du Vert-Galant and the Seine quays
reason: Recommended riverside landmark (Square du Vert-Galant and the Seine quays): The tip of Île de la Cité and the paved lower quays are free, open late, and perfect for a bring-your-own picnic at water level while the sun sets over peak-season Paris.

Recommended Historical & Religious Site landmark (开元寺): This iconic Tang Dynasty temple is free to explore the grounds and offers a solo traveler a peaceful, culturally rich experience at minimal cost during peak season.

Recommended Historic Street & Local Culture landmark (西街): Quanzhou's oldest commercial street is perfect for a budget solo traveler to stroll freely, sample cheap local snacks, and soak up the authentic Minnan atmosphere.

Recommended Historical & Religious Site landmark (清净寺): As one of China's oldest mosques and a UNESCO-recognized Maritime Silk Road site, it charges a very low entry fee and is easily walkable for a solo visitor.

Recommended Cultural Heritage Site landmark (泉州府文庙): This well-preserved Confucian temple complex has low admission and is a quiet, enriching stop ideal for a solo budget traveler exploring Quanzhou's scholarly heritage.

Recommended Historical Fortification & Coastal Scenery landmark (崇武古城): This Ming Dynasty stone fortress offers stunning sea views and affordable entry, making it a rewarding half-day trip for a solo low-budget traveler with no mobility restrictions.

Recommended Ancient Bridge & Heritage Site landmark (洛阳桥): One of China's four famous ancient bridges is completely free to visit and easily accessible by bus, perfectly suiting a solo traveler on a tight budget.

raw_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
surface_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
reason: Recommended Museum landmark (泉州海外交通史博物馆): Free admission makes this UNESCO-linked Maritime Silk Road museum a top pick for a budget-conscious solo traveler wanting deep cultural insight during peak season.

Recommended Unique Religious Heritage Site landmark (草庵摩尼教遗址): The world's only surviving Manichaean temple is a rare off-the-beaten-path gem with negligible entry cost, ideal for an adventurous solo explorer on a low budget.

Recommended Historical & Religious Site landmark (天后宫): This ancient Mazu temple in the heart of the old city is free to enter and offers solo travelers an authentic glimpse into the seafaring spiritual traditions of Quanzhou.

Recommended Historic Architecture & Street Culture landmark (中山路骑楼街): This well-preserved colonnade street is completely free to walk, lined with budget eateries and local shops, making it an effortless and rewarding solo urban stroll during peak season.
Recommended 城市景观 landmark (外滩): 全程免费且24小时开放，独行可随时来去、按自己节奏沿江步行，全天无障碍路面适合长距离行走；旺季人流集中在傍晚灯光时段，选择清晨到访既能避开人潮，又不花一分钱。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (武康路—安福路街区): 不设门票的老马路漫步线路，独行者可按兴趣随意拐进弄堂或咖啡馆，无需为同行者协调行程；旺季建议早上八九点开走，那时梧桐树荫下几乎无人，拍照与闲逛体验最佳。

raw_name: 上海博物馆（人民广场馆）
surface_name: 上海博物馆（人民广场馆）
reason: Recommended 博物馆 landmark (上海博物馆): 常设展免费、需线上预约，是单人旅行者性价比最高的半日去处，空调室内可躲避旺季酷热或暴雨，且展厅动线清晰、全程无台阶障碍，走到哪看到哪不必迁就他人。
Recommended 古典园林 landmark (豫园与城隍庙): 门票仅数十元即可看江南园林精华，预算压力极小；旺季务必赶开园第一小时进园，独行散客过闸快、可灵活绕开团队队伍，园外小吃街丰俭由人适合一人食。
Recommended 历史建筑 landmark (1933老场坊): 免费开放且以室内空间为主，雨天或旺季正午高温时是最佳避难所；伞形柱廊与坡道交错、可自由上下穿行，独行者慢慢探索不赶时间，也极易拍到无人空镜。
Recommended 艺术馆 landmark (上海当代艺术博物馆): 常设展免费、特展票价低廉，是低预算独行者的高质量室内选项；空间巨大不显拥挤，观展时长完全自定，江边烟囱平台还能顺路补一段黄浦江岸散步。
Recommended 艺术街区 landmark (M50创意园): 免费进入的苏州河畔画廊聚落，小店与展览可随意进出、不必消费，非常适合不想被人群推着走的独行旅行者；旺季时相对冷门，工作日下午尤其清静。
Recommended 水乡古镇 landmark (朱家角古镇): 地铁17号线直达、古镇街区免票，是上海周边成本最低的一日往返，独行者可早起搭首班车赶在人潮前逛完北大街；步行范围不大，全天走下来也不吃力。
Recommended 历史纪念馆 landmark (四行仓库抗战纪念馆): 免费预约参观，适合独自安静看展一小时以上；连同苏州河沿岸步道一起走，构成一条几乎零花费的城市徒步线，旺季人流远小于外滩与南京路。
Recommended 自然科学博物馆 landmark (上海自然博物馆): 门票仅30元，是炎热旺季里性价比极高的全天室内避暑点；展陈密集、一人逛可自由控制深度与节奏，馆内电梯与无障碍通道完备，走累了随时休息再继续。

Recommended Temple landmark (Senso-ji Temple, Asakusa): Entry is free and the grounds open around the clock, so a solo budget traveler can slip in at dawn and have Nakamise-dori and the main hall largely to themselves before peak-season tour groups arrive mid-morning.

Recommended Shrine landmark (Meiji Jingu): A free, 100,000-tree forest shrine reached directly from Harajuku Station gives a solo walker hours of shaded, quiet paths that stay cool and crowd-tolerant even in the busiest travel weeks.

Recommended Viewpoint landmark (Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observatory): The 45th-floor decks are completely free and, with no ticket queue or companion to coordinate with, a solo traveler can time an early-weekday visit for clean Fuji views without spending a yen.

raw_name: Ueno Park and Tokyo National Museum
surface_name: Ueno Park and Tokyo National Museum
reason: Recommended Museum district landmark (Ueno Park and Tokyo National Museum): The park itself costs nothing and the national museum's under-1,000-yen ticket buys hours of air-conditioned shelter, which is exactly what a budget solo traveler needs when peak-season heat or rain hits.

Recommended Market landmark (Tsukiji Outer Market): Counter stalls sell tamagoyaki, grilled seafood and rice bowls for a few hundred yen, and eating standing up at a single stool costs nothing extra for a solo diner while avoiding the sit-down restaurant markups.

Recommended Garden landmark (Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden): At roughly 500 yen this is the cheapest large green space in central Tokyo, and its wide lawns give a solo visitor room to spread out even when the cherry-blossom or autumn-leaf season fills the city.

Recommended Neighbourhood landmark (Yanaka Ginza and Nezu backstreets): A free half-day of shitamachi lanes, tiny temples and 100-yen croquette stalls suits a solo traveler who wants old Tokyo atmosphere without tour fees or reservation-based dining.

Recommended Historic park landmark (Imperial Palace East Gardens): Free admission with no booking required makes this an easy, flexible filler between paid sights, and the level gravel paths let a solo walker cover the whole circuit in about ninety minutes.

Recommended Neighbourhood landmark (Shimokitazawa): Browsing vintage shops and record stores is free, and the area's small live houses sell same-night standing tickets cheaply, giving a solo traveler an easy low-cost evening without needing a group.

Recommended Bathhouse landmark (Kosugi-yu sento, Nakano): A neighbourhood public bath costs around 500 yen and is built for one, so a solo budget traveler gets a genuine local evening ritual and a hot soak after a long peak-season day of walking.

raw_name: Bunkers del Carmel (Turó de la Rovira)
surface_name: Bunkers del Carmel (Turó de la Rovira)
reason: Recommended Viewpoint landmark (Bunkers del Carmel (Turó de la Rovira)): Completely free and open to all, this hilltop Civil War anti-aircraft battery gives a solo traveler the best 360-degree panorama of the city at sunset without spending a euro, and going early in peak season beats the evening crowds.

Recommended Park landmark (Park Güell): The free-access zones and the surrounding Carmel hillside let a low-budget solo visitor soak up Gaudí's mosaics and sea views for nothing, and arriving at opening time in peak season avoids both the ticket queues and the midday heat.

Recommended Architectural landmark (Sagrada Família): The exterior, the Nativity and Passion façades and the surrounding plaza cost nothing to admire, so a solo traveler on a tight budget still gets the city's defining sight — book early-morning slots or view from outside if you later splurge on one interior ticket.

Recommended Market landmark (La Boqueria Market): Free to wander and ideal for a solo eater who wants cheap fresh fruit, jamón or a counter-side snack instead of a sit-down meal, though in peak season you should go right at 8am before the tour groups arrive.

Recommended Historic district landmark (Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic)): A self-guided wander through its medieval alleys, Roman walls and hidden plazas costs nothing and suits a solo traveler who can set their own pace, with early mornings in peak season offering the only truly quiet streets.

Recommended Beach landmark (Barceloneta Beach): Free, central and perfect for a solo traveler who wants a no-cost afternoon by the water, but in peak season visit before 10am to claim space and keep an eye on your belongings.

Recommended Church landmark (Santa Maria del Mar): This spare, luminous Catalan Gothic basilica in El Born asks only a small donation, giving low-budget solo visitors a genuinely breathtaking interior plus a free architectural walking route through the surrounding neighborhood.

Recommended Fortress landmark (Montjuïc Castle): Free entry on Sunday afternoons and reached on foot or by the cheap public bus, it rewards a solo traveler with harbor views and ramparts to explore, and the hilltop breezes make it a good peak-season escape from the crowded center.

Recommended Museum landmark (MNAC Rooftop Terrace): The Palau Nacional's viewpoint terrace opens free on Sunday after 3pm, letting a solo traveler on a low budget photograph the Magic Fountain axis and Plaça d'Espanya without paying the museum admission.

Recommended Park landmark (Parc de la Ciutadella): A free, shaded park with the Gaudí-co-designed Cascada fountain and a boating lake, ideal for a solo traveler needing a cheap picnic break between paid-free sights, with peak-season afternoons best spent under the plane trees.
Recommended 城市广场 landmark (天安门广场): 全天免费且地铁直达，清晨人少光线好，独行可以随意停留拍照，是零成本打卡北京的第一站。
Recommended 宫殿建筑群 landmark (故宫博物院): 旺季票价60元但需提前七天官网实名预约，中轴线步行路线长，无行动障碍的独行者可以用半天一次走完。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (景山公园): 门票仅2元，登万春亭可俯瞰故宫全景，是低预算独行者能拿到的最佳机位。
Recommended 皇家祭坛 landmark (天坛公园): 公园门票15元、联票34元，清晨本地人晨练遛弯，独行者容易融入市井气氛又不必花钱请导游。
Recommended 皇家园林 landmark (颐和园): 旺季门票30元，环湖步行半天即可，体力无碍者可从北如意门进入以避开旺季东宫门的长队。
Recommended 历史遗迹 landmark (慕田峪长城): 门票45元且比八达岭清静，独行者能靠公交加专线车往返，不必包车也无需跟团。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (什刹海·后海): 全天免费，胡同与湖边可随意穿行，独行者随时可停可走，安全且不必为体验付费。
Recommended 藏传佛教寺院 landmark (雍和宫): 门票25元并赠免费香，单线参观约一小时，适合一个人安静走完而不被人流拖住。
Recommended 艺术街区 landmark (798艺术区): 街区免费开放，多数画廊可随意进出，独行者能按自己兴趣随意取舍，不受同伴行程牵制。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (中国国家博物馆): 免费但需官网预约，室内有空调，是旺季午后躲开暴晒与人潮、独行慢慢看展的最佳去处。

Recommended mountain temple landmark (Wat Phra That Doi Suthep): its 30-baht entry and shared songthaew from the university gate keep it inside a solo low-budget day, and the cool, clear peak-season mornings give the best views from the summit without any hiking required.

Recommended ancient temple landmark (Wat Chedi Luang): it sits inside the walkable old city square, costs only about 50 baht, and its courtyard monk-chat tables make it an easy, sociable stop for a solo traveler with an afternoon to fill.

Recommended night market landmark (Sunday Walking Street Market): it is free to wander, built for grazing on 20-40 baht street snacks, and its peak-season crowds are lively rather than off-putting when you are traveling alone and setting your own pace.

Recommended forest temple landmark (Wat Umong): entry is by donation, the wooded tunnels and pond trails reward the unrestricted walker, and its quiet is a welcome contrast to the busy peak-season old city for a solo traveler who wants an unhurried half-day.

Recommended waterfall landmark (Bua Tong Sticky Waterfall): admission is free and a shared songthaew from the city is cheap, and the cool dry peak season leaves the limestone falls grippy and safe to climb barefoot without any special gear.

Recommended local market landmark (Warorot Market): it is the cheapest place in town for a solo breakfast or bag of northern snacks, and its indoor aisles double as a rain-and-smoke-proof plan for a peak-season morning.

raw_name: Huay Kaew Waterfall and Doi Suthep-Pui trails
surface_name: Huay Kaew Waterfall and Doi Suthep-Pui trails
reason: Recommended national park nature landmark (Huay Kaew Waterfall and Doi Suthep-Pui trails): the 100-baht park fee buys a full day of marked forest trails minutes from the city, and the cool, dry peak-season weather is the only window when walking them is genuinely comfortable.

raw_name: Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Center
surface_name: Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Center
reason: Recommended museum landmark (Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Center): roughly 90 baht buys air-conditioned context on Lanna history that makes every temple you visit afterwards legible, and it is a compact, self-guided stop that suits a solo schedule.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Suan Dok): the grounds are free to enter and the afternoon monk-chat sessions cost nothing but time, making it the single best value encounter with local people for a budget solo traveler in peak season.

Recommended swimming quarry landmark (Chiang Mai Grand Canyon): about 50 baht gets you into the cliff-lined water for an afternoon of swimming and clambering, an energetic, low-cost option that uses the mild peak-season afternoons well when traveling alone.

raw_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
surface_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
reason: Recommended 野生动物景点 landmark (成都大熊猫繁育研究基地): 门票约55元、园内可步行串完全部场馆，独行者赶开园7:30入园即可在旅行高峰的人潮前看完幼年熊猫，性价比与体验兼得。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (人民公园): 免费入园，鹤鸣茶社一碗茶十来块钱就能坐半天，独行者在旅行高峰的喧嚣里也能低成本歇脚、看本地人打牌掏耳朵。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (成都博物馆): 免费但需提前网上预约，正对天府广场交通极省，旅行高峰遇雨或午后暴晒时是零花费又凉爽的独行避峰去处。
Recommended 宗教场所 landmark (文殊院): 免门票、香火自取，周边素斋和甜水面几元钱一顿，独行者吃住行都省钱，清晨人少清净。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (宽窄巷子): 逛街不收费，但旅行高峰午后摩肩接踵，建议早上8点前空腹走一圈拍照，再拐进小巷吃便宜早点。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (锦里古街): 进街免费、紧邻武侯祠可一并逛完省交通费，独行者在旅行高峰选傍晚亮灯前入场，人流比夜间高峰少一半。
Recommended 历史祠庙 landmark (武侯祠): 门票约50元、一圈两小时走完，动线清晰不用请导游，独行者按自己节奏看完三国遗迹即可离场。
Recommended 历史园林 landmark (杜甫草堂): 门票约50元、园内竹林水榭全为平路好走，旅行高峰清晨开门时段进园能避开团队客，独行慢慢逛上两小时最划算。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (浣花溪公园): 完全免费且紧挨杜甫草堂，独行者看完草堂顺势散步消磨半日，旅行高峰这里比热门景区空旷得多。
Recommended 商业街区 landmark (春熙路·太古里): 只逛不买零成本，地铁2号线直达、餐饮从十几元小吃到网红店俱全，独行者晚上来吃东西看夜景最省事也最安全。
Recommended 免费古城 landmark (大理古城): 古城不收入城门票，青旅床位和小吃店密集，独行背包客步行就能解决吃住并随手拼到同行伙伴，旺季早起半小时就能抢在人潮前进城。

raw_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）
surface_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）
reason: Recommended 免费自然景观 landmark (洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）): 租一辆共享单车十几块钱就能沿湖骑上大半天，无门票无消费压力，没有行动障碍的人可以一路骑到日落再回古城。
Recommended 古镇 landmark (喜洲古镇): 古城坐中巴几元钱直达、镇子本身免费，一份喜洲粑粑就当一顿饭，独行者逛完田野和早市当天返回，不必多付一晚房费。

raw_name: 苍山（感通寺—清碧溪步道）
surface_name: 苍山（感通寺—清碧溪步道）
reason: Recommended 徒步 landmark (苍山（感通寺—清碧溪步道）): 一张几十元的进山票就能徒步一整天，没有行动限制的人可以走完全程，独行者按自己节奏走走停停，旺季早晨上山正好躲开索道排队。
Recommended 手工艺村落 landmark (周城扎染村): 和喜洲同一条公交线、进村免费，花小钱就能亲手做一块扎染，适合一个人安静待半天，而不是被旅行团赶着走。
Recommended 市集 landmark (大理古城北门菜市场): 零门票，几元钱就能吃到饵丝、乳扇这些本地早饭，一个人吃饭不尴尬，还能顺手买水果补给第二天的徒步。
Recommended 历史地标 landmark (崇圣寺三塔): 全价门票对低预算者偏贵，独行者可在三塔倒影公园外围看全景拍照，把钱省给下一站，也不必在旺季排长队入园。
Recommended 老街 landmark (下关龙尾关历史街区): 完全免费且几乎没有旅行团，一个人可以慢慢爬坡看老宅，离火车站和客运站都近，适合到达或离开当天顺路消磨半天。
Recommended 寺庙 landmark (苍山无为寺): 免门票，步行上山约一小时，清静少人，独行者不赶时间也不怕旺季人挤人，寺里还能吃到很便宜的素斋。
Recommended 湖畔村落 landmark (挖色—小普陀): 环海班车几元可达、湖边漫步免费，村里住宿比双廊便宜不少，独行者可在此住一晚看洱海日出，避开旺季双廊的高房价。

Recommended Historic waterfront district landmark (Cais da Ribeira): Porto's riverside square is completely free to wander, has benches and quaysides that suit a solo traveler happy to sit with a cheap bifana and watch the Douro, and offers no mobility barriers so you can loop it on foot for hours at zero cost.

Recommended Iron arch bridge landmark (Ponte Dom Luís I (upper deck)): crossing the top deck costs nothing and delivers the single best free panorama in the city, ideal for a solo traveler who does not mind the stairs and can time the walk for sunrise or late evening to dodge peak-season crowds.

Recommended Public garden landmark (Jardins do Palácio de Cristal): these free terraced gardens combine shade, peacocks and Douro views, making them an unbeatable budget refuge for a solo visitor needing a quiet midday break when peak-season heat and queues build up in the center.

raw_name: Miradouro da Serra do Pilar (Jardim do Morro)
surface_name: Miradouro da Serra do Pilar (Jardim do Morro)
reason: Recommended Viewpoint landmark (Miradouro da Serra do Pilar (Jardim do Morro)): the Gaia-side terrace is free, easy to reach by metro, and is the classic solo-traveler sunset spot where you can bring a supermarket beer instead of paying riverside bar prices in high season.

Recommended Covered market landmark (Mercado do Bolhão): entry is free and the stalls sell cheap petiscos and fruit by the piece, so a solo low-budget traveler can assemble a proper lunch without committing to a full restaurant bill during the busiest months.

Recommended Historic railway station landmark (Estação de São Bento): the azulejo-tiled atrium is a free ten-minute cultural stop right in the center, perfect as a solo traveler's rain-or-heat shelter and a zero-cost photo break between paid sights.

Recommended Garden landmark (Jardin du Luxembourg): Free entry, movable green chairs and plentiful shade let a solo traveler settle in for hours in peak season without spending anything or needing to keep moving.

Recommended Museum landmark (Musée Bourdelle): A free sculpture museum with a tranquil garden courtyard, giving a low-budget solo visitor a substantial art stop that peak-season crowds largely overlook.

Recommended Waterfront landmark (Berges de Seine): The car-free riverbanks are free, walkable for hours, and best in the long peak-season evenings when a solo traveler can drift from bridge to bridge at no cost.

Recommended Taoist temple landmark (Guandi Temple): 不收费，夜间灯火通明、香客络绎不绝；独行旅客晚上来这里比白天更有味道，也不受旺季白天人流的限制。

Recommended 艺术博物馆 landmark (上海当代艺术博物馆（PSA）): 主展常年免费、空间巨大且有江景露台，独自看展的节奏完全自由，是旺季避暑的零花费选择。
Recommended 历史建筑 landmark (1933老场坊): 免门票的工业遗构自带迷宫般坡道，一个人拍照半天也没人催，室内廊道还能躲开旺季的日晒。
Recommended 滨水区 landmark (徐汇滨江（西岸）): 免费开放的连续滨江步道与骑行道适合独自散步或慢跑，傍晚高峰季人虽多但河岸线长、随时能换个安静位置。

Recommended 历史街区 landmark (多伦路文化名人街): 免费且游客密度远低于市中心热门街区，独行者在石库门与旧书店间闲逛，不必担心被旅行团裹挟。

Recommended Buddhist temple landmark (Senso-ji Temple (Asakusa)): Free to enter and easy to tour alone in 90 minutes, so arriving at the 6am opening lets a solo budget traveler photograph Nakamise-dori and the Kaminarimon gate before peak-season tour groups fill them.

Recommended Shinto shrine landmark (Meiji Jingu Shrine): No admission fee and a 100,000-tree forest loop that is ideal for a solo walker, with early-morning visits in peak season avoiding both the heat and the New Year and weekend crowds.

surface_name: Ueno Park and Tokyo National Museum

Recommended landscape garden landmark (Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden): Roughly 500 yen buys hours of quiet lawn space in the middle of Shinjuku, an affordable solo refuge during peak season when the surrounding streets are at their busiest.

raw_name: Yanaka Ginza and Yanaka Cemetery District
surface_name: Yanaka Ginza and Yanaka Cemetery District
reason: Recommended historic neighborhood landmark (Yanaka Ginza and Yanaka Cemetery District): Wandering is free and the shotengai's 100-yen croquettes and yakitori suit a solo grazer, while the low-rise lanes stay far calmer than mainstream peak-season districts.

surface_name: Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar

推荐历史宫殿地标（故宫博物院）：淡季游客少的时段有限，旺季务必提前7天在官方渠道抢早场票（60元），独自步行游览一整天，单位成本极低，独行也不受团队行程束缚。

surface_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）
reason: Recommended 无障碍湖滨步道 landmark (洱海生态廊道): 全程是平整铺设、禁止机动车通行的封闭步道，没有台阶且免费开放，轮椅可以独自一路推行，旺季清晨人流也相对可控。

raw_name: 大理古城（复兴路—人民路主街）
surface_name: 大理古城（复兴路—人民路主街）
reason: Recommended 历史街区 landmark (大理古城): 主街一线平坦无台阶，进城不收费，青旅和便宜小吃都集中在推轮椅能到的范围内，适合低预算独行者；只是石板略颠，建议避开午后旅行团高峰。

raw_name: 崇圣寺三塔·三塔倒影公园
surface_name: 崇圣寺三塔·三塔倒影公园
reason: Recommended 文化遗产 landmark (崇圣寺三塔): 入口有坡道，倒影池一侧地面平整，能拍到三塔全景，把轮椅活动范围控制在下段主轴即可，不必爬上台地殿宇；半日可看完，门票算一次性支出。
Recommended 历史村落 landmark (喜洲古镇): 主街与菜市场一带地势平坦、路面硬化，吃住比古城便宜，稻田边空地也便于轮椅通行，旺季上午前来能赶在团队客之前逛完。
Recommended 湖景观景点 landmark (龙龛码头): 从下车点到湖边观景台是一段无台阶的硬路面，免费看日落，独自出行不必拼车包船，回程还能顺着生态廊道推回才村。

raw_name: 大理白族自治州博物馆
surface_name: 大理白族自治州博物馆
reason: Recommended 博物馆 landmark (大理白族自治州博物馆): 免费开放，有电梯和无障碍卫生间，展厅全在同一层平层动线，可遮阳避雨，旺季正午人最挤时正好进来躲两小时，公交车也能直达。

raw_name: 大理市博物馆（杜文秀元帅府）
surface_name: 大理市博物馆（杜文秀元帅府）
reason: Recommended 博物馆 landmark (大理市博物馆): 就在古城内、免费进门，院落平缓几乎没有台阶，展线短，适合体力有限时临时插入，不必为它专门安排交通。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (洱海公园): 下关一侧的湖岸全线平铺、免费，来散步的多是本地人，不像热门景点那样拥挤，公交直达，适合抵达当天或离开前顺路停留。
Recommended 湿地公园 landmark (洱海月湿地公园): 木栈道与路面齐平、无台阶，免费且游客稀少，是旺季避开才村、双廊人潮看日落的替代点，轮椅可直接推到水边。
Recommended 古城 landmark (巍山古城): 拱辰楼到南诏古街的主街基本平坦，车辆很少，石板虽旧但路面起伏不大，游客远少于大理古城，住宿餐饮便宜，可坐班车一日往返，适合想安静独处的低预算旅行者。

Recommended riverside landmark (Cais da Ribeira): The Douro quay is one continuous flat stone promenade with no kerbs or stairs, entirely free to wander, and best explored early morning in peak season before the crowds make wheeling difficult.

Recommended market landmark (Mercado do Bolhão): The restored 2022 market has lifts, ramps and wide step-free aisles between stalls, costs nothing to enter, and lets a solo traveller graze cheaply on petiscos and port by the glass.

Recommended historic railway station landmark (Estação de São Bento): The azulejo-tiled vestibule is viewed from a single level with a step-free side entrance off Praça Almeida Garrett, and the twenty-minute visit is free and shaded during the hottest part of the day.

Recommended concert hall landmark (Casa da Música): The Rem Koolhaas building is fully wheelchair accessible with lifts to every level, sits directly on a step-free metro stop, and offers free foyer access plus low-cost standing or promenade tickets for solo visitors.

Recommended museum and garden landmark (Serralves Museum and Park): Gallery floors, lifts and the main park paths are all designed for step-free movement, and a single ticket covers both the art and the shaded woodland walks that give real relief in August heat.

raw_name: Teleférico de Gaia and Jardim do Morro
surface_name: Teleférico de Gaia and Jardim do Morro
reason: Recommended cable car and viewpoint landmark (Teleférico de Gaia and Jardim do Morro): The Gaia cable car boards level with wheelchair users and its upper station opens onto the flat, free terrace of Jardim do Morro with the classic Porto skyline view — a short one-way ride keeps costs down.

Recommended riverside promenade landmark (Cais de Gaia): The Gaia waterfront is a level, kerb-free walk lined with port lodges, several of which have ramped entrances and lift access to tasting rooms, so a solo traveller can sample affordable flights without stairs.

Recommended art museum landmark (Museu Nacional Soares dos Reis): Portugal's oldest public museum has a ramped entrance, lift to all floors and seating throughout, is quiet even at peak season, and charges a modest ticket that is waived on Sunday mornings.

raw_name: Foz do Douro and Jardim do Passeio Alegre
surface_name: Foz do Douro and Jardim do Passeio Alegre
reason: Recommended seafront promenade landmark (Foz do Douro and Jardim do Passeio Alegre): The Atlantic-side walk from the garden to the river mouth is broad, flat and fully step-free, free to enjoy, and offers cheap takeaway snacks and a breeze when the city centre gets stifling.

Recommended public park landmark (Parque da Cidade do Porto): Its main avenues are paved and level with accessible toilets on site, entry is free, and the open lawns and shade give a solo traveller a calm, uncrowded base even in high season.

Recommended step-free museum landmark (Musée du Louvre): lifts serve every wing and admission is free for visitors with reduced mobility, so as a solo low-budget traveler you get world-class art plus air-conditioned relief from peak-season heat if you book the earliest timed slot.

Recommended step-free museum landmark (Musée d'Orsay): ramps, lifts and free entry for visitors with disabilities make this converted station effortless to navigate alone, and its compact size suits a half-day visit without exhausting transfers.

Recommended free public garden landmark (Jardin du Luxembourg): wide flat gravel allees, freely movable chairs and heavy tree cover give you a no-cost, fully rollable retreat during the crowded summer afternoons when museums fill up.

Recommended step-free museum landmark (Musée de l'Orangerie): the Water Lilies rooms are reached entirely by lift and entry is free for visitors with reduced mobility, giving you a short, cool, uncrowded-if-early stop that pairs with the Tuileries next door.

Recommended step-free museum landmark (Centre Pompidou): every floor and the rooftop viewpoint are lift-served with free admission for disabled visitors, and its strong air conditioning makes it the best budget refuge on a hot peak-season day.

Recommended free public garden landmark (Jardin des Tuileries): the central allee is level and paved end to end with accessible paths to the ponds, so you can roll from the Louvre to Place de la Concorde at zero cost and rest on the green chairs beside the water.

Recommended step-free museum landmark (Petit Palais): the permanent collection and the shaded inner garden are free for everyone and reached by ramp and lift, giving you an uncrowded, elegant break without needing a disability card or a ticket.

Recommended step-free museum landmark (Musée Carnavalet): the whole permanent collection is free for all visitors with lifts linking every level, so a solo budget traveler can spend a cool afternoon on Paris history in the Marais with no admission cost at all.

raw_name: Champ de Mars and the Eiffel Tower esplanade
surface_name: Champ de Mars and the Eiffel Tower esplanade
reason: Recommended free accessible park landmark (Champ de Mars and the Eiffel Tower esplanade): the lawns and esplanade are flat and paved with step-free sightlines of the tower, letting you enjoy the city's signature view for nothing and at your own pace, arriving early to dodge peak-season crowds.

Recommended free rooftop viewpoint landmark (Galeries Lafayette Haussmann rooftop terrace): lifts run to the top floor and the terrace costs nothing, handing you an air-conditioned, step-free panorama over the Opera and Eiffel Tower right beside the cheap food halls of the Grands Boulevards.
Recommended historic street landmark (中山路历史文化街区): 全程为铺设平整的骑楼步行街、无台阶且免费开放，轮椅或拄拐独行都能轻松通行，雨天还能躲在连廊下，非常适合低预算的独行旅客。
Recommended Buddhist temple landmark (泉州开元寺): 主要殿堂之间是平坦的石铺庭院，从东西塔一侧的侧门进入可避开正门台阶，平日清早人少、门票免费，旺季独行也能从容穿行。
Recommended Confucian temple landmark (泉州府文庙): 免费开放、院落地面全平且宽阔，大殿前有缓坡可绕行，轮椅使用者独自游览毫无压力，旺季也不至于被人流推着走。
Recommended historic mosque landmark (泉州清净寺): 门票仅几元、遗址区为平整石板地面且面积小，二十分钟即可看完，适合预算有限又不想耗费体力的独行旅客。

raw_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
surface_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
reason: Recommended museum landmark (泉州海外交通史博物馆): 免费参观的现代展馆，配有电梯、无障碍卫生间和休息座椅，是旺季中午避暑避人潮、独自慢慢看展的最佳去处。
Recommended museum landmark (中国闽台缘博物馆): 免费开放、入口有无障碍坡道与电梯，室内恒温且座椅充足，独行轮椅旅客可在此安稳消磨半天，躲开旺季户外人潮。
Recommended temple landmark (泉州天后宫): 免费入内、正殿前场地平坦开阔，紧邻中山路步行街，逛完顺路即达，无需额外交通开销，适合低预算独行且行动不便者。
Recommended ancient bridge landmark (洛阳桥): 免费开放的平直宋代石桥，桥面坡度极缓并有护栏，乘公交即可直达，轮椅独行者可在清晨人少时慢慢推行赏江景。
Recommended food street landmark (西街): 一条平坦直街集中了面线糊、润饼等便宜小吃，独行旅客花钱少、吃得快、随时可坐下歇脚，旺季避开午晚高峰即可顺畅通行。
Recommended historic quarter landmark (晋江五店市传统街区): 免费开放的红砖厝步行街区，地面平整无台阶、休息点密集，离主城人潮稍远，适合旺季独行轮椅旅客安静地逛上半天。

Recommended free waterfront promenade landmark (The Bund (Waitan)): the whole riverside promenade is one continuous level surface with curb cuts at every crossing and benches along the way, so a solo wheelchair user can roll the full skyline route at zero cost and duck into adjacent air-conditioned buildings when peak-season heat or crowds peak.

Recommended free museum landmark (Shanghai Museum (People's Square)): admission is free, every gallery level is reachable by lift, loaner wheelchairs and accessible toilets are on site, and the air-conditioned halls make it the best no-cost refuge from peak-season heat and afternoon thunderstorms, with no group booking needed for a solo visitor.

Recommended free contemporary art museum landmark (Power Station of Art): entry costs nothing, ramps and oversized freight lifts connect all floors of the converted power plant, and the wide galleries let a solo traveller in a chair spend a whole rainy or blistering afternoon indoors without spending a yuan.

Recommended free art museum landmark (China Art Museum): the former Expo pavilion has step-free entrances, lifts to every level, accessible restrooms and free admission, giving a budget solo visitor a large, cool, crowd-absorbing indoor route during the busiest weeks of the year.

Recommended free public library landmark (Shanghai Library East): the entrance is fully step-free with lifts, accessible toilets and generous seating, so a solo wheelchair user gets a free, quiet, air-conditioned base to rest, recharge devices and plan the next stop in peak-season heat.

Recommended free sculpture park landmark (Jing'an Sculpture Park): a compact, level paved loop with benches at short intervals and no admission charge, ideal for a solo visitor who wants open-air time without long distances or stairs, and it sits beside a metro lift and the Natural History Museum.

Recommended free riverside park landmark (West Bund Riverside (Xuhui Riverside Park)): the converted industrial waterfront is one flat, wide, ramp-served promenade with free access and plentiful shaded seating, giving a solo wheelchair user a long roll with room to avoid the peak-season crush of the central Bund.

Recommended free historic park landmark (Fuxing Park): entrances are level, the paths are paved and mostly flat, benches and accessible toilets are within the grounds, and it is free, so a solo budget traveller can take an unhurried early-morning break from the crowds in the French Concession.

Recommended low-cost indoor museum landmark (Shanghai Urban Planning Exhibition Center): a modest single ticket buys a lift-served, fully indoor route past the huge city model, which is exactly what a solo visitor on a low budget needs when peak-season heat or rain makes outdoor sightseeing impractical.

Recommended low-cost municipal park landmark (Century Park): a token entry fee buys kilometres of wide, level, step-free paths with accessible gates, toilets and lakeside benches, and it is reachable by lift from the metro, making it an easy half-day outing for a solo wheelchair user away from the packed central sights.

Recommended Park landmark (Ueno Park): This expansive, fully paved public park is free to enter, offers wide accessible pathways throughout, and is especially stunning during peak cherry blossom season making it ideal for solo budget travelers with mobility needs.

Recommended Cultural landmark (Senso-ji Temple): Tokyo's most iconic temple features smooth stone pathways, step-free access through the main gate approach, and is completely free to visit, perfect for a solo low-budget traveler during the busy tourist season.

Recommended Park landmark (Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden): With a very low entry fee, paved wheelchair-accessible paths throughout all garden sections, and serene beauty during peak seasons, this garden is an excellent affordable solo outing.

Recommended Viewpoint landmark (Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observatory): This free observation deck on the 45th floor is fully elevator-accessible with no stairs required, offering panoramic city views without any cost to budget-conscious solo visitors.

Recommended Park landmark (Odaiba Seaside Park): This free waterfront park is entirely flat and accessible via step-free transit on the Yurikamome line, offering stunning bay views and a relaxed atmosphere perfect for solo travelers on a low budget.

Recommended Shopping & Culture landmark (Akihabara Electric Town): The main streets and many ground-floor shops are accessible and free to explore, making it a vibrant solo experience during peak season without requiring significant spending.

Recommended Garden landmark (Hamarikyu Gardens): This historic garden charges a modest entry fee, provides well-maintained paved accessible paths throughout, and offers a peaceful contrast to busy peak-season crowds for solo wheelchair users.

Recommended Cultural landmark (Yanaka Ginza Shopping Street): This charming old-town shopping street is largely flat and step-free, free to stroll through, and offers an authentic local atmosphere that solo budget travelers can enjoy without crowds overwhelming smaller sites.

Recommended Art & Technology landmark (teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum): Designed with fully accessible, step-free immersive environments, this world-famous attraction offers a uniquely engaging solo experience that justifies its ticket cost during peak travel season.

Recommended Food & Market landmark (Tsukiji Outer Market): This iconic open-air market has wide, flat, and freely walkable lanes accessible to wheelchair users, where solo travelers can enjoy affordable fresh street food and local culture during peak season.

Recommended basilica landmark (Sagrada Família): the basic timed-entry ticket is the cheapest way inside, a first-slot morning booking dodges the peak-season crush and heat, and step-free entry plus internal lifts let a solo wheelchair user cover the whole nave independently.

Recommended art museum landmark (Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya): entry is free on Saturday afternoons and the first Sunday of the month, every level is reached by lift or ramp from the Montjuïc side, and the sheer size of the galleries keeps peak-season crowds spread thin.

Recommended public park landmark (Parc de la Ciutadella): it costs nothing, the paths are flat asphalt with plenty of benches and shade, and its wide entrances make it an easy solo wander that never requires a kerb or a step.

Recommended food market landmark (Mercat de la Boqueria): admission is free, the aisles are level and paved throughout, and arriving at the 8am opening lets a solo budget traveller see it before the peak-season tour groups make the corridors impassable.

raw_name: Rambla de Mar and Port Vell waterfront
surface_name: Rambla de Mar and Port Vell waterfront
reason: Recommended waterfront promenade landmark (Rambla de Mar and Port Vell): the wooden boardwalk is completely level and ramped from street to water, it is free to walk end to end, and evening is the quietest time to enjoy it alone in high season.

Recommended art museum landmark (Museu Picasso): free entry on Thursday evenings and the first Sunday makes it viable on a low budget, and lifts serve every floor of the five medieval palaces so no staircase is unavoidable.

raw_name: Museu d'Història de Barcelona (MUHBA), Plaça del Rei
surface_name: Museu d'Història de Barcelona (MUHBA), Plaça del Rei
reason: Recommended history museum landmark (Museu d'Història de Barcelona): free on Sunday afternoons, a lift carries you down to the Roman streets beneath the square, and the underground route is smooth and level once you are below ground, which also means cool air at the height of summer.

raw_name: Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona (CCCB)
surface_name: Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona (CCCB)
reason: Recommended cultural centre landmark (Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona): Sunday afternoon entry is free, the building is fully step-free with lifts to every exhibition floor, and its courtyard and café give a solo visitor an air-conditioned base during the hottest part of a peak-season day.

Recommended accessible beach landmark (Platja de la Nova Icària): it is free, the promenade and wooden beach walkways are step-free, and the summer accessibility service provides beach wheelchairs and adapted showers so a solo wheelchair user can actually reach the water.

raw_name: Telefèric de Montjuïc and Castell de Montjuïc
surface_name: Telefèric de Montjuïc and Castell de Montjuïc
reason: Recommended viewpoint and fortress landmark (Telefèric de Montjuïc and Castell de Montjuïc): the cable car takes wheelchairs, the castle has step-free access and a lift up to the terrace, and it delivers the city's best panorama without a single stair or a guided tour fee.

Recommended imperial palace landmark (Forbidden City): the whole central axis from Meridian Gate to the Imperial Garden is level stone paving with ramps at the side gates, wheelchairs are lent free at the ticket office, the 60 CNY peak-season ticket is the trip's one real splurge, and arriving at the 08:30 opening keeps a solo visitor ahead of the midday crush.

Recommended public square landmark (Tiananmen Square): entry is free with an online reservation, the entire square is flat and paved with wide gaps between barriers that a chair clears easily, and staffed security lanes at the underpasses make it simple to navigate alone.

Recommended imperial ritual park landmark (Temple of Heaven): the 34 CNY through-ticket covers the Hall of Prayer and Echo Wall, the Danbi Bridge axis and surrounding park paths are smooth level tarmac, and early mornings are given over to locals doing tai chi, so there is room to move at peak season.

Recommended imperial garden landmark (Summer Palace): the East Palace Gate to Long Corridor to Kunming Lake promenade is level and paved, so the 30 CNY peak ticket buys all the classic lake views with none of the hill climbs, and the lakeside breeze makes a hot peak-season afternoon bearable.

raw_name: 中国国家博物馆 (National Museum of China)
surface_name: 中国国家博物馆 (National Museum of China)
reason: Recommended national museum landmark (National Museum of China): admission is free with an ID reservation, lifts reach every gallery and accessible toilets are on each floor, and timed entry slots cap the crowd even in high season, which suits a solo visitor who wants to set their own pace in air-conditioned comfort.

Recommended art district landmark (798 Art District): there is no entry fee, the old factory streets are flat and wide, most galleries have level or ramped entrances, and it is an easy place to spend a cheap half-day wandering alone without needing to book anything.

Recommended modern Olympic landmark (Olympic Park): the promenade between the Bird's Nest and Water Cube is free, broad and completely level, benches and shade are plentiful, and going after 18:00 avoids both the peak-season heat and the tour-bus peak, which is ideal on a low budget.

Recommended imperial lake park landmark (Beihai Park): the 10 CNY ticket is a bargain, the south-shore loop around the lake is level with ramped boat docks, and the pavilions and snack stalls give a solo traveler cheap places to rest whenever needed.

raw_name: 前门大街 / 大栅栏 (Qianmen Street & Dashilan)
surface_name: 前门大街 / 大栅栏 (Qianmen Street & Dashilan)
reason: Recommended historic pedestrian street landmark (Qianmen Street & Dashilan): it is free to walk, the granite pedestrian paving has curb cuts throughout and the larger shops and restaurants are step-free, and starting around 09:00 beats the peak-season foot traffic; it is also well lit and busy enough to feel safe alone in the evening.

Recommended city museum landmark (Capital Museum): free with an online reservation, purpose-built with ramps, lifts, accessible washrooms and loaner wheelchairs, and fully indoor and air-conditioned, making it the obvious low-cost refuge when peak-season heat or a sudden storm rules out the parks.

raw_name: Wat Phra Singh (Wat Phra Singh Woramahawihan)
surface_name: Wat Phra Singh (Wat Phra Singh Woramahawihan)
reason: Recommended temple landmark (Wat Phra Singh (Wat Phra Singh Woramahawihan)): Its old-city compound is almost entirely level and paved, with ramps and a ground-level entry into the main viharn, so a solo wheelchair user can roll the whole circuit independently for a 50-baht ticket and skip the pricier guided tours.

Recommended park landmark (Nong Buak Haad Public Park): A free, flat, paved loop on the southwest corner of the moat with accessible toilets and shaded benches, making it the cheapest reliable rest-and-refuel stop between old-city sights during the busy cool-season weeks.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Chedi Luang): The central old-city grounds are level and step-free around the massive ruined chedi, entry is only 50 baht, and its location means one solo traveler can reach it on foot or by a single short songthaew hop without needing an accessible vehicle hire.

raw_name: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center and Lanna Folklife Museum
surface_name: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center and Lanna Folklife Museum
reason: Recommended museum landmark (Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center and Lanna Folklife Museum): Both sit in the same renovated colonial-era building behind the Three Kings Monument with a lift, ramps and accessible restrooms, giving a low-cost air-conditioned half-day of Lanna history when peak-season crowds fill the streets outside.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Suan Dok): A broad, flat, mostly paved courtyard with the royal chedi and white stupa cluster laid out at ground level, plus free evening monk-chat sessions that suit a solo traveler looking for inexpensive, low-effort company.

Recommended market landmark (Warorot Market (Kad Luang)): The main aisles and riverside food stalls are on one level with no stairs, so you can graze cheap northern Thai snacks and buy supplies early in the morning before the peak-season crowds make the narrow lanes hard to navigate.

Recommended museum landmark (MAIIAM Contemporary Art Museum): Purpose-built with a lift, wide doorways and level galleries throughout, it is the most genuinely wheelchair-independent attraction near Chiang Mai and offers a quiet, crowd-free contrast to old-city sightseeing for a 150-baht ticket.

raw_name: Three Kings Monument Plaza and Sunday Walking Street
surface_name: Three Kings Monument Plaza and Sunday Walking Street
reason: Recommended square landmark (Three Kings Monument Plaza and Sunday Walking Street): The plaza is flat and open and the Sunday pedestrian market runs along level Ratchadamnoen Road, letting a solo wheelchair user join the biggest free evening event of the week without needing to pre-book transport or help.

Recommended garden landmark (Royal Park Rajapruek): Its wide, flat, fully paved avenue of international gardens is designed for wheeled access with borrowed wheelchairs on site, though the 200-baht foreigner ticket and out-of-town songthaew ride make it the pricier splurge on this list.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Chet Yot (Wat Jed Yot)): A quiet, flat, lawn-set temple complex about two kilometres north of the old city with level paths to the distinctive seven-spired chedi, free entry and almost no tour traffic, which makes it an easy low-budget morning outing for a solo visitor.

raw_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
surface_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
reason: Recommended 野生动物保护基地 landmark (成都大熊猫繁育研究基地): 主环路平整，有轮椅坡道和园内观光车，独自出行无需他人协助；旺季清晨开园就入园，赶在团队到达前看完，一张门票就能撑起半天的行程，也是全程性价比最高的一笔花费。
Recommended 城市博物馆 landmark (成都博物馆): 免费预约，电梯直达各层，馆内可借轮椅；旺季午后馆内阴凉，正好避开高温和人流，一个人慢慢看也不赶时间。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (人民公园): 全园平坦，全是硬化步道，免费进出；鹤鸣茶社一杯茶十几元就能坐上一下午，最适合独自出行、预算有限又想体验本地生活节奏的人。
Recommended 历史园林 landmark (杜甫草堂): 园内步道平整、坡道衔接良好，轮椅通行顺畅；清晨或闭园前两小时进去，能避开旺季团队，一个人逛园林、看碑刻都很从容。
Recommended 省级博物馆 landmark (四川博物院): 免费开放，入口有无障碍坡道、馆内有电梯；馆藏集中，不必走很多路，旺季把它当作半天的室内备选最稳妥。
Recommended 考古遗址博物馆 landmark (金沙遗址博物馆): 遗迹馆和陈列馆都由电梯和无障碍通道串联，室外路线也平坦；一个人可以按自己的节奏走，室内外结合，下雨或大太阳都不怕。
Recommended 佛教寺院 landmark (文殊院): 院落平坦、门槛低，主要殿宇之间没有台阶；免门票，寺内素斋和茶园价格低，旺季人流也相对分散，适合独自安静待半天。
Recommended 文创园区 landmark (东郊记忆): 原厂区改造而成，地面整体平整无坡坎，免费进入；独自逛展、拍照、进小馆子都方便，预算可控且不需要预约抢票。
Recommended 古典园林 landmark (望江楼公园): 沿锦江的竹林步道全程平坦，门票仅二十元；比热门园林清静得多，旺季一个人也能找到长椅歇脚、慢慢走完。
Recommended 商业街区 landmark (太古里·春熙路): 步行区无高差、坡道完善，地铁站有电梯直达；不花钱也能逛，餐饮便利店密集，独自出行补给和休息都方便，旺季清晨或晚间人少时最舒适。

surface_name: 大理古城 Dali Old Town (Wuhua Tower, Renmin Road, Foreigner Street)

raw_name: 大理白族自治州博物馆 Dali Prefectural Museum
surface_name: 大理白族自治州博物馆 Dali Prefectural Museum

surface_name: 喜洲古镇 Xizhou Ancient Town

surface_name: 崇圣寺三塔 Three Pagodas & Chongsheng Temple
reason: Recommended religious landmark (Three Pagodas): the ticketed compound is the one unmissable icon and its main courtyards are level with an electric shuttle cart covering the long distances, though budget travellers should note the ticket is the trip's biggest single cost and go at 8am to beat peak-season queues.

Recommended craft landmark (Zhoucheng Village): village lanes around the main dye yards are flat and paved, and a short hands-on tie-dye session is one of the cheapest souvenirs-and-company activities for a solo traveller, with staff happy to bring the work to a seated visitor.

raw_name: 洱海月湿地公园 Erhai Moon Wetland Park (Xiaguan)
surface_name: 洱海月湿地公园 Erhai Moon Wetland Park (Xiaguan)
reason: Recommended park landmark (Erhai Moon Wetland Park): free entry, boardwalks and paved loops with no steps, quiet even in peak season, and a short flat walk from Xiaguan's cheap guesthouses and bus station.

raw_name: 大理床单厂艺术区 Dali Bed Sheet Factory Art District
surface_name: 大理床单厂艺术区 Dali Bed Sheet Factory Art District
reason: Recommended arts landmark (Bed Sheet Factory Art District): a free, single-level converted factory with smooth concrete floors and open courtyards, good for a solo low-budget afternoon of small galleries and cheap coffee without stairs or ticket queues.

Recommended Historic waterfront landmark (Cais da Ribeira): A completely flat, cobbled-but-paved riverside promenade with free access, benches every few metres and no steps, so a solo wheelchair user can spend a whole peak-season evening people-watching, eating cheaply and catching the Douro light without any planning.

Recommended Historic railway station landmark (São Bento Railway Station): Entry is step-free from the street through wide doors onto one level, admission is free, and the famous azulejo panels can be admired from a seated position in ten minutes — an ideal low-cost stop that slots into any step-free route through the centre.

Recommended Municipal market landmark (Mercado do Bolhão): The renovated building has lifts and ramps to both levels, free entry, and dozens of cheap counter seats where a solo traveller can eat a fresh, budget-friendly lunch without booking — useful in peak season when restaurants are full.

Recommended Public garden landmark (Jardins do Palácio de Cristal): The main paths are wide, gently graded and step-free with free entry and shaded benches, giving a solo visitor a quiet, cool retreat with Douro views exactly when summer crowds and heat peak.

Recommended Art museum landmark (Museu Nacional Soares dos Reis): A lift serves every floor, the courtyard and entrance are level, and free Sunday/admission-free slots plus a small collection make it a low-cost, air-conditioned step-free option for the hottest part of a peak-season day.

Recommended Contemporary art museum landmark (Serralves Museum and Park): The museum and the park's main trails are designed with ramps, lifts and accessible toilets throughout, and a single ticket covers both, so a solo wheelchair user gets a full half-day of art and gardens for one modest fee.

Recommended Concert hall landmark (Casa da Música): The whole building is served by lifts with level access to every hall and free entry to the foyer and terrace, and its cheap standing or reduced-price tickets make an evening concert realistic on a low budget for a solo traveller.

Recommended Coastal promenade landmark (Foz do Douro promenade): A long, flat, fully paved seafront walk with accessible tram/bus stops nearby and no entry cost, offering a breezy escape from the crowded historic centre during the peak season.

surface_name: Cais de Gaia and port wine lodge
reason: Recommended Riverside wine district landmark (Cais de Gaia and port wine lodge): The Gaia riverfront is level and the major lodges such as Sandeman run lift-accessible guided tours with tastings, so a solo visitor can do Porto's signature experience independently, step-free, at an entry-level price.

Recommended Scenic viewpoint landmark (Jardim do Morro): The metro station is fully step-free with lifts straight to the park, entry is free, and the terraced lawn gives a wheelchair user one of the best sunset views over Porto without climbing a single stair.

Recommended art museum landmark (Musée du Louvre): Entry is free for visitors with disabilities and one accompanying person, the Pyramid entrance and every wing are served by lifts, and booking the first morning slot lets a solo traveller see the star works before peak-season crowds and heat build up.

Recommended impressionist museum landmark (Musée d'Orsay): The whole collection sits behind a step-free entrance with lifts to every level, admission is free for disabled visitors plus a companion, and the vast converted station hall gives a solo visitor plenty of uncrowded, shaded bench space to rest between galleries.

Recommended small collection museum landmark (Musée de l'Orangerie): It is compact, fully lift-accessible and free for disabled visitors, so an hour in the two oval Water Lilies rooms with their soft daylight and seats makes an ideal low-effort, low-cost stop on a hot peak-season afternoon.

Recommended fine arts museum landmark (Petit Palais): The permanent collection costs nothing, the building is step-free with lifts throughout, and its quiet garden courtyard café is an affordable, wheelchair-friendly retreat a few steps from the Champs-Élysées crowds.

Recommended city history museum landmark (Musée Carnavalet): Free permanent entry, full lift access across its floors, and reliable air conditioning make this Marais museum a budget-friendly way for a solo traveller to shelter from peak-season heat while still sightseeing.

Recommended sculpture museum and garden landmark (Musée Rodin): Disabled visitors enter free and the gravel-and-lawn sculpture garden is largely flat and step-free, so a solo visitor can picnic among The Thinker in the shade without paying for a full indoor visit.

Recommended public garden landmark (Jardin du Luxembourg): Entry is free, the main allées and the area around the pond are paved and level for a wheelchair, and the early-morning or late-afternoon hours give a low-budget solo traveller shade, benches and drinking fountains away from the midday crush.

Recommended riverside promenade landmark (Parc Rives de Seine): The car-free lower quays are flat, smoothly paved and free to use, and with lifts and ramps at ponts along the route they make a cool, shaded picnic route for a solo wheelchair user at peak season.

surface_name: Tour Eiffel and Champ de Mars
reason: Recommended iconic landmark landmark (Tour Eiffel and Champ de Mars): The tower's lifts take wheelchair users to the second floor while the Champ de Mars itself is free, flat and grassy, so a solo budget traveller can enjoy the view and a picnic without paying for a summit ticket or managing stairs.

surface_name: Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie and Parc de la Villette
reason: Recommended science museum landmark (Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie and Parc de la Villette): One of Paris's most thoroughly accessible venues, with step-free entrances, lifts and adapted facilities throughout plus a free, flat surrounding park, it gives a solo low-budget traveller a full air-conditioned day out at peak season.

Recommended 历史商业街 landmark (中山路骑楼老街): 整条街有骑楼顶棚遮阳挡雨，地面平整无台阶，轮椅推行顺畅，沿线老字号、便利店与公交站点密集，独行者补给和临时撤返都方便。

surface_name: 中华艺术宫 China Art Museum

surface_name: 人民公园与人民广场 People's Park & People's Square

surface_name: 上海自然博物馆 Shanghai Natural History Museum

surface_name: 静安雕塑公园 Jing'an Sculpture Park

raw_name: National Museum of Nature and Science
surface_name: National Museum of Nature and Science
reason: Recommended Science Museum landmark (National Museum of Nature and Science): lifts connect every floor, interactive exhibits sit at wheelchair height, and the modest ticket keeps a solo, budget-conscious day fully indoors and fully step-free.

raw_name: Miraikan — National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation
surface_name: Miraikan — National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation
reason: Recommended Innovation Museum landmark (Miraikan): step-free lifts, wide galleries and seating throughout make this Odaiba museum easy to self-navigate alone, and its low admission suits a budget indoor day when peak-season weather turns.

Recommended Imperial Garden landmark (Imperial Palace East Gardens): the free, fully paved circuit over the palace grounds is gentle on wheels, and entering at opening time gives a solo traveler space and shade before peak-season tour groups arrive.

Recommended Food Market landmark (Tsukiji Outer Market): the lanes are flat and stone-paved enough for a wheelchair to move through, and grazing on cheap sushi and tamagoyaki lets a solo traveler eat well for under ¥1,500 — best done right at opening before the crowds thicken.

Recommended architectural landmark (Sagrada Família): the whole visit is step-free, with a lift to the tower and a separate accessible entrance, so a solo wheelchair user can book a timed early-morning slot online and move through the nave before peak-season crowds build.

raw_name: La Rambla and Mercat de la Boqueria
surface_name: La Rambla and Mercat de la Boqueria
reason: Recommended market landmark (La Rambla and Mercat de la Boqueria): a flat, continuous, curb-free promenade with level entry into the market hall makes this the cheapest and easiest full morning out for a solo traveler on a low budget.

Recommended park landmark (Parc de la Ciutadella): free entry, wide paved loop paths and accessible toilets make it an ideal no-cost, step-free base for a picnic lunch away from the summer crowds on the beach.

Recommended museum landmark (Museu Picasso): every floor is reached by lift, entry is free on Thursday afternoons and the first Sunday of the month, and booking that free timed slot keeps both the budget low and the crowds manageable in peak season.

raw_name: El Born Centre de Cultura i Memòria
surface_name: El Born Centre de Cultura i Memòria
reason: Recommended historic landmark (El Born Centre de Cultura i Memòria): free admission, level thresholds and lifts onto the raised walkways let a wheelchair user look down over the excavated 1700s street grid without dealing with the cobbled lanes outside.

Recommended museum landmark (Museu Marítim de Barcelona): the converted royal shipyards are entirely flat with ramps and a lift to the rooftop viewpoint, and admission is free on Sunday afternoons, which suits a solo traveler watching costs.

Recommended 古城街区 landmark (大理古城): 进城免门票，城内青石板路平坦好走，客栈和小吃价格梯度大，情侣可以白天逛街、晚上泡人民路夜市，预算压力最小。

surface_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）

Recommended 白族古镇 landmark (喜洲古镇): 免门票，从古城坐公交几元即到，喜洲粑粑和凉鸡米线便宜管饱，稻田和转角楼是情侣拍照的零成本背景。

surface_name: 崇圣寺三塔（倒影公园视角）

Recommended 湿地公园 landmark (海舌公园): 门票免费或极低，步行强度低、路线短，清晨人少风小，适合两人慢慢走到洱海边发呆看苍山倒影。

surface_name: 苍山玉带云游路（感通索道上下）

raw_name: 大理市博物馆（杜文秀元帅府）
surface_name: 大理市博物馆（杜文秀元帅府）
reason: Recommended 历史博物馆 landmark (大理市博物馆（杜文秀元帅府）): 免费开放，正午旺季太阳最毒、古城最挤时躲进来吹风看展，等于零成本的中场休息。
Recommended 湖畔古镇 landmark (双廊古镇): 入镇不收费，坐班车前往成本很低，傍晚在洱海边看落日是免费的高光时刻，选工作日或清早去能躲开旺季人潮。
Recommended 古城 landmark (巍山古城): 班车票便宜、古城本身免费，游客密度远低于大理古城，同样预算能住得更舒服、吃到更地道的粑肉饵丝。
Recommended 茶马古道古镇 landmark (沙溪古镇): 班车往返几十元、古镇自由进出，住一晚便宜的客栈就能换来几乎没有旺季人流的寺登街清晨，性价比最高的一日或两日行程。

Recommended historic landmark (Ribeira District): The riverside lanes cost nothing to wander and give a low-budget couple the classic Porto evening — golden light on the Douro, buskers on the quay, and plenty of cheap tascas — though in peak season you should come at breakfast or after 20:00 to dodge the cruise crowds.

Recommended architectural landmark (Dom Luís I Bridge): Walking the upper deck is completely free and delivers the city's best two-person photo op and sunset panorama, with the lower deck letting you cross into Gaia for a cheap port-lodge browse without paying for a single tasting.

Recommended garden landmark (Jardins do Palácio de Cristal): These free terraced gardens are the ideal low-cost couple's picnic spot, with shady lawns, roaming peacocks and Douro views that stay pleasant even in the peak-season heat.

Recommended architectural landmark (São Bento Railway Station): Entry is free and the 20,000 azulejo tiles in the main hall make a five-minute stop that punches far above its price, fitting neatly into a walking day when you need an air-conditioned breather between sights.

Recommended literary landmark (Livraria Lello): The ornate staircase is a must for a couple, and the modest entrance fee is redeemable against a book purchase, so you leave with a souvenir rather than a sunk cost — but in peak season book a timed slot online and arrive at opening to avoid the queue.

Recommended religious landmark (Porto Cathedral): The church itself is free to enter and its terrace gives a broad rooftop view over the old town, while the small optional cloister-and-tower fee is one of the cheapest paid upgrades in the city for two people.

Recommended viewpoint landmark (Miradouro da Vitória): A free, unsignposted terrace a few minutes uphill from Ribeira, it is where locals go at dusk and gives couples the same Douro panorama as the paid attractions with none of the queue.

Recommended market landmark (Mercado do Bolhão): Browsing is free and the restored two-floor market is the smartest low-budget move in town — assemble bread, cheese, fruit and a bottle of vinho verde for a fraction of a restaurant lunch, ideally before 11:00 in peak season.

Recommended religious landmark (Igreja de São Francisco): For a few euros each you get the city's most jaw-dropping interior — walls of baroque gilded carving — which is a far better value hour than most paid museums and stays cool during the hottest peak-season afternoons.

Recommended coastal landmark (Foz do Douro): A cheap bus or tram ride buys you an afternoon of Atlantic beach, promenade walks and sunset drinks at the river mouth, giving a low-budget couple a full change of scene without leaving the city.
Recommended garden landmark (Jardin du Luxembourg): free to enter and made for two, with a morning stroll before peak-season tour groups fill the chairs around the basin.

Recommended museum landmark (Petit Palais): its permanent collection costs nothing, so a couple on a tight budget gets a real art museum plus a shaded garden café without touching the Louvre's queue or ticket price.

Recommended elevated park landmark (Promenade Plantée (Coulée verte René-Dumont)): a free 4.7 km garden walkway above the streets, walkable end to end with no mobility limits and far quieter than ground-level sights in July and August.

Recommended waterway landmark (Canal Saint-Martin): the canal banks are free and ideal for an evening picnic and wine bought from a nearby shop, with lock-watching and iron footbridges that suit a couple's slow pace.
Recommended basilica landmark (Sacré-Cœur and Montmartre): entry to the basilica is free, and climbing the hill at sunrise on a weekday gives couples the view before the summer crowds arrive.

Recommended historic cemetery landmark (Père Lachaise Cemetery): free, deeply shaded, and blessedly uncrowded even in peak season, with cobbled lanes that reward couples who don't mind walking for an hour or two.
Recommended Roman ruin landmark (Arènes de Lutèce): a free Gallo-Roman arena hidden in the Latin Quarter where couples can sit on the ancient terraces mid-afternoon for nothing at all.

Recommended market landmark (Marché d'Aligre): a covered food market where a low-budget couple assembles a full lunch of cheese, fruit and bread for a few euros, best on a weekday morning before the Saturday crush.

surface_name: Square du Vert-Galant and the Seine quays

Recommended 宗教古迹 landmark (开元寺): 免费开放、东西塔与古榕构成最上镜的画面，适合情侣在清晨人少时慢逛拍照，完全不增加预算。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (西街): 一条街解决吃与逛，面线糊、润饼等小吃单价低，两人花小钱就能吃饱，旺季避开正午进街即可绕开人潮。
Recommended 历史建筑 landmark (泉州府文庙): 免门票的大成殿与广场适合坐下歇脚，旺季傍晚常有南音或演出可免费围观，是零成本的约会停留点。
Recommended 宗教古迹 landmark (清净寺): 门票仅数元，花岗岩穹顶与阿拉伯碑刻在城内独一份，情侣十几分钟就能看完却极出片，性价比在旺季尤其突出。
Recommended 民俗信仰 landmark (通淮关岳庙): 免费入内、香火极旺，两人可一起抽签祈福讨彩头，位于老城中心，步行串联其他景点不额外花交通钱。
Recommended 民俗信仰 landmark (泉州天后宫): 免票且殿宇精美，门前德济门遗址可顺路同看，全程室内外皆有遮蔽，旺季午后避晒又不必消费。
Recommended 古桥景观 landmark (洛阳桥): 免费开放的宋代跨海石桥，日落时分光线柔和最适合两人散步合影，避开上午团队客就能独享桥面。
Recommended 民俗村落 landmark (蟳埔村): 进村免费，蚵壳厝巷弄随便逛，簪花围可两人只租一套轮流拍，是低预算也能拿到的独家照片与体验。

surface_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
reason: Recommended 博物馆 landmark (泉州海外交通史博物馆): 免费预约入场，空调展厅正适合旺季正午避暑，一边看海丝文物一边歇脚，零花费补足行程的知识背景。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (中山路骑楼街): 夜间免费漫步的骑楼长廊，灯光下的南洋立面适合两人慢走收尾，骑楼下有遮挡，旺季下雨或闷热都不影响。
Recommended 滨江地标 landmark (外滩): 全天免费，你们两人可以在黄昏时从外白渡桥慢慢走到延安东路，一路看着对岸的灯光亮起来，花不到钱就能看到上海最经典的夜景；旺季人多，可以挑清晨或晚上十点后错峰去。

surface_name: 豫园与城隍庙 Yu Garden
reason: Recommended 古典园林 landmark (豫园): 门票只要几十元，两人一起逛明代假山、九曲桥和老街小吃，性价比很高；旺季排队很长，建议开园就进门，或者傍晚再去。

surface_name: 武康路—安福路街区 Wukang Road
reason: Recommended 历史街区 landmark (武康路): 完全不收门票，梧桐树荫下沿路看老洋房、买杯便宜的咖啡就能消磨半天，很适合预算有限的情侣慢慢散步；旺季中午很晒，建议上午或日落前去。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (上海博物馆): 常设展免费预约，青铜和陶瓷馆够你们看一整个下午，旺季午后暑热或下雨时，这里是最舒服、最省钱的室内去处。
Recommended 石库门弄堂 landmark (田子坊): 逛弄堂不用花钱，小店和街头小吃单价低，适合两个人边走边分着吃；旺季巷子很挤，建议工作日上午去。

reason: Recommended 当代艺术馆 landmark (上海当代艺术博物馆): 主展览免费，大烟囱和老厂房很好拍照，还能顺路去黄浦江边吹风，情侣在旺季把它当避暑半日行程刚刚好。
Recommended 佛教寺庙 landmark (静安寺): 门票便宜，地铁直达，金色殿宇和商圈高楼形成很好的对比，一小时就能逛完，适合塞进预算紧张的旺季行程里。
Recommended 水乡古镇 landmark (朱家角): 坐地铁17号线即可直达，古镇本身免费，两个人合租一条摇橹船，人均开销也低，是旺季里换换节奏的慢半日游。
Recommended 工业遗产 landmark (1933老场坊): 免费开放，伞形廊桥和清水混凝土很适合两个人互相拍照，室内有遮蔽，旺季正午躲太阳、躲雨都合适。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (复兴公园): 免费，法式梧桐和玫瑰园安静好坐，可以在逛完新天地后进来歇脚，预算几乎为零，还能看到本地人跳舞下棋的生活场面。

Recommended historic temple landmark (Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise-dori, Asakusa): Entry is free and the lantern-lit lanes are at their most romantic in the early morning, letting a low-budget couple enjoy Tokyo's oldest temple before peak-season crowds arrive and cheap street snacks replace a sit-down meal.

Recommended shrine and park landmark (Meiji Jingu and Yoyogi Park): Both are free, the forested shrine approach is a cool, quiet escape from peak-season heat and crowds, and Yoyogi's lawns make a zero-cost picnic spot for two.

Recommended landscape garden landmark (Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden): A ticket costs only a few hundred yen, the lawns and cherry trees are the classic peak-season couple's setting, and booking the timed entry slot online ahead keeps costs low while avoiding the longest queues.

Recommended observation deck landmark (Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observatory): Free 360-degree views over the city are ideal for a low-budget couple, and going at sunset on a clear peak-season evening gives a Mt. Fuji silhouette for the price of nothing.

Recommended park and market street landmark (Ueno Park and Ameyoko Market): Park entry is free, the cluster of national museums lets you pick one cheap exhibit, and Ameyoko's stalls feed two people well for very little even in the busiest travel weeks.

Recommended old-town district landmark (Yanaka Ginza and Nezu Shrine): This low-rise shitamachi area is free to wander, its croquettes and cheap eateries suit a tight budget, and it stays noticeably calmer than headline sights during peak season.

Recommended historic garden landmark (Imperial Palace East Gardens): Admission is free, the former castle grounds give couples a spacious, green walk, and the limited daily entry means arriving at opening is the reliable peak-season strategy.

raw_name: Odaiba Seaside Park and Rainbow Bridge Promenade
surface_name: Odaiba Seaside Park and Rainbow Bridge Promenade
reason: Recommended waterfront landmark (Odaiba Seaside Park and Rainbow Bridge Promenade): The bay walk, beach and bridge views cost nothing, evening is the most romantic hour for a couple, and the open waterfront absorbs peak-season crowds far better than enclosed attractions.

Recommended park and boating pond landmark (Inokashira Park, Kichijoji): Entry is free and a rowboat for two is a small, memorable splurge, while the surrounding Kichijoji arcades offer cheap lunches away from central Tokyo's peak-season price inflation.

Recommended shopping street landmark (Takeshita-dori and Omotesando, Harajuku): Window-shopping and people-watching cost nothing, the walk from kawaii Takeshita-dori to tree-lined Omotesando is a free couple's route, and starting before mid-morning beats the worst peak-season congestion.

surface_name: Basílica de la Sagrada Família (exterior and Plaça de Gaudí)
reason: Recommended architecture landmark (Basílica de la Sagrada Família (exterior and Plaça de Gaudí)): you can circle the façade and the pond-side plaza for free and photograph it together at golden hour, then dodge the peak-season ticket price and crowds entirely.

raw_name: Park Güell (free zone and Carmel hillside)
surface_name: Park Güell (free zone and Carmel hillside)
reason: Recommended park landmark (Park Güell (free zone and Carmel hillside)): the paid monumental core is skippable on a low budget since the free hillside paths and terraces give couples the same mosaic-and-city views, best entered on foot before 9am to beat peak-season queues.

raw_name: Bunkers del Carmel (Turó de la Rovira)
surface_name: Bunkers del Carmel (Turó de la Rovira)
reason: Recommended viewpoint landmark (Bunkers del Carmel (Turó de la Rovira)): a free 360-degree sunset perch that fits a couple's budget perfectly, and with no mobility limits you can walk up from Guinardó and carry a supermarket picnic instead of paying for a rooftop bar.

Recommended market landmark (Mercat de la Boqueria): entry is free and couples can graze cheaply on jamón, fruit cups and a shared plate at a counter, though in peak season arrive right at 8am opening to browse before the tour groups pack the aisles.

Recommended historic quarter landmark (Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic)): a self-guided wander through Roman walls, hidden plazas and the cathedral's cloister costs nothing and rewards unrestricted walkers with endless shaded alleys to escape the midday peak-season heat.

raw_name: Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar and El Born
surface_name: Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar and El Born
reason: Recommended church landmark (Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar and El Born): entry is free outside restricted hours and its cool, austere nave plus the surrounding El Born lanes make a romantic, zero-cost evening loop for a couple on a tight budget.

Recommended park landmark (Parc de la Ciutadella): free to enter with the Gaudí-designed fountain and a small rowing-boat lake that costs only a few euros, giving couples a cheap shaded siesta spot in the worst of the summer afternoon.

Recommended beach landmark (Barceloneta and Bogatell beaches): free sand and sea let a low-budget couple swim and sunbathe all day, and walking a little north to Bogatell buys calmer water and fewer crowds at peak season for no extra cost.

raw_name: Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya (MNAC) and Montjuïc gardens
surface_name: Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya (MNAC) and Montjuïc gardens
reason: Recommended museum landmark (Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya (MNAC) and Montjuïc gardens): entry is free on Saturday afternoons and the first Sunday of the month, and the surrounding Montjuïc terraces and stairs give couples panoramic picnic spots without a single ticket.

raw_name: Passeig de Gràcia and the Block of Discord
surface_name: Passeig de Gràcia and the Block of Discord
reason: Recommended architecture walk landmark (Passeig de Gràcia and the Block of Discord): Casa Batlló and La Pedrera are best admired from the pavement for free, so a couple can stroll the modernist boulevard after dark when the façades are lit and peak-season daytime heat has gone.
Recommended 历史宫殿 landmark (故宫博物院): 旺季门票仅60元、两人一天的核心行程性价比极高，无行动限制可以全程步行从中轴线逛到神武门，提前7天线上预约就能避开现场排队的长队。
Recommended 皇家园林 landmark (景山公园): 门票只要2元，是情侣拍故宫全景和日落的最省钱机位，登顶万春亭台阶不多、腿脚无碍者十几分钟就能上去，适合安排在故宫出宫后的黄昏时段。
Recommended 城市地标 landmark (天安门广场): 完全免费、两人零门票压力，清晨看升旗或傍晚散步都不花钱，广场平坦开阔、行动自如，只需按旺季规定提前预约并带好身份证件。
Recommended 皇家祭祀建筑 landmark (天坛公园): 旺季联票34元即可看完祈年殿与回音壁，园内古柏成荫、夏天旺季也凉快，两人沿丹陛桥慢走很适合清晨人少时拍照。
Recommended 皇家园林 landmark (颐和园): 旺季门票30元、昆明湖与长廊一条线路可以走上一整天，属于低预算里最“值回票价”的大园子，腿脚无限制可以环湖走完不必坐船加钱。
Recommended 长城 landmark (慕田峪长城): 门票45元、比八达岭人少且保存更完整，两人坐公交或S2线往返是最便宜的长城方案，体力无碍者可徒步西段避开缆车花费。
Recommended 胡同街区 landmark (什刹海与南锣鼓巷): 逛街本身免费，两人分吃一份小吃就能解决一顿，旺季傍晚沿后海走一圈吹风看灯，比进任何收费景点都划算。
Recommended 皇家园林 landmark (北海公园): 旺季门票10元，白塔与荷花池是情侣合影的经典背景，园子不大、步行强度低，可以半天轻松逛完再顺路接什刹海。
Recommended 艺术街区 landmark (798艺术区): 大部分画廊和展览免费开放，是旺季高温或下雨天的最佳室内替代方案，两人边逛边拍砖厂房和涂鸦，零门票也能待上半天。
Recommended 历史商业街 landmark (前门大街与大栅栏): 免费开放、就在天安门南侧步行可达，旺季把住宿和晚餐安排在这一带能省下交通费，两人尝几家老字号小吃即可低成本收尾一天的行程。

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Phra That Doi Suthep): A shared songthaew up the mountain costs a few baht each, and in peak season the cool, clear dry-season air gives couples the classic golden-chedi panorama without any need for a pricier guided tour.

Recommended national park landmark (Doi Inthanon National Park): Thailand's highest peak is a cheap full-day escape where the cool-season mornings bring cloud seas and blooming flowers along the Ang Ka trail, ideal for a couple splitting transport costs.

Recommended market landmark (Sunday Walking Street): Browsing is free and street snacks are pocket-change cheap, making it the best value evening out for two people in the dry, comfortable peak-season weather.

raw_name: Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phan Tao
surface_name: Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phan Tao
reason: Recommended temple landmark (Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phan Tao): The two adjacent Old City temples charge only a token entry fee and are an easy walk apart, so a couple can cover them in one cool-season afternoon for almost nothing.

Recommended waterfall landmark (Bua Tong Sticky Waterfalls): Entry is free and the limestone tiers are climbable in trainers, and the dry peak season keeps the water low and the trail safe for a couple on a tight budget.
Recommended market landmark (Warorot Market): It is the cheapest place in town for northern Thai food and picnic supplies, which suits a couple who would rather spend on experiences than restaurants.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Umong): A forest temple with walkable tunnels and a small pond, it asks only a donation-sized fee and offers a quiet, shaded half-day for two when the peak-season sun is strongest.

Recommended viewpoint landmark (Mon Jam): Peak season is exactly when the terraced flower fields and valley mist are at their best, and a songthaew or rented scooter keeps the trip within a low budget for a couple.

raw_name: Lanna Folklife Museum and Three Kings Monument square
surface_name: Lanna Folklife Museum and Three Kings Monument square
reason: Recommended museum landmark (Lanna Folklife Museum): A low entry fee buys a cool, air-conditioned hour of northern Thai culture right beside a free public square, a good cheap rainy-or-hot afternoon option for two.

Recommended recreation landmark (Chiang Mai Grand Canyon): Entry is minimal and the cliff-jump pools and walking paths make a fun shared half-day, with the cool peak season keeping the site pleasant rather than scorching.

raw_name: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding
