Recommended 城市公园 landmark (复兴公园): 免门票、主园路为平整沥青并有缓坡入口，轮椅通行轻松，周边法租界梧桐街道也平坦好走，可串成一条零花费的半日路线。

raw_name: 西岸滨江步道 West Bund Riverside Promenade
surface_name: 西岸滨江步道 West Bund Riverside Promenade
reason: Recommended 滨水步道 landmark (西岸滨江步道): 全新铺装的江岸步道全程无台阶并有坡道衔接、免费开放，旺季人流远少于外滩，适合情侣推着轮椅看江景与美术馆外立面。

raw_name: 上海图书馆东馆 Shanghai Library East
surface_name: 上海图书馆东馆 Shanghai Library East
raw_category: 公共文化空间 public cultural venue
reason: Recommended 公共文化空间 landmark (上海图书馆东馆): 免费入馆、全楼无障碍电梯与轮椅通道按最新标准配置，空调充足、座位多，是旺季午后躲避高温与人潮的低成本休息站。

Recommended Shinto shrine landmark (Meiji Jingu): the wide gravel-and-paved approach from Harajuku or Sangubashi stations is level and step-free throughout, entry is free, and the forested grounds stay a few degrees cooler than the surrounding city — an easy, cheap couple's stroll even at the height of peak season.

Recommended landscape garden landmark (Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden): for roughly 500 yen you get broad paved loop paths with gentle gradients and accessible toilets at every gate, plus three wheelchair-accessible entrances — a low-cost half-day of lawns and glasshouse that absorbs crowds well in high season.

raw_name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observation Deck
surface_name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observation Deck
reason: Recommended free observation deck landmark (Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observation Deck): elevators run directly to the 45th-floor decks with no stairs or ticket queue, so a couple on a tight budget gets skyline and, on clear days, Fuji views at zero cost — go at opening time to dodge peak-season lines.

Recommended museum landmark (Tokyo National Museum, Ueno Park): step-free from the Ueno Station park exit with ramps, lifts and loaner wheelchairs inside, and admission under 1,000 yen buys hours of air-conditioned relief from peak-season heat and crowds.

Recommended Buddhist temple landmark (Senso-ji and Nakamise approach): the temple precinct is free and flat with ramps to the main hall and an accessible toilet on site, though the shopping street is packed at peak times, so arrive before 8am for a calm, unobstructed roll-through with your partner.

raw_name: Odaiba Marine Park and Rainbow Bridge promenade
surface_name: Odaiba Marine Park and Rainbow Bridge promenade
reason: Recommended waterfront park landmark (Odaiba Marine Park and Rainbow Bridge promenade): the whole bayfront boardwalk is level, paved and free, with lifts connecting the Yurikamome line, making it one of Tokyo's best sunset spots for a couple without spending anything.

raw_name: Miraikan – National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation
surface_name: Miraikan – National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation
reason: Recommended science museum landmark (Miraikan – National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation): fully barrier-free with lifts to every floor and wheelchair loan at the desk, and at around 630 yen it is a genuinely cheap, crowd-managed indoor option for a couple during peak-season afternoons.

Recommended Edo-period garden landmark (Hama-rikyu Gardens): entry is about 300 yen and the main circuit is broad, level gravel with an accessible gate and toilets, giving a quiet tidal-pond walk framed by skyscrapers that feels far from the peak-season crush.

raw_name: Imperial Palace East Gardens and Kokyo Gaien
surface_name: Imperial Palace East Gardens and Kokyo Gaien
reason: Recommended palace garden landmark (Imperial Palace East Gardens and Kokyo Gaien): admission is free, wheelchairs are lent at the gates, and the Kokyo Gaien outer plaza is smooth asphalt — a flat, unhurried circuit that suits a couple pacing themselves in hot peak-season weather.

raw_name: Tokyo Station Marunouchi Building and Gyoko-dori
surface_name: Tokyo Station Marunouchi Building and Gyoko-dori
reason: Recommended historic architecture landmark (Tokyo Station Marunouchi Building and Gyoko-dori): the restored brick facade, the broad brick-paved plaza and the straight, level Gyoko-dori axis toward the palace are entirely step-free and free to view, and station lifts make it a natural low-budget anchor between other stops.

Recommended architecture landmark (Basílica de la Sagrada Família): Gaudí's unfinished basilica is the one Barcelona sight worth splurging on even on a tight budget, and off-peak winter slots are cheaper and far less crowded than the summer queues you would face as a couple.

Recommended park landmark (Park Güell): the free wooded upper sections and the mosaic terraces give you a romantic half-day of walking and city views for a few euros, and in low season you can often enter the ticketed zone without booking weeks ahead.

Recommended historic quarter landmark (Barri Gòtic): a completely free maze of medieval lanes, hidden squares and cathedral cloisters that rewards slow wandering hand-in-hand, and off-peak you can actually walk it without being swept along by tour crowds.

Recommended viewpoint landmark (Bunkers del Carmel): a free Civil War anti-aircraft battery on Turó de la Rovira with the best 360-degree panorama in the city, ideal for a cheap sunset picnic as a couple and quiet enough to linger in the off-season.

Recommended museum landmark (Museu Picasso): five medieval palaces packed with early Picasso, free on Sunday afternoons and the first Sunday of each month, which makes a low-budget couple's rainy-day plan genuinely affordable in the off-peak months.

Recommended market landmark (Mercat de la Boqueria): browsing the stalls costs nothing and a cone of jamón, fresh fruit or a bar-counter plate feeds two cheaply, with off-peak weekdays far calmer than the summer crush along La Rambla.

Recommended hilltop park landmark (Montjuïc): you can walk or take a regular city bus up to free gardens, fortress exteriors and cliff-edge views over the port, giving a couple a full free day out with no mobility constraints to worry about.

Recommended church landmark (Santa Maria del Mar): a soaring Catalan Gothic nave in El Born that asks only a small donation, pairs beautifully with a free evening stroll through the neighbourhood, and is peaceful rather than packed outside high season.

Recommended park landmark (Parc de la Ciutadella): free entry, a monumental fountain, rowing boats and lawns made for a lazy shared picnic, and in the off-season you get the space largely to yourselves instead of competing for grass.

Recommended viewpoint landmark (Tibidabo): the hilltop Temple del Sagrat Cor is free to enter and its terrace delivers the widest sweep over Barcelona, so a couple can ride up cheaply on the funicular for the view alone without paying for the vintage amusement park.
Recommended imperial palace landmark (故宫博物院): 淡季门票仅40元且人流比旺季少得多，情侣可以慢悠悠走完中轴线，预算压力也很小。
Recommended royal garden landmark (景山公园): 门票只要2元，登万春亭能俯瞰整座紫禁城，淡季傍晚人少，是性价比极高的情侣看日落地点。
Recommended imperial temple landmark (天坛公园): 淡季联票约28元，清早能看本地人晨练、听回音壁，安静又便宜，很适合两人慢慢逛半天。
Recommended royal garden landmark (颐和园): 淡季门票降到20元，昆明湖与长廊在清冷天气里人少景阔，散步拍照都不用挤，对低预算情侣很友好。
Recommended hutong district landmark (什刹海与南锣鼓巷): 完全免费，沿湖和胡同随便走就是风景，淡季小店不排队，两人可以只花几块钱买串糖葫芦逛一下午。
Recommended royal garden landmark (北海公园): 淡季门票约5元，白塔、九龙壁和湖边步道都适合并肩慢走，是市区里最便宜的一段浪漫路线。
Recommended art district landmark (798艺术区): 进区免费、多数画廊展览也不收门票，淡季展厅清静，冷天还可以躲进咖啡馆取暖，几乎不花钱就能过一天。
Recommended museum landmark (中国国家博物馆): 免费预约参观，室内暖气充足，淡季最适合避寒，两人可以看一整天而交通之外几乎没有支出。
Recommended Great Wall landmark (慕田峪长城): 淡季票价更低、游客稀少，能独享一段城墙的安静，坐公交或景区班车往返即可，是低预算也能实现的必打卡项。
Recommended historic street landmark (前门大街与大栅栏): 逛街免费，老字号小吃单价低，淡季不用排长队，适合情侣傍晚随意走走、花小钱吃点北京味道。

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Phra That Doi Suthep): entry is only about 30 baht and a shared red songthaew from the old city keeps the trip cheap for two, while the off-peak green season wraps the mountain in mist and thins the crowds on the 306-step staircase you can comfortably climb together.

Recommended market landmark (Sunday Walking Street Market): free to wander and ideal on a low budget since you and your partner can graze on 20-40 baht street snacks and split one souvenir instead of paying for a restaurant, and off-peak rains keep the famous crowds manageable.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Chedi Luang): a roughly 50 baht ticket buys the city's most photogenic ruined stupa plus the free Monk Chat tables where couples can sit and talk with novices in the low-season quiet.

raw_name: Bua Tong Sticky Waterfalls (Nam Phu Chet Si)
surface_name: Bua Tong Sticky Waterfalls (Nam Phu Chet Si)
reason: Recommended nature landmark (Bua Tong Sticky Waterfalls): there is no entry fee at all, and the limestone cascade is at its most dramatic and slippy-fun in the off-peak wet months, so a couple with full mobility can actually walk up the falls instead of just photographing them.

raw_name: Monk's Trail to Wat Pha Lat
surface_name: Monk's Trail to Wat Pha Lat
reason: Recommended hike landmark (Monk's Trail to Wat Pha Lat): a free 45-60 minute jungle climb from Suthep Road ends at a moss-covered forest temple that is at its greenest and most atmospheric during the rainy low season, making it the best zero-cost morning out for two fit walkers.

Recommended market landmark (Warorot Market): this is where local prices rule, so a couple on a tight budget can assemble a full picnic of northern sausage, nam prik and fruit for under 100 baht, and off-peak means you can actually move through the aisles.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Umong): the forest temple's brick tunnels and lake are a nearby 20 baht stop that stays cool and peaceful in the wet season, offering a quiet, uncrowded half-day that costs less than a coffee for two.

Recommended historic site landmark (Wiang Kum Kam): renting one bicycle or songthaew for a couple to tour these free-floating ancient brick ruins on the Ping River flats is cheap, and the low-season flooding and greenery give the site an overgrown, romantic character that peak visitors miss.

raw_name: Three Kings Monument and Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Center
surface_name: Three Kings Monument and Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Center
reason: Recommended museum landmark (Three Kings Monument and Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Center): a single roughly 90 baht ticket covers the air-conditioned city museum, a smart off-peak choice because it doubles as a rain shelter while giving you the historical grounding for every other temple on this list.

raw_name: Ang Kaew Reservoir and Huay Kaew Waterfall, Chiang Mai University
surface_name: Ang Kaew Reservoir and Huay Kaew Waterfall, Chiang Mai University
reason: Recommended nature landmark (Ang Kaew Reservoir and Huay Kaew Waterfall): both are free and a short walk apart at the foot of Doi Suthep, giving a low-budget couple a sunset lakeside stroll plus a cool green-season waterfall without paying for transport beyond a songthaew ride.

raw_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
surface_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
reason: Recommended 自然野生动物 landmark (成都大熊猫繁育研究基地): 门票几十元就能看到活体大熊猫，淡季早晨人少不挤，情侣可以慢慢逛上半天，是预算低也不容错过的一站。
Recommended 免费城市公园 landmark (人民公园): 免门票，两人点两碗盖碗茶二三十元就能坐一下午，淡季茶客不多，最适合情侣体验成都最便宜的慢生活。
Recommended 免费历史街区 landmark (宽窄巷子): 不收门票的清代街巷，淡季没有旺季那种人挤人，两人可以空手闲逛、拍合照，不进店消费也毫无压力。
Recommended 世界遗产水利古迹 landmark (都江堰景区): 淡季门票常有优惠，动车几十分钟直达，情侣沿鱼嘴到宝瓶口走完全程不累，性价比在周边一日游里最高。
Recommended 免费宗教古建 landmark (文殊院): 免费入园，院内免费茶水配十几元的素斋就能吃饱，淡季清静适合两人慢慢走、慢慢聊，是低预算的正经一餐。
Recommended 山林徒步 landmark (青城山前山): 淡季人少、票价更低，两人体能没问题可以全程步行上下，不必买索道，幽静山道正合情侣安静出游。
Recommended 免费博物馆 landmark (成都博物馆): 常设展免费预约，天府广场地铁直达零交通成本，淡季工作日几乎不用排队，雨天或阴冷天最好的免费去处。
Recommended 免费文创园区 landmark (东郊记忆): 老厂房改造的园区免费开放，红砖墙和铁轨很适合两人拍情侣照，淡季店铺不拥挤、咖啡也常有折扣。
Recommended 免费近郊古镇 landmark (洛带古镇): 古镇本身不收门票，公交或地铁加短驳即可到达，淡季客家人少，两人吃点小吃逛半天，人均花费很低。

raw_name: 合江亭—九眼桥锦江沿岸
surface_name: 合江亭—九眼桥锦江沿岸
reason: Recommended 免费夜间街区 landmark (合江亭—九眼桥锦江沿岸): 完全免费的江边夜景路线，淡季夜里安静好走，两人散步看灯、听河边唱歌，不必进酒吧也能收尾一天。
Recommended 历史古城 landmark (大理古城): 进城免费，淡季古城内客栈价格常比旺季低一半，两人可以慢慢逛人民路、洋人街和五华楼，预算压力很小。

raw_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）
surface_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）
reason: Recommended 湖滨步道 landmark (洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）): 全程免费开放，可扫码租双人自行车沿湖骑行，淡季人少，清晨看日出、傍晚看霞光最适合情侣慢行。
Recommended 白族古镇 landmark (喜洲古镇): 古镇本身不收门票，喜洲粑粑等小吃几元一份，淡季田野边的老宅和照壁拍照几乎无人干扰，是低预算情侣的最佳半日线路。
Recommended 宗教建筑地标 landmark (崇圣寺三塔): 大理的标志性景观，淡季游客稀少、能安静拍出三塔倒影，门票虽需购买但可提前比价联票，两人分摊后仍在低预算范围内。
Recommended 山地徒步 landmark (苍山玉带云游路): 你们没有行动限制，正好可以走这条平缓的横向山道，淡季云雾少、视野通透，进山费用低，半天徒步几乎不额外花钱。
Recommended 湖畔渔村 landmark (双廊古镇): 淡季洱海东岸的客栈价格大幅回落，两人用很低的预算就能订到能看日落的房间，白天逛渔村小巷也不收门票。
Recommended 湿地公园 landmark (海舌生态公园): 免费或仅收极低费用，狭长半岛伸入洱海、两侧水景对称，淡季安静得只剩风声，是情侣拍照和散步的省钱去处。
Recommended 手工艺村落 landmark (周城村（扎染体验）): 村里扎染作坊体验价几十元，两人可以一起做一块方巾当纪念品，淡季师傅有空手把手教，比买成品更有意思也更省钱。
Recommended 茶马古道古镇 landmark (沙溪古镇): 淡季住宿便宜到百元上下，寺登街和玉津桥一带几乎空街，适合情侣住两三晚慢慢消磨，交通以班车为主、花费不高。
Recommended 历史文化名城 landmark (巍山古城): 南诏发源地却少有游客，街区免费、民宿与一根面等小吃价格极低，淡季出行两人一天的花销可以控制在很小额度内。

Recommended historic waterfront landmark (Ribeira and Cais da Ribeira): costs nothing to wander, and off-peak you and your partner can stroll the riverfront alleys and grab a cheap bifana without the summer crush.

Recommended iron bridge landmark (Ponte Dom Luís I): a completely free walk across the upper deck gives couples the city's best panorama, and the absence of queues in low season means you can linger on the rail as long as you like.

Recommended azulejo-tiled station landmark (São Bento Railway Station): free to enter, it is a five-minute tile-art detour that fits a tight budget perfectly and is far calmer to photograph as a couple outside peak months.

Recommended religious landmark (Porto Cathedral): entry is only a few euros, and with no mobility limits you can climb the cloister stairs and terrace for rooftop views over the rooftops you just walked from.

Recommended literary landmark (Livraria Lello): a small ticket fee that can be credited against a book purchase lets you two share one souvenir, and visiting off-peak avoids the hour-long summer line outside.

Recommended market landmark (Mercado do Bolhão): free to browse and the cheapest place in town for a shared plate of cheese, presunto and a glass of vinho verde, with produce stalls at their quietest in low season.

Recommended garden landmark (Jardins do Palácio de Cristal): free, quiet and terraced, it is an ideal low-cost picnic spot for a couple, and the hillside paths are no problem given your unrestricted mobility.

Recommended baroque church landmark (Igreja de São Francisco): a modest ticket buys one of Europe's most extravagant gilded interiors and the catacombs, and off-peak you can take it in without being herded through in a crowd.

Recommended hilltop viewpoint landmark (Mosteiro da Serra do Pilar): free entry to the terrace above Vila Nova de Gaia delivers the postcard view of both bridges and Ribeira, and the walk up is well within your mobility.

Recommended coastal landmark (Foz do Douro promenade): a free tram-end walk or bus ride out to the river mouth gives you an Atlantic sunset for nothing, while off-peak restaurant prices along the front drop enough for a budget dinner for two.
Recommended free museum landmark (Musée Carnavalet): the permanent collection costs nothing and its warm, hushed galleries are a perfect off-peak afternoon for a couple keeping costs down.
Recommended public garden landmark (Jardin du Luxembourg): entry is free and out of season you and your partner can claim a chair by the basin without fighting the summer crowds.

Recommended free-entry basilica landmark (Basilique du Sacré-Cœur): visiting the basilica itself costs nothing, and the walk up through quiet Montmartre streets gives a couple a free sunset viewpoint.
Recommended historic cemetery landmark (Père Lachaise Cemetery): it is free to wander, and the bare trees and empty paths of the low season make it an eerily romantic stroll for two.
Recommended free cathedral landmark (Cathédrale Notre-Dame de Paris): entry costs nothing and off-peak queues are far shorter, so a couple can linger inside without paying or waiting long.
Recommended elevated garden walk landmark (Promenade Plantée (Coulée verte René-Dumont)): the whole 4.7 km route is free and almost deserted outside high season, ideal for a slow hand-in-hand walk.
Recommended free museum landmark (Musée de la Vie Romantique): the permanent collection is free and the courtyard tearoom gives a couple a cheap, cosy pause in a converted Romantic-era house.

raw_name: Passage des Panoramas and Galerie Vivienne
surface_name: Passage des Panoramas and Galerie Vivienne
reason: Recommended covered arcade landmark (Passage des Panoramas and Galerie Vivienne): browsing these 19th-century glass-roofed passages costs nothing and keeps a couple dry during off-peak drizzle.
Recommended open-air market landmark (Marché d'Aligre): it is free to browse and lets a budget-conscious couple assemble a picnic of cheese, bread and wine for a fraction of restaurant prices.

raw_name: Berges de Seine and Île Saint-Louis
surface_name: Berges de Seine and Île Saint-Louis
reason: Recommended riverside promenade landmark (Berges de Seine and Île Saint-Louis): the car-free banks are free to walk and the off-season dusk, with few tourists and soft river light, is one of the cheapest romantic outings in Paris.
Recommended Buddhist heritage landmark (开元寺)：免费开放、无需预约，双塔与古榕树荫下的院落适合两人慢慢逛，淡季人少时几乎可以独享整片石庭，也是低预算行程里性价比最高的一站。
Recommended historic street landmark (西街)：紧邻开元寺、完全免费，面线糊、润饼、石花膏等小吃单价极低，两个人边吃边走就能解决一顿，淡季不必排队。
Recommended ancient bridge landmark (洛阳桥)：不收费的宋代跨海石桥，傍晚沿桥走到江心看落日最适合couple，淡季无旅行团喧嚣，来回一趟不产生任何花费。
Recommended folk temple landmark (通淮关岳庙)：免费入内，香火极旺且建筑彩瓷剪粘密集精致，是零成本感受泉州民间信仰活力的地方，淡季上香不必挤。
Recommended Islamic heritage landmark (清净寺)：门票仅几元，中国现存最古老的伊斯兰教寺院之一，残存石构门楼极具氛围，淡季安静到能听见风穿过拱门，适合两人低语闲逛。
Recommended fishing village landmark (蟳埔村)：进村免费，蚵壳厝巷弄随便走，簪花围体验可自行取舍花费，淡季拍到的照片里没有别人，是低预算也能有记忆点的一站。
Recommended arcade street landmark (中山路骑楼)：免费步行街，南洋骑楼连廊遮阳避雨，夜晚灯光下的老字号与糖水铺适合两人散步消食，不花一分钱也能逛足一小时。
Recommended mountain landmark (清源山)：全程可徒步、无障碍限制者也能走完，老君岩与山脊视野适合couple半日游，成人票七十元左右是行程里最主要的一笔支出，淡季淡价、人少清凉。
Recommended Manichaean heritage landmark (草庵)：免费开放，世界仅存的摩尼教石雕光佛在此，山间小庵清幽少人，淡季去几乎包场，适合预算紧又想避开人潮的两人半天。

Recommended heritage compound landmark (上生新所): 老建筑改造的园区整体在平整地面上，没有台阶，咖啡馆与书店都有无障碍入口，人流量比热门景点小得多，正好避开旺季排队，让情侣能悠闲地坐一下午。

Recommended landscape garden landmark (Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden): Its broad, level, fully paved loop paths are genuinely rollable and wheelchairs are lent free at the gates, making it the rare Tokyo garden where a couple can spend a slow afternoon together without a single stair or gravel track.

Recommended art and antiquities museum landmark (Tokyo National Museum): Ramps, lifts to every gallery floor and free loaner wheelchairs mean the couple can see the samurai swords and screens at their own pace, and the air-conditioned halls are a sensible escape when peak-season humidity peaks.

Recommended rooftop observation deck landmark (Shibuya Sky): A dedicated lift carries you from the 14th floor to the 45th-floor deck on a barrier-free route, and the sunset slot over the Scramble Crossing is the single most couple-friendly view in the city — reserve the timed sunset entry well ahead during peak season, as it sells out.

Recommended 街区漫步 landmark (宽窄巷子): 免费开放，淡季巷子里不拥挤，两人可以慢慢逛小店、坐院子里的咖啡馆，消费可控。

Recommended 历史街区 landmark (中山路骑楼老街): 全线为无台阶的平整步行路面、骑楼连廊全天遮阳挡雨，轮椅推行顺畅，两侧老字号小吃与咖啡馆价格亲民，淡季傍晚散步最适合两人慢慢逛。

Recommended 世界遗产·民间信仰 landmark (天后宫): 山门至正殿一路平地、无高差门槛可绕行，免费开放，位于城南生活区、周边餐饮便宜，淡季清幽，适合情侣顺路串游德济门遗址。

Recommended 历史街区 landmark (五店市传统街区): 经整治的步行街区地面平整、主街无台阶并配有无障碍卫生间，红砖厝与咖啡馆适合情侣拍照小坐，免费进入、消费中等，淡季来几乎可以包场慢逛。
Recommended 文创园区 landmark (源和1916创意产业园): 旧厂房改造后地面全部硬化平整、无台阶障碍，电梯与缓坡连接各栋，免费开放、咖啡馆与创意小店客单价中等，淡季夜晚灯光安静，适合两人作为一天行程的轻松收尾。
Recommended waterfront landmark (外滩): 1.5公里滨江步道全程平坦无台阶、坡度极缓，轮椅可直上观景平台，沿线有无障碍卫生间与多处休息座椅，淡季清晨或夜晚人少，很适合两人慢慢推着走看天际线。

surface_name: 上海博物馆（人民广场馆）

surface_name: 上海中心大厦“上海之巅”观光厅
reason: Recommended observation deck landmark (上海中心大厦上海之巅观光厅): 从地下入口到118层全程电梯直达、无台阶换乘，观景层地面平整且轮椅回转空间充足，淡季傍晚购票不排长队，两人并肩看落日与夜景是此行的高光。
Recommended science museum landmark (上海自然博物馆): 坡道入口、全馆无障碍电梯与宽敞展区对轮椅非常友好，门票价格中等、淡季不限流，展陈节奏舒缓，适合情侣边看边聊度过一个下午。
Recommended art museum landmark (上海当代艺术博物馆): 由老电厂改造，特设无障碍坡道与直达各展厅的电梯，展厅开阔无门槛，多数常设展免费、特展票价温和，淡季观展人少，适合两人慢慢看展拍照。

surface_name: 徐汇滨江（西岸滨江步道）

Recommended historic district landmark (新天地): 石库门街区经过改造后主通道平坦、路口有缓坡，餐厅与咖啡馆密集且价位中等，淡季露天座位好找，两人可以坐着喝一杯、慢慢逛小店而不必赶路。
Recommended library landmark (上海图书馆东馆): 新建馆体从地铁口到各阅览层全程无高差、电梯与无障碍卫生间齐全，免费入馆，淡季工作日极为安静，适合情侣各拿一本书待上半天、顺便看建筑本身。
Recommended urban park landmark (世纪公园): 园内主环道平整可全程轮椅通行，门票仅十元上下，淡季游人稀疏、秋冬季节庆活动少，租一辆双人车或在湖边坐着都很惬意，性价比极高。

surface_name: 苏州河滨水步道（外滩源—四行仓库段）
reason: Recommended waterfront walk landmark (苏州河滨水步道): 新贯通的步道设有连续无障碍坡道、无台阶断点，全程免费且淡季几乎无人，傍晚沿河慢行看老桥与仓库改造建筑，是外滩之外更安静的一条两人路线。

Recommended Historic temple landmark (Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise-dori): The flat, paved approach and ramped main-hall entrance keep the whole route step-free for a wheelchair, while off-peak mornings let a couple wander the lantern-lit lane and garden at an easy pace without the peak-season crush.

Recommended Observation tower landmark (Tokyo Skytree & Tokyo Solamachi): Elevators run door-to-deck with no stairs anywhere in the building, and off-peak ticketing means a couple can share the Tembo Deck sunset view and the adjacent mall's affordable food floor without standing in long queues.

Recommended Landscape garden landmark (Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden): A level loop of paved and firm-gravel paths links all three garden styles, free wheelchair loans are available at the gates, and the modest entry fee plus quiet off-peak weekdays make it a low-cost, unhurried half-day for two.

Recommended Digital art museum landmark (teamLab Borderless (Azabudai Hills)): The entire gallery is served by lifts and level floors with no stepped sections, so a wheelchair user and partner can drift through the immersive rooms together, and off-peak timed slots cost the same but come with far more breathing room.

Recommended Art and antiquities museum landmark (Tokyo National Museum, Ueno Park): Step-free entrances, lifts to every gallery and complimentary wheelchair loans mean the collections are fully navigable, and the flat central promenade of Ueno Park makes the approach from the station easy for a couple on a medium budget.

raw_name: Miraikan – National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation
surface_name: Miraikan – National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation
reason: Recommended Science museum landmark (Miraikan – National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation): Purpose-built barrier-free design with lifts, wide aisles and accessible restrooms on every floor suits a wheelchair user perfectly, and the flat Odaiba waterfront outside gives a couple an easy, budget-friendly walk to lunch afterwards.

Recommended Tidal landscape garden landmark (Hama-rikyu Gardens): The level circuit around the tidal pond is fully passable by wheelchair with an accessible route to the island teahouse, so a couple can share matcha and a skyline view without stairs, and off-peak entry is inexpensive and rarely crowded.

Recommended Traditional performing arts landmark (Kabukiza Theatre, Ginza): Wheelchair spaces are bookable in advance and lifts reach the upper tiers, and single-act 'makumi' tickets let a couple sample kabuki in Ginza at a fraction of a full-programme price without committing a whole day.

Recommended Free city observatory landmark (Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observatory): Lift access runs from the ground floor directly to the 45th-floor deck with no stairs, entry costs nothing, and off-peak weekday visits give a couple an uncrowded panorama that leaves more of the budget for dinner.

raw_name: Odaiba Seaside Park & Rainbow Bridge Promenade
surface_name: Odaiba Seaside Park & Rainbow Bridge Promenade
reason: Recommended Waterfront park landmark (Odaiba Seaside Park & Rainbow Bridge Promenade): Wide, level boardwalks and ramped access to the beach and promenade make the whole bayfront route wheelchair-friendly, and a couple can take in the Rainbow Bridge sunset and the free Yurikamome-view terraces without spending on paid attractions.

Recommended basilica landmark (Sagrada Família): Step-free entry with lifts to the tower and an accessible ground-floor route make Gaudí's masterpiece easy for a couple to enjoy at a quieter off-peak pace, and mid-range timed tickets keep the cost reasonable.

Recommended park landmark (Park Güell): The monumental zone has a signed accessible route with ramps and a shuttle from the entrance, so you can take in the mosaic terraces and city views together without stairs, and off-peak queues are short.

Recommended museum landmark (Casa Batlló): A step-free entrance on Passeig de Gràcia, a lift serving every floor and an accessible rooftop make this Modernista house fully visitable, and the smart-ticket price sits comfortably in a medium budget.

Recommended museum landmark (La Pedrera): A dedicated accessible entrance and lift take you up to the warrior rooftops and the attic exhibition, giving a couple the full Gaudí experience with no stairs and thinner off-peak crowds.

Recommended historic site landmark (Hospital de Sant Pau): Flat paved paths, ramps and lifts across the restored Modernista pavilions suit wheelchair users perfectly, and it is one of the calmest, least crowded major sights in the off-peak months.
Recommended museum landmark (MNAC): Full step-free access from the Montjuïc side with lifts to every gallery, plus broad uncrowded halls and a moderate ticket price that works well for two.
Recommended art gallery landmark (Fundació Joan Miró): Lifts connect all levels and the terraces offer step-free city views, making this a relaxed, affordable off-peak stop for a couple on Montjuïc.
Recommended science museum landmark (CosmoCaixa): Everything is served by lifts and gentle ramps, it is fully climate-controlled for cooler off-peak days, and combined couple tickets are modest.

Recommended waterfront landmark (Port Vell and Barceloneta promenade): A continuous flat, kerb-free boardwalk links the Rambal de Mar, the marina and the accessible beach walkways, ideal for an easy low-cost evening stroll for two.

Recommended concert hall landmark (Palau de la Música Catalana): Step-free access, a lift and an accessible route through the guided tour let you both see the Modernista interior, and off-peak tour slots are cheaper and less busy.
Recommended 皇家宫殿 landmark (故宫博物院（紫禁城）): 午门可免费租借轮椅并设有官方无障碍参观线路，主要门区铺坡道，中轴线参观路线平缓；淡季门票便宜、人流少，适合两人在无障碍通道上从容游览。
Recommended 城市广场 landmark (天安门广场): 广场为平整的花岗岩地面、无台阶，轮椅通行顺畅，地铁1号线直达；淡季清晨人少，适合情侣看升旗仪式并顺路游览，而且免费。
Recommended 皇家祭坛 landmark (天坛公园): 丹陛桥与主要园路都是平缓坡道，园区可在门口借轮椅；淡季的早晨能看本地人晨练、听回音壁，节奏慢，两人慢慢走也不累。
Recommended 皇家园林 landmark (颐和园): 从东宫门进园后，长廊一带地势平坦，园内提供轮椅租借，也可乘游船横渡昆明湖来避开爬坡；淡季票价低、湖面清静，适合情侣慢逛。
Recommended 国家级博物馆 landmark (中国国家博物馆): 免费预约参观，馆内电梯、坡道与轮椅租借齐备，全程可无障碍通行；淡季（冬季）室内恒温，可作为半天的室内行程，省去户外受冻。
Recommended 城市博物馆 landmark (首都博物馆): 全馆无障碍设计完善（电梯、无障碍卫生间、轮椅借用），免费预约；淡季人少时可以安静看老北京展，室内行程也不受天气影响。
Recommended 艺术区 landmark (798艺术区): 园区主路为平整沥青、基本没有台阶，画廊多有坡道，免费进入，咖啡馆价位适中；淡季工作日人少，适合情侣拍照、看展，一逛就是半天。

surface_name: 奥林匹克公园（鸟巢·水立方外观）
reason: Recommended 现代地标 landmark (奥林匹克公园（鸟巢·水立方外观）): 中轴景观大道宽阔平整、没有台阶，地铁8号线可直达，无障碍设施完善；淡季傍晚灯光亮起时人少景美，免费散步很适合情侣。
Recommended 历史商业街 landmark (前门大街与大栅栏): 前门大街为平坦的无障碍步行街，可乘坐铛铛车代步，沿途老字号餐饮价格中档；淡季游人稀少，两人可轻松逛店、吃小吃。
Recommended 遗址公园 landmark (圆明园遗址公园): 东侧湖区与遗址主路地势平坦，门口可租轮椅，园内电瓶车可代步；淡季门票便宜、园中清静，适合情侣在湖边慢走、看西洋楼遗址。

Recommended contemporary art museum landmark (MAIIAM Contemporary Art Museum): Entirely step-free from car park to galleries — ramps, wide doorways and a lift between floors — so a couple can spend an unhurried, air-conditioned afternoon with Lanna and Southeast Asian art for about 200 THB each, and its café terrace stays pleasantly quiet through the green season.

Recommended botanical garden landmark (Royal Park Rajapruek): A paved, near-level loop links the royal pavilions, orchid house and international gardens, wheelchairs are available at the entrance and a shuttle tram covers the longer stretches, while off-peak months mean you two get the flower beds and mountain backdrop almost to yourselves.

raw_name: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center and Lanna Folklife Museum
surface_name: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center and Lanna Folklife Museum
reason: Recommended cultural centre landmark (Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center and Lanna Folklife Museum): Ramp entry, a lift to the upper galleries and cool, seated-friendly exhibition rooms make this twin museum on the Three Kings Monument square the most reliable rain-proof half-day in the old city, and at a few hundred baht for two it sits comfortably in a medium budget.

Recommended Buddhist temple landmark (Wat Chedi Luang): The walled compound is flat and paved with only a couple of shallow steps at the main vihara, so a wheelchair rolls easily around the great ruined chedi, and late-afternoon light there is the closest thing to a romantic set piece in the old city once low-season crowds thin out.

Recommended Buddhist temple landmark (Wat Suan Dok): A wide, level entrance gate and a spacious paved courtyard mean no stairs between the road and the white burial chedis, and the weekday monk-chat session gives a couple an easy, free cultural hour with sunset views back to Doi Suthep.

Recommended forest temple landmark (Wat Umong): Shaded, largely level paths run between the tunnel shrines, fish pond and stupa, keeping you cool in the hot or wet months, though the surface turns gravelly and uneven in patches so a partner's push is worth planning for.

raw_name: Warorot Market (Kad Luang) and Ton Lamyai Flower Market
surface_name: Warorot Market (Kad Luang) and Ton Lamyai Flower Market
reason: Recommended market landmark (Warorot Market (Kad Luang) and Ton Lamyai Flower Market): The ground-floor aisles are flat and step-free, so a couple can graze northern Thai snacks and browse the flower stalls at street level — go early on a weekday morning in the off-season for space to move and the best food.

Recommended shopping and dining district landmark (Nimmanhaemin Road and One Nimman): Flat, kerbed-but-ramped pavements, lift access and clustered galleries, coffee bars and mid-range restaurants make this the easiest evening out for two, with the covered One Nimman courtyard doubling as shelter when the monsoon arrives.

Recommended national museum landmark (Chiang Mai National Museum): Ramped entrance, an internal lift and full air-conditioning make it the dependable wet-day plan for a couple, and its Lanna Buddhist art collection pairs well with a short hop to nearby Wat Chet Yot's flat, grassy grounds.

Recommended mountain temple landmark (Wat Phra That Doi Suthep): A funicular lift beside the main stairway carries wheelchair users up to the golden chedi terrace, so the city's signature sight is reachable with a companion's help — arrive by songthaew early on a weekday in low season, when the narrow upper terrace is clear enough to move through.

Recommended 城市博物馆 landmark (成都博物馆): 免费，全馆电梯和无障碍卫生间齐全，全程无台阶。淡季不拥挤，阴冷天也能舒适逛，在天府广场地铁站旁，适合中预算情侣。
Recommended 考古博物馆 landmark (金沙遗址博物馆): 展厅与遗迹馆都有电梯和无障碍坡道，园区步道平坦。提供轮椅借用，淡季观展安静，票价适中。
Recommended 古典园林 landmark (杜甫草堂博物馆): 主要游览线为平整石板路，入口有坡道，轮椅可通行全园。淡季清幽，适合情侣慢走拍照，门票价格中等。
Recommended 历史文化 landmark (武侯祠): 中轴主线平坦，有坡道和轮椅借用点，参观动线集中、不耗体力。与锦里相连，一天可轻松安排，淡季票价更从容。
Recommended 传统街区 landmark (锦里古街): 主街整体平坦，无台阶，轮椅可直行，小吃和茶馆密集。淡季傍晚人少，情侣逛吃方便，花费可控。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (宽窄巷子): 三条主巷平整可推轮椅，部分院落门槛略高可绕行。淡季客流少更好通行，街区免费，茶馆消费适合中预算。
Recommended 省级博物馆 landmark (四川博物院): 免费开放，设无障碍电梯、坡道和轮椅借用，展厅全程无台阶。淡季人少，室内不受湿冷天气影响，适合情侣半日游。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (人民公园（鹤鸣茶社）): 园内道路平坦硬化，入口无台阶，轮椅可直达茶社。淡季喝盖碗茶、看本地生活，人均几十元，很合适情侣耗一整个下午。
Recommended 现代商业街区 landmark (成都远洋太古里·IFS): 开放式街区全平层，电梯与无障碍卫生间完善，全程无需上下台阶。淡季逛街不挤，餐饮选择多、中档价位，适合情侣晚间散步用餐。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (大理古城): 复兴路与人民路两条主街平缓无台阶，淡季游客稀少时轮椅可从容通行，两边咖啡馆与客栈价格适中，适合两人慢逛半天。
Recommended 湖滨步道 landmark (洱海生态廊道): 全线为平整的沥青路与木栈道，坡度极缓，入口处有坡道，淡季几乎无人，是情侣推轮椅看日落最省力的一段。
Recommended 佛教古迹 landmark (崇圣寺三塔): 景区用观光车和坡道把各殿连接起来，主步道是平整石板，淡季门票和讲解常有折扣，两人可以轻松走完核心区。
Recommended 古典园林 landmark (三塔倒影公园): 园区地势平坦，环绕水池一圈的路径都没有台阶，门票便宜且淡季清静，是拍三塔合影时最省力的取景点。
Recommended 白族古镇 landmark (喜洲古镇): 四方街与主街基本平整，轮椅可以直接推到严家大院门口和稻田观景处，淡季住宿餐饮价格低，适合安排住一晚。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (大理州博物馆): 新馆设有无障碍坡道、电梯和无障碍卫生间，免费参观且淡季人少，下雨或风大时是稳妥的室内备选。

surface_name: Thai cooking class at a countryside farm school

Recommended historical landmark (武侯祠): 红墙竹影是成都最出片的角落之一，淡季光线通透无需排队等人散，两人可搭配锦里一同安排半日，再在附近选一家高端川菜馆收尾。

Recommended historic district landmark (宽窄巷子): 淡季的清晨巷子里几乎无人，适合牵手拍空镜，两旁院落院坝里的私房菜与精品茶室正好承接高预算的午晚餐安排。

Recommended 历史古迹 landmark (崇圣寺三塔)：淡季可从容请讲解员细看三塔与倒影公园，清晨光线最好且几乎无人，适合情侣拍质感照片而非赶场打卡。
Recommended 古镇 landmark (喜洲古镇)：预算充足可入住古镇精品院落酒店，白天逛严家大院、尝喜洲粑粑，淡季店铺不排队，适合两人慢节奏过半天到一晚。

Recommended 古城 landmark (巍山古城)：游客远少于大理古城，淡季更清净，两人可整日扫街吃𤆵肉饵丝、蜜饯与一根面，是预算充裕时最有味道的一日美食之旅。
Recommended 古村落 landmark (诺邓古村)：上千年的盐井村落层层叠叠，淡季几乎无团队客，两人可请当地向导走盐马古道、住村中改造院落并尝年份诺邓火腿。
Recommended 文化体验 landmark (张家花园)：白族三坊一照壁建筑的精品范例，淡季可包场看白族歌舞与三道茶表演，无需与团队客拼场，适合追求私密感的高预算情侣。

Recommended Literary and architectural landmark (Livraria Lello): In the off-peak months you can book a timed premium entry and actually linger on the forked Neo-Gothic staircase as a couple, instead of being swept along by the summer convoys that make the €8 ticket feel like a queue fee.

Recommended Historic landmark (Palácio da Bolsa): Off-peak guided tours of the Arab Room and the General Assembly Hall run with small groups, and the palace's private after-hours visit is both bookable and genuinely intimate for two when the cruise crowds are absent.

Recommended Monument landmark (Torre dos Clérigos): Climbing the 240-odd steps late on a grey-season afternoon means you and your partner get the 360° rooftop view over the tiled rooftops almost to yourselves, rather than shuffling up behind a queue in July heat.

Recommended Baroque religious landmark (Igreja de São Francisco): The astonishing gilded interior and the catacombs beneath are best absorbed in near-silence, which is exactly what the low season delivers, and the modest ticket leaves budget for the private guide who explains the gilding properly.

Recommended Wine cellar landmark (Taylor's Port Lodge): High-budget couples can take a reserved Vintage flight or a private tasting room in Vila Nova de Gaia during off-peak, when booking a prime sunset slot on the terrace is easy and the cellars are quiet enough to talk.

Recommended Contemporary art museum landmark (Museu de Serralves): The pink Art Deco villa, the Álvaro Siza galleries and the wooded park make a full unhurried half-day for two, and off-peak exhibitions mean you can stand in front of a piece without a school group behind you — with rain as a non-issue indoors.

Recommended Culinary market landmark (Mercado do Bolhão): The restored 1914 market lets a couple graze premium presunto, Serra da Estrela cheese and tinned fish at the counters, and in the off-peak months the stalls are calm enough to chat with vendors rather than fight through tour throngs.

Recommended Scenic river landmark (Six Bridges Douro cruise): Chartering a small private sailboat or the premium cockpit of a rabelo at golden hour is far easier and more negotiable off-peak, giving you both the Douro bridges and a glass of port without a shared-deck crowd.

Recommended Coastal landmark (Foz do Douro and Matosinhos): A long Atlantic walk from the Felgueiras lighthouse to the Matosinhos fish grills pairs well with a high-end seafood lunch, and off-peak you can actually get a table at the celebrated spots without the summer reservation scramble.

Recommended Music venue landmark (Casa da Música): Rem Koolhaas's angular concrete hall stages fado, jazz and classical year-round, and in the off-peak season good seats for two are available at short notice — a civilised rainy-evening counterpoint to the historic centre.

Recommended museum landmark (Musée du Louvre): In off-peak months the Richelieu and Sully wings are quiet enough for two people to drift between rooms at their own pace, and a high budget buys a private after-hours or opening-hour guide who can route you past the crowds entirely.

Recommended palace landmark (Palace of Versailles): Off-peak is the one window when the Hall of Mirrors isn't shoulder-to-shoulder, and with no mobility constraints you can pair a chauffeured private transfer with the full walk out to the Grand Canal and Marie-Antoinette's estate.

Recommended monument landmark (Eiffel Tower): Shorter off-peak lift queues make a sunset summit visit genuinely relaxed, and a high budget secures a table at Le Jules Verne plus the stairs-down descent that only unrestricted walkers can enjoy.

Recommended museum landmark (Musée d'Orsay): The converted Belle Époque station is intimate enough for a couple to share headphones over the Impressionist galleries, and off-peak timing plus a private curator-led slot turns a two-hour visit into a leisurely half-day.

Recommended opera house landmark (Palais Garnier): Booking a box for a ballet or opera in the quieter off-peak season is exactly the kind of splurge a couple with a generous budget can plan months ahead, and the gilded Grand Foyer is best lingered in when the interval crowd thins.

Recommended church landmark (Sainte-Chapelle): Low off-peak sun angles light the 1,113 stained-glass panels at their most dramatic, and the narrow spiral stair up to the upper chapel is no obstacle for a couple with full mobility.

Recommended neighbourhood landmark (Montmartre and Sacré-Cœur): Out of season the vine-covered lanes and Place des Abbesses belong to locals again, so a couple can climb the hill through the quieter back streets at dawn and finish with a long lunch on a terrace.

Recommended cruise landmark (Private Seine dinner cruise): A chartered or small-vessel evening sailing past the illuminated Louvre and Notre-Dame is a natural couple's set piece, and off-peak pricing makes a fully private boat with a dedicated chef an easy call at this budget.

Recommended neighbourhood landmark (Le Marais and Musée Picasso): Off-peak the hôtels particuliers, concept boutiques and gallery openings are unhurried enough for a couple to browse for hours, with a high budget covering a private Picasso collection walk and a table at a Michelin-starred bistro nearby.

Recommended garden landmark (Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden): Its main loop is broad, level and paved with free wheelchair loans, accessible toilets and no stairs on the central routes, making a quiet off-peak weekday morning the ideal time for a couple to wander the English and Japanese landscapes at a slow pace.

Recommended museum landmark (Tokyo National Museum, Ueno): All wings are served by lifts with step-free entry, loaner wheelchairs and seating in every gallery, and the off-peak months let a couple take the Honkan and Hyokeikan at gallery-quiet pace before a high-end lunch in Ueno's museum district.

Recommended botanical garden landmark (Jardin des Plantes): Free garden access plus a cheap menagerie and the free Grande Galerie side galleries make this the best value half-day for a family on a tight budget.

Recommended basilica landmark (Sacré-Cœur and Montmartre): Basilica entry costs nothing, the funicular saves little legs, and the car-free square with street performers and crepe stalls entertains children without a paid attraction.

surface_name: Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden, Mae Rim
reason: Recommended garden landmark (Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden): Cheap entry with discounted children's tickets, glasshouses and canopy walkways that feel adventurous to a kid, and cool-season flowering at its peak — worth the songthaew or rented-car trip north as a half-day low-budget outing.

raw_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
surface_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
reason: Recommended Wildlife & Nature landmark (成都大熊猫繁育研究基地): Watching giant pandas up close is a magical, affordable, and child-friendly experience that tops every family's bucket list in Chengdu, with early morning visits offering the best activity from the animals during peak season.

Recommended Cultural Street landmark (锦里古街): This lively, free-to-enter ancient street offers children colorful snacks, folk performances, and traditional crafts at very low cost, making it a perfect budget-friendly family outing during the busy travel season.

Recommended Historical Site landmark (武侯祠): Located next to Jinli, this low-cost shrine brings Three Kingdoms history to life for curious children and parents alike, offering great educational value without straining a tight family budget.

Recommended UNESCO Heritage & Nature landmark (都江堰景区): This 2,000-year-old irrigation wonder combines scenic river landscapes and open-air exploration that energetic children love, with a reasonable entrance fee and easy accessibility for the whole family.

Recommended Cultural Street landmark (宽窄巷子): Free to stroll through, these well-preserved Qing Dynasty alleyways offer families affordable street food, local performances, and a vivid taste of old Chengdu culture that keeps children engaged.

Recommended Zoo & Family Attraction landmark (成都动物园): One of China's most affordable city zoos, it houses hundreds of species including red pandas and is perfectly suited for young children who can enjoy a full day of animal encounters without exceeding a low budget.

Recommended Scenic Mountain landmark (青城山): Known as the 'Most Secluded Mountain Under Heaven,' its gentle forested trails and Taoist temples are manageable for children of all ages, offering a refreshing natural escape at a budget-friendly entrance price.

Recommended Public Park landmark (人民公园): This free urban park features a beloved teahouse culture, pedal boats on the lake, and open lawns where children can play freely, making it an ideal low-cost relaxation spot for families during the peak travel rush.

Recommended Museum landmark (成都自然博物馆): This modern, visually stunning museum with impressive dinosaur skeletons and geological exhibits sparks children's curiosity at a very low admission fee, offering a cool indoor retreat during the hot peak-season weather.

Recommended Historical Park landmark (望江楼公园): This tranquil riverside park with a famous Ming Dynasty tower and the world's largest bamboo collection provides a serene, low-cost family walk where children can discover giant bamboo groves and enjoy riverside scenery.
Recommended 自然景观 landmark (洱海生态廊道): 全线免费开放、路面平坦宽阔，孩子可以安全骑车跑跳，旺季清晨或傍晚来避暑避人流，一分钱不花就能玩上大半天。
Recommended 历史人文 landmark (大理古城): 进城不收门票，街巷里小吃和米线价格亲民，孩子走累了随时能找地方坐下，无行动限制的一家人逛起来最省力。
Recommended 古镇 landmark (喜洲古镇): 古镇本身免费，几块钱的喜洲粑粑就能哄住孩子，周边稻田开阔可撒欢，比隔壁双廊更适合带小孩慢逛。
Recommended 宗教古迹 landmark (崇圣寺三塔): 大理地标值得看一次，儿童按身高免票、一家四口花费可控，旺季务必赶开门时段入园，避开正午暴晒与团队人流。
Recommended 山岳 landmark (苍山（感通索道·清碧溪）): 坐索道上山省去爬坡体力，孩子对缆车和溪水兴趣大，山顶气温比古城低好几度，是旺季最有效的天然避暑方案。
Recommended 自然景观 landmark (蝴蝶泉公园): 门票便宜、园区不大，蝴蝶标本和泉水对孩子有天然吸引力，一两小时就能逛完，不会让小朋友走到崩溃。

raw_name: 大理白族自治州博物馆
surface_name: 大理白族自治州博物馆
reason: Recommended 博物馆 landmark (大理白族自治州博物馆): 免费参观且室内有空调，旺季正午暴雨或暴晒时的最佳备选，孩子能看懂的白族服饰和民俗展陈很友好。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (洱海公园（团山）): 免票入园、有草坪和儿童游乐设施，湖景一览无余，适合当作行程间隙让孩子放电、大人歇脚的低成本半日点。
Recommended 湖滨 landmark (龙龛码头): 完全免费，水浅岸平适合孩子踩水看日出，旺季清早六点多人少凉爽，是全程性价比最高的一次清晨出行。
Recommended 古镇 landmark (双廊古镇): 逛镇不花钱、洱海视野最好，但旺季午后极挤，建议带娃上午前往并只在主街短逛，避免在窄巷里推挤。

Recommended garden landmark (Jardins do Palácio de Cristal): free to enter, with roaming peacocks, playgrounds, fountains and lots of mature shade that lets kids burn energy while parents escape the peak-summer heat without spending a euro.

Recommended park landmark (Parque da Cidade do Porto): Porto's biggest green space is completely free, flat and stroller-friendly, and its shaded lawns plus lakes make an ideal low-cost half-day where children can run freely after a morning of sightseeing.

Recommended beach landmark (Praia de Matosinhos): a wide, free Atlantic beach with lifeguards, calm-enough shallow edges for young swimmers and a promenade of cheap snack spots, perfect for cooling off during the hot peak-season afternoons.

Recommended bridge landmark (Ponte Luís I (upper deck walk)): crossing the top deck on foot costs nothing and delivers the city's most thrilling free viewpoint, with a tram ride back down as an optional cheap treat for kids who love anything on rails.

Recommended waterfront landmark (Cais da Ribeira): strolling the old riverfront is free, and the boats, buskers and plaza fountains give children constant free entertainment while the family soaks up Porto's most photogenic quarter.

Recommended viewpoint garden landmark (Jardim do Morro): a free grassy hilltop in Gaia where kids can roll down the slope and watch the sunset over the bridge, making it a no-cost evening highlight that suits energetic families with no mobility limits.

Recommended tidal pool landmark (Piscina das Marés): architect Álvaro Siza's seawater pools in Leça da Palmeira charge only a few euros, giving children safe, supervised ocean swimming in peak season for far less than a theme park or aquarium ticket.

Recommended market landmark (Mercado do Bolhão): entry is free and the two floors of produce, fish and counters turn grocery shopping into a sensory outing, with inexpensive fresh fruit, pastries and petiscos to feed a family on a tight budget.

Recommended funicular landmark (Funicular dos Guindais): for the price of pocket change, this short steep ride between Ribeira and Batalha is a mini roller-coaster thrill for children and saves the family a hot uphill climb in peak season.

Recommended fortress landmark (Castelo do Queijo): the exterior, ramparts and surrounding rocks are free to explore and sit right beside Foz's beaches, so a single low-cost afternoon covers a mini castle adventure, tide-pooling and a seaside picnic.

raw_name: Notre-Dame Cathedral and Île de la Cité
surface_name: Notre-Dame Cathedral and Île de la Cité
reason: Recommended cathedral landmark (Notre-Dame Cathedral and Île de la Cité): Entry is free, the newly reopened interior and the open square give restless kids room to move, and the surrounding island walk costs nothing — ideal for a low-budget family in peak season if you arrive early to beat the queue.

Recommended garden landmark (Jardin du Luxembourg): Free to enter, with a fenced playground, pony rides, toy sailboats and endless shaded paths where children can run while parents sit — the single best value afternoon for a family on a low budget.

Recommended garden landmark (Jardin des Plantes): A free botanical garden with a small zoo, a free children's maze and the Grande Galerie de l'Évolution next door, giving a whole day of kid-friendly content for a few euros at most.

Recommended basilica landmark (Sacré-Cœur Basilica and Montmartre): The basilica is free to visit, the steps and carousel outside are a hit with children, and the climb through Montmartre's streets rewards you with the city's best free viewpoint.

Recommended museum landmark (Musée Carnavalet): Permanent collections are free, the galleries are compact enough for short attention spans, and the Paris history displays give kids a story to follow on every later walk.

Recommended museum landmark (Petit Palais): Free entry to the permanent collection plus a lovely courtyard café and garden, making it an easy, low-cost rainy-day or heat-break stop with children in the middle of peak season.

Recommended park landmark (Parc de la Villette): Free to enter and packed with themed playgrounds, water features and wide lawns, and its Canal de l'Ourcq setting offers a full free day out with no ticket needed.

Recommended riverfront event landmark (Paris Plages): Every summer the Seine banks are turned into free beaches with sand, games and water play, which is exactly the kind of zero-cost, high-energy activity that suits a low-budget family in the hottest weeks.

raw_name: Champ de Mars and the Eiffel Tower esplanade
surface_name: Champ de Mars and the Eiffel Tower esplanade
reason: Recommended esplanade landmark (Champ de Mars and the Eiffel Tower esplanade): You get the iconic tower view, a huge lawn for a picnic and free space to run without buying a ticket, and it pairs well with a cheap bakery lunch.

raw_name: Bois de Vincennes and the Ferme de Paris
surface_name: Bois de Vincennes and the Ferme de Paris
reason: Recommended farm landmark (Bois de Vincennes and the Ferme de Paris): A free working farm with animals plus a vast wooded park with lakes and boats, giving a full countryside-style day inside the city at almost no cost.
Recommended temple landmark (开元寺): 门票免费、院落地势平坦开阔，孩子可以在东西塔前跑动拍照，不用花钱也不累，旺季一早开门就进去能避开人流高峰。
Recommended historic street landmark (西街—中山路历史街区): 街区完全免费，骑楼有遮阳挡雨的长廊，小吃单价低、孩子边走边吃就能逛半天，适合低预算家庭在旺季灵活安排时间。

raw_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
surface_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
reason: Recommended museum landmark (泉州海外交通史博物馆): 免费参观且有空调，旺季正午最热最挤的时段正好带孩子进馆看宋代古船和航海模型，寓教于乐又零花费。
Recommended historic bridge landmark (洛阳桥): 免费开放、桥面平缓无台阶，孩子能近距离看千年石梁和养蛎固基的构造，清早或傍晚去既凉快又避开团队游客。
Recommended village landmark (蟳埔村): 不用门票，蚵壳厝和中老年妇女的簪花围头饰对孩子来说像逛活的民俗展，拍照体验花销小，是低预算亲子行程里最出片的一站。
Recommended temple landmark (泉州府文庙): 免费进入，大成殿前有大片广场和树荫可以歇脚，旺季碰上周末还能免费听一场南音，孩子坐得住也不额外花钱。
Recommended temple landmark (天后宫): 免票且紧邻德济门遗址，动线短、步行量小，孩子看完妈祖像还能在周边老街买便宜小吃，适合安排在行程较满的那天。
Recommended mountain landmark (清源山): 门票价格低，老君岩石像对孩子有天然吸引力，山道有台阶但你们无行动限制可以边走边玩，建议旺季清晨上山避开日晒和人潮。
Recommended ancient city landmark (崇武古城): 门票便宜且一票兼得古城墙与海滨沙滩，孩子可以在海边玩沙玩水一整天，是低预算家庭把'看历史'和'放电'合并解决的选择。
Recommended temple landmark (泉州少林寺): 免费或象征性门票，固定时段的南少林武术表演对孩子吸引力最大，看完还能在寺内空地走动，旺季建议提前确认表演时间再前往。

Recommended Theme Park landmark (上海迪士尼乐园): This world-class family theme park offers countless child-friendly rides and entertainment that perfectly suits families traveling with children, and budget-conscious visitors can plan ahead with combo tickets and packed meals to manage costs during peak season.

Recommended Nature & Wildlife landmark (上海野生动物园): This expansive zoo features up-close animal encounters and safari bus rides that children absolutely love, with affordable family group tickets making it a great low-budget option during peak travel season.

Recommended Cultural Heritage landmark (豫园): This classical Ming Dynasty garden in the heart of the old city offers free or low-cost entry and immerses families with children in authentic Chinese culture and architecture, especially lively during peak season festivals.

Recommended Iconic Landmark landmark (外滩): This iconic riverside promenade is completely free to stroll along and provides stunning views of the Pudong skyline, making it a perfect no-cost family outing that children and adults alike enjoy during peak season evenings.

Recommended Museum & Education landmark (上海科技馆): This highly interactive science museum features hands-on exhibits designed specifically for children that spark curiosity and learning, with reasonably priced family tickets that suit a low budget.

raw_name: 人民广场与城市规划展示馆
surface_name: 人民广场与城市规划展示馆
reason: Recommended Cultural & Educational landmark (人民广场与城市规划展示馆): The expansive public square is free to visit and the adjacent urban planning museum offers affordable entry with fascinating scale models of Shanghai that captivate children's imagination.

Recommended Nature & Wildlife landmark (上海动物园): One of China's largest urban zoos with a wide variety of animals including giant pandas, offering very affordable admission fees that fit a low-budget family trip during the busy peak season.

Recommended Cultural & Leisure landmark (田子坊): This free-to-enter creative arts and crafts alley in the French Concession is fun to explore with children, offering affordable local snacks and souvenirs in a vibrant atmosphere popular during peak season.

Recommended Museum & Education landmark (上海自然博物馆): This modern natural history museum features life-size dinosaur skeletons and immersive exhibits that fascinate children of all ages, with budget-friendly ticket prices and online reservation options to avoid peak season queues.

raw_name: 滨江大道（陆家嘴滨水区）
surface_name: 滨江大道（陆家嘴滨水区）
reason: Recommended Outdoor & Leisure landmark (滨江大道（陆家嘴滨水区）): This free scenic riverside walkway along the Pudong waterfront offers beautiful views, open spaces for children to run and play, and is easily accessible by metro, making it an ideal zero-cost family outing during peak travel season.

Recommended Zoo landmark (Ueno Zoo): At roughly 600 yen for adults and free for elementary-age children, it is the cheapest big-animal day out in Tokyo, and its giant pandas and petting corner keep kids engaged for hours if you arrive at the 9:30 opening before peak-season queues build.

raw_name: National Museum of Nature and Science, Ueno
surface_name: National Museum of Nature and Science, Ueno
reason: Recommended Museum landmark (National Museum of Nature and Science, Ueno): Its 630-yen adult ticket with free entry for young children buys a dinosaur hall and hands-on science floors that are fully indoors, making it a reliable air-conditioned refuge when peak-season heat or rain hits, and it sits a two-minute walk from Ueno Zoo for a single-transport-cost double day.

Recommended Temple landmark (Senso-ji Temple, Asakusa): Entry is free, the Nakamise arcade lets you feed the family on 100-300 yen snacks instead of a restaurant bill, and the grounds are flat and stroller-friendly, so go at 7-8am in peak season to photograph the pagoda before the crowds arrive.

Recommended Shrine landmark (Meiji Jingu and Yoyogi Park): Both cost nothing, the forested shrine approach is shaded and quiet enough for small legs, and adjacent Yoyogi Park gives children open space to run after the shrine visit, which makes it the best zero-cost half-day for a budget family in the hot months.

Recommended Observation landmark (Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observatories): Free entry to the 45th-floor observatory gives the same skyline and, on clear days, Mt. Fuji views that cost 3,000+ yen at the Skytree, freeing that money for meals, and the indoor queue-and-elevator format is easy with children in peak-season heat.

Recommended Museum landmark (Fukagawa Edo Museum): For a token 400-yen adult admission, children can walk through a full-scale reconstructed Edo-period neighborhood, climb into merchant houses and handle props, which delivers a history lesson they actually enjoy at a fraction of theme-park pricing.

Recommended Park landmark (Kasai Rinkai Park): Park entry is free, it has one of Tokyo's largest free playgrounds plus a bird sanctuary and seaside lawn, and you can add the modestly priced aquarium only if the budget allows, making it a flexible low-cost full day near the bay.

raw_name: Inokashira Park and Inokashira Park Zoo
surface_name: Inokashira Park and Inokashira Park Zoo
reason: Recommended Zoo landmark (Inokashira Park and Inokashira Park Zoo): The zoo costs only a few hundred yen, the park is free, and pedal or swan boats on the pond are a cheap treat that suits a family with children, with plenty of shade and a relaxed Kichijoji food street nearby for budget lunches.

Recommended Garden landmark (Imperial Palace East Gardens): Admission is free and the wide gravel paths, lawns and moat views give children room to move without any spend, though in peak season you should queue at the earliest opening slot since daily visitor numbers are capped.

Recommended Museum landmark (Tokyo Water Science Museum, Koto): Free admission and interactive water experiments make it an ideal indoor break during peak-season heat, and its location near Kasai Rinkai Park allows you to combine a no-cost morning with a free-play afternoon on a single train fare.

Recommended beach landmark (Bogatell and Nova Icària beaches): Free all day, with lifeguards, shallow entry and a playground right on Nova Icària, so kids can swim and burn energy without spending a euro, and the promenade showers and shade make peak-season afternoons manageable.

Recommended park landmark (Parc de la Ciutadella): A free, fenced green space with several playgrounds, a rowing lake, the famous mammoth statue and plenty of tree shade, which makes it the ideal low-cost base camp for a full family morning in the July-August heat.

Recommended park landmark (Park Güell): The surrounding free pine-shaded paths and gingerbread pavilions satisfy kids' curiosity at zero cost, while a single early-morning timed ticket for the monument zone is cheap enough for adults and free for the youngest, and going at opening avoids both the heat and the peak-season sell-out crowds.

Recommended viewpoint landmark (Bunkers del Carmel): A free 360-degree hilltop terrace where families can bring a picnic and let children run on the open plain while watching the sunset, costing nothing and timed naturally for the cooler evening hours of high season.

Recommended market landmark (La Boqueria market): Free to wander and full of cheap fruit cups, fresh juice and nut stalls that keep children entertained and fed for a couple of euros, with an early-morning visit beating the midday crush and letting you picnic back at the beach.

Recommended museum landmark (CosmoCaixa science museum): Low-cost entry with discounted family and child rates buys hours of hands-on experiments, a flooded Amazon rainforest and a planetarium, all fully air-conditioned, making it a lifesaver when peak-season temperatures peak at midday.

Recommended fortress landmark (Castell de Montjuïc): Very cheap entry with free access on Sunday afternoons, and its grassy moats, ramparts and cannons give kids room to explore and picnic while parents enjoy the harbour views.

Recommended garden landmark (Parc del Laberint d'Horta): Free on Wednesdays and Sundays and only a few euros otherwise, this shaded neoclassical garden with its hedge maze and canals turns a cheap outing into a game for children and a cool retreat from the summer sun.

raw_name: Sagrada Família exterior and Plaça de Gaudí playground
surface_name: Sagrada Família exterior and Plaça de Gaudí playground
reason: Recommended architecture landmark (Sagrada Família exterior and Plaça de Gaudí playground): You can admire Gaudí's masterpiece from outside for free while the children play in the pond-side playground opposite, delivering the city's iconic sight on a low budget and without committing to pricey timed interior tickets in high season.

Recommended museum landmark (Museu Marítim de Barcelona): Free on Sunday afternoons and inexpensive at other times, its full-size royal galley that children can climb aboard plus air-conditioned halls make it a smart, low-cost escape from peak-season crowds in the old harbour.
Recommended imperial palace landmark (故宫博物院 Palace Museum): 旺季门票仅60元且未成年子女免票或半价，中轴线全程步行无台阶障碍；孩子可边逛边数屋脊兽，建议赶在8:00开门首批入场以避开暑期人流高峰。
Recommended imperial ritual park landmark (天坛公园 Temple of Heaven): 联票旺季34元、公园大门票15元，孩子跑跳空间大；清晨入园还能看到北京大爷打太极、抖空竹，是零成本的本地生活体验，早去也能躲开中午最晒最挤的时段。
Recommended imperial garden landmark (颐和园 Summer Palace): 旺季联票60元、单门票30元，昆明湖长廊可坐可走、树荫多，孩子在长廊彩画里找故事、在石舫边看船，一天下来花费很低还不会累。
Recommended zoological park landmark (北京动物园 Beijing Zoo): 门票仅15元、熊猫馆另加5元，是全国性价比最高的亲子半日行程；无行动限制可慢慢逛完所有展区，建议开园即入直奔熊猫馆，避开上午十点后的旅行团人潮。

raw_name: 中国科学技术馆（China Science and Technology Museum）
surface_name: 中国科学技术馆（China Science and Technology Museum）
reason: Recommended interactive science museum landmark (中国科学技术馆 China Science and Technology Museum): 主展厅学生票20元、儿童科学乐园30元，几乎全部展项可动手操作，是高温或雷雨天的室内避暑首选，需提前几天在官网抢票，旺季当天基本约不到。

raw_name: 北京自然博物馆（Beijing Museum of Natural History）
surface_name: 北京自然博物馆（Beijing Museum of Natural History）
reason: Recommended natural history museum landmark (北京自然博物馆 Beijing Museum of Natural History): 免费预约入场，恐龙骨架和古生物展厅对孩子吸引力极强，位于天坛西门旁可与天坛同日串联，零门票支出又能在正午最热时待在空调馆内。
Recommended hilltop park landmark (景山公园 Jingshan Park): 门票仅2元，从故宫神武门出来过条街就到，登万春亭十几分钟即可俯瞰整座紫禁城，是给孩子留下"全景记忆"的最便宜方式，体力要求低但视野回报极高。
Recommended imperial lake garden landmark (北海公园 Beihai Park): 旺季门票10元，白塔、九龙壁、仿膳小吃都在步行范围内；租一条脚踏船几十元就能让孩子在水上消磨两小时，比任何付费乐园都划算，还能顺路衔接着什刹海。
Recommended world heritage fortification landmark (八达岭长城 Badaling Great Wall): 门票旺季40元、学生半价，从北京北站坐市郊铁路S2线直达，全程交通费不到二十元，是低预算家庭最省钱的登城路线；无行动限制可选择北线，务必赶最早一班车以避开旺季午后的拥堵。

raw_name: 什刹海—烟袋斜街胡同区（Shichahai Hutongs）
surface_name: 什刹海—烟袋斜街胡同区（Shichahai Hutongs）
reason: Recommended historic hutong district landmark (什刹海—烟袋斜街胡同区 Shichahai Hutongs): 完全免费，沿湖步行可看摇橹船、逛胡同小店、吃几块钱一串的糖葫芦；傍晚来最凉快也最有生活气，孩子能在老北京街巷里自由走动，无需任何门票预算。

Recommended Temple landmark (Wat Phra That Doi Suthep): the 30-baht hilltop temple is the city's signature sight, reached by a cheap shared songthaew instead of a private tour, and its cool, clear peak-season mornings make the 300-step naga staircase an easy, exciting climb for children with no mobility limits.

raw_name: Buak Haad Public Park (Nong Buak Haad)
surface_name: Buak Haad Public Park (Nong Buak Haad)
reason: Recommended Park landmark (Buak Haad Public Park): a free, flat, shaded park inside the old city walls with a playground, ducks and open lawn where kids can burn energy between temple visits, and its central location means zero transport cost in the peak season's pleasant daytime temperatures.

Recommended Temple landmark (Wat Chedi Luang): for roughly 50 baht a family can stand beside a vast collapsed 15th-century chedi right in the old town, giving children a genuine sense of scale and history in under an hour, which suits a tight budget and short attention spans.

Recommended Market landmark (Sunday Walking Street): a free-to-browse evening market where 20-40 baht street snacks and handcraft stalls let a low-budget family eat dinner and souvenir-shop in one walk, and the peak-season dry, cool evenings make strolling with children genuinely comfortable.

Recommended Nature landmark (Huay Tueng Thao Lake): a small entry fee buys a lakeside morning of bamboo huts, fish feeding, swimming and grassy space for running, making it the cheapest full half-day outdoors outing that children actually remember, and peak-season weather keeps the water and shade inviting.

raw_name: Wat Pha Lat and the Monk's Trail
surface_name: Wat Pha Lat and the Monk's Trail
reason: Recommended Nature walk landmark (Wat Pha Lat): this free forest temple reached by a short, gentle jungle trail is the best no-cost adventure for a family with no mobility restrictions, and the cool, dry peak season is precisely when the path is mud-free and the waterfall photogenic.

Recommended Wildlife park landmark (Chiang Mai Zoo): a single modest ticket (about 150 baht adult, 70 baht child) covers a whole hillside day of animals, an aquarium and a kids' zone, which is solid value for a low-budget family, and the cooler peak-season months mean you can walk the sloping paths without heat exhaustion.

Recommended Arts village landmark (Baan Kang Wat): free entry to a cluster of craft studios, a small library and garden cafes where children can try cheap hands-on workshops while parents buy nothing, and its leafy, low-key atmosphere is ideal in the busy peak season when the old city is crowded.

Recommended Market landmark (Warorot Market): the city's local food market is free to wander and is where a low-budget family buys fruit, sai ua sausage and snacks at the cheapest prices in town, giving children a loud, colourful, genuinely Thai slice of daily life rather than a tourist set-piece.

raw_name: Chiang Mai University Ang Kaew Reservoir
surface_name: Chiang Mai University Ang Kaew Reservoir
reason: Recommended Campus park landmark (Ang Kaew Reservoir): this free reservoir-side green space on the CMU campus is a favourite sunset picnic and cycling spot for local families, and its flat, traffic-free paths make an easy, no-cost late-afternoon outing during the peak season's dry, golden evenings.

raw_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
surface_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
reason: Recommended 亲子景点 landmark (成都大熊猫繁育研究基地): 门票约55元且儿童票半价，是孩子最期待的一站；旺季建议7:30前入园，既避开人流和排队，也能赶上熊猫最活跃的早晨。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (人民公园): 完全免费，有茶座、儿童游乐设施和开阔空地，旺季午后带孩子到树荫下喝茶，坐下来歇脚花费也很低。
Recommended 历史博物馆 landmark (成都博物馆): 免费预约入场，空调展馆正好避开旺季正午高温，儿童互动展区和皮影木偶类展项对孩子很有吸引力。
Recommended 科技馆 landmark (四川科技馆): 免费（需提前网上预约），可亲手操作的展项多，孩子能玩上半天，完全不受高温或下雨影响。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (锦里古街): 不进武侯祠、只逛古街不收门票，傍晚灯笼亮起后小吃和糖画、面人花费都可控，孩子边走边吃最开心。
Recommended 动物园 landmark (成都动物园): 门票仅约20元、儿童半价，动物种类多、园路平整好推车，是比熊猫基地更省时省钱的半日亲子方案。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (宽窄巷子): 免费开放，孩子可以看三大炮现做、尝钵钵鸡等小吃，住附近的家庭一早去最能避开旺季人潮。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (浣花溪公园): 免费的大公园，树荫多、有草坡和湖边可跑动，紧挨杜甫草堂，一次出行可以省下额外打车钱。
Recommended 综合博物馆 landmark (四川博物院): 免费参观、室内凉快，有面向儿童的讲解和手作活动，是旺季高温或下雨天最稳妥的备用行程。
Recommended 园林公园 landmark (望江楼公园): 门票约20元，成片竹林是市区里最凉快的地方之一，游客密度低，适合带着孩子慢慢走、不赶行程。
Recommended ancient-town landmark (大理古城)：这里免门票，街巷平缓、行走轻松，孩子可以随时停下来歇脚或买点小吃，建议清晨入场，避开旺季午后的人流高峰。

raw_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）
surface_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）
reason: Recommended lakeside-path landmark (洱海生态廊道才村—龙龛段)：这里免费开放，全程路面平坦，没有台阶，孩子可以租车骑行、看水鸟，旺季早点去人少，适合安排半天、不花钱的行程。
Recommended ancient-town landmark (喜洲古镇)：古镇不收门票，稻田和大青树能给孩子提供跑跳空间，现烤粑粑几块钱就能吃饱，赶在旅行团到达之前逛完最舒服。
Recommended craft-village landmark (周城)：扎染体验课的单价低，成品还能带回家当纪念，孩子亲手染一块布不容易玩腻，也是旺季正午暴晒或下雨时的室内安排。
Recommended temple-pagoda landmark (崇圣寺三塔)：一张票就能看遍大理最具代表性的地标，园内有电瓶车可以代步、减轻走路负担，出发前查清儿童按身高免票的政策，还能再省一笔。

raw_name: 苍山感通索道—清碧溪步道
surface_name: 苍山感通索道—清碧溪步道
reason: Recommended mountain landmark (苍山感通索道—清碧溪步道)：这条索道比洗马潭那条便宜不少，沿溪步道短而有趣，一家人没有行动限制，半小时左右就能走到水边玩水。
Recommended spring landmark (蝴蝶泉)：门票便宜，园区小、树荫多，孩子看蝴蝶标本和泉水不会太累，旺季下午旅行团散去后体验更好。
Recommended lakeside-village landmark (双廊古镇与小普陀)：沿湖散步不收费，冬季还能坐船看海鸥，孩子会很喜欢，建议早班车进镇或住一晚，以避开旺季进出镇的高峰。
Recommended historic-town landmark (巍山古城)：这里免费开放，游客密度远低于大理古城，一碗耙肉饵丝几块钱，适合在旺季安排一次避开人流的一日游。
Recommended city-park landmark (洱海公园)：免费入园，有儿童游乐设施和开阔草坪，是等车途中或傍晚消磨时间的低成本去处，孩子也能自由活动，不会觉得无聊。

Recommended urban park landmark (Parque da Cidade): Porto's biggest green space is completely free and gives kids room to run while offering tree shade and ponds that make a peak-season afternoon bearable for a low-budget family.

Recommended garden landmark (Jardins do Palácio de Cristal): free entry, roaming peacocks, playgrounds and Douro viewpoints make this the cheapest way to combine a picnic, a playground stop and sightseeing in one outing.

Recommended beach landmark (Praia de Matosinhos): an Atlantic beach reachable on a cheap metro ride where children can paddle and dig sand all day without spending anything beyond sunscreen and an ice cream.

Recommended bridge landmark (Ponte Dom Luís I): walking the upper deck is free, thrilling for children, and best done early in the morning during peak season before the crowds and midday heat build up.

Recommended historic district landmark (Ribeira): a free riverside promenade where street performers, boats and open space keep kids entertained, with cheap snack stalls instead of sit-down restaurant prices.

Recommended heritage railway station landmark (Estação de São Bento): free to enter, its enormous azulejo tile panels work as a five-minute treasure hunt for children and it doubles as a cool, shaded break from peak-season heat.

Recommended viewpoint park landmark (Jardim do Morro): free grass terraces above the Douro let a family watch the sunset and river traffic with a supermarket picnic, and they sit right at the metro exit with no climbing required.

Recommended transport museum landmark (Museu do Carro Elétrico): a small, inexpensive tram museum beside the river where children can climb aboard vintage cars, an easy indoor option when peak-season afternoons get too hot.

Recommended market landmark (Mercado do Bolhão): free to wander, its stalls of fruit, cheese and pastries let a low-budget family assemble a cheap lunch while children enjoy the noise, colour and vendors' samples.

Recommended heritage tram ride landmark (Historic tram Line 1 to Foz): a single low-cost ticket buys a rattling seafront ride along the Douro to the Foz beaches, which children treat as the day's main attraction rather than transport.

Recommended garden landmark (Jardin du Luxembourg): Its free playgrounds, Guignol puppet theatre and pony rides keep children happily occupied for hours, and the shaded chairs and basin toy boats give low-budget parents a genuinely cheap half-day in the peak-season heat.

raw_name: Jardin des Plantes and the Grande Galerie de l'Évolution
surface_name: Jardin des Plantes and the Grande Galerie de l'Évolution
reason: Recommended museum landmark (Jardin des Plantes and the Grande Galerie de l'Évolution): The gardens, menagerie and maze are free and the whale-and-elephant parade of the evolution gallery is a modestly priced, air-conditioned rain-or-heat escape that children find mesmerizing.

raw_name: Champ de Mars and the Eiffel Tower
surface_name: Champ de Mars and the Eiffel Tower
reason: Recommended landmark landmark (Champ de Mars and the Eiffel Tower): You get the full icon moment, a huge lawn to run on and the evening sparkle for nothing, making a supermarket picnic here the single best-value family evening in a peak-season Paris.

Recommended park landmark (Parc des Buttes-Chaumont): Its cliffs, grotto, waterfall and suspension bridges feel like an adventure trail for kids, with free entry and enough space to escape the August crowds that pack the central gardens.

raw_name: Notre-Dame Cathedral and Île de la Cité
surface_name: Notre-Dame Cathedral and Île de la Cité
reason: Recommended landmark landmark (Notre-Dame Cathedral and Île de la Cité): Entry to the cathedral is free, the surrounding island walk past the flower market and riverbank is free too, and arriving at opening time keeps a family with children ahead of the peak-season queues.

Recommended museum landmark (Musée Carnavalet): The permanent collection tracing Paris's history is free, indoor and full of models, signs and objects that read like a storybook to children, which makes it the ideal low-budget break on a hot or rainy afternoon.

Recommended landmark landmark (Montmartre and the Sacré-Cœur): The stair-streets, street artists at Place du Tertre and the free steps-and-view over the city turn a simple walk into a treasure hunt that costs nothing beyond the optional funicular fare.

Recommended market landmark (Marché d'Aligre): Cheap fruit, cheese and bread straight from the stalls let a family assemble lunch for a few euros, and the bustle, colours and street musicians are entertainment in themselves for children.

raw_name: Canal Saint-Martin and Bassin de la Villette
surface_name: Canal Saint-Martin and Bassin de la Villette
reason: Recommended walk landmark (Canal Saint-Martin and Bassin de la Villette): Free locks, footbridges and waterside paths plus a summer swimming basin and pedal-boat hire give kids space to roam and splash without an entry ticket.

Recommended park landmark (Parc de la Villette): Themed free playgrounds, the dragon slide, the Géode exterior and wide lawns make it a full free day out, and its size absorbs peak-season crowds far better than the small central squares.

Recommended Historical & Cultural landmark (开元寺): This iconic free-to-enter ancient temple with twin pagodas offers an awe-inspiring yet budget-friendly cultural experience that children and families can enjoy together during peak season.

Recommended Street & Shopping landmark (西街): This lively historic pedestrian street is packed with affordable local snacks and souvenirs, making it a fun and low-cost outing perfect for families with children during the busy travel season.

Recommended Nature & Scenic landmark (清源山风景区): With accessible hiking trails, the famous giant Song-dynasty Laozi statue, and beautiful greenery, this scenic area provides an exciting and affordable outdoor adventure for the whole family.

raw_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
surface_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
reason: Recommended Museum landmark (泉州海外交通史博物馆): This free museum vividly showcases Quanzhou's Maritime Silk Road heritage with ship models and artifacts that spark children's curiosity without straining a low budget.

Recommended Historical & Cultural landmark (崇武古城): This well-preserved Ming-dynasty coastal fortress combined with seaside scenery offers a unique and affordable family day trip with plenty of open space for children to explore.

Recommended Historical & Cultural landmark (泉州府文庙): This beautifully maintained Confucian temple complex has a very low entrance fee and provides a peaceful, educational environment where families can learn about traditional Chinese culture together.

Recommended Heritage & Religious landmark (晋江草庵摩尼教遗址): As a rare and fascinating Manichean relic site with minimal entry cost, it offers families with children a unique UNESCO-linked heritage experience that stands out during peak travel season.

Recommended Cultural Performance landmark (泉州木偶剧院): Affordable traditional puppet shows are highly entertaining for children and provide an authentic taste of Quanzhou's intangible cultural heritage that the whole family can enjoy.

Recommended Folk Culture landmark (惠安女民俗文化村): This village showcasing the distinctive Hui'an women's costumes and customs is a low-cost, visually engaging cultural stop that broadens children's horizons in an interactive way.

Recommended Beach & Nature landmark (石狮黄金海岸): This accessible sandy beach near Quanzhou is free to visit and offers children a joyful seaside playtime, making it an ideal budget-friendly family outing during the peak summer travel season.

raw_name: 外滩滨江步道（含黄浦江轮渡金陵东路—东昌路航线）
surface_name: 外滩滨江步道（含黄浦江轮渡金陵东路—东昌路航线）
reason: Recommended 免费城市江景地标 landmark (外滩滨江步道（含黄浦江轮渡金陵东路—东昌路航线）): 全程免费、轮渡单程仅2元，孩子可以上船看大船，全程平坦好推车，无行动障碍的一家人傍晚步行最省力也最省钱。

raw_name: 上海博物馆（人民广场馆）
surface_name: 上海博物馆（人民广场馆）
reason: Recommended 免费公共博物馆 landmark (上海博物馆（人民广场馆）): 常设展免费、空调充足，旺季午后高温或下雨时是最省钱的亲子避暑点，青铜与陶瓷展厅对孩子也足够新奇。

raw_name: 上海自然博物馆（静安雕塑公园）
surface_name: 上海自然博物馆（静安雕塑公园）
reason: Recommended 低价自然科普馆 landmark (上海自然博物馆（静安雕塑公园）): 门票几十元就能看巨型恐龙骨架和马门溪龙，是全室内行程，适合旺季避开暴晒，馆外雕塑公园还能免费放电。
Recommended 低价互动科技馆 landmark (上海科技馆): 票价低、可玩半天以上，儿童科学乐园能动手操作，全室内空调环境正适合旺季人流高峰时提前网约入场。
Recommended 低价大型城市公园 landmark (世纪公园): 门票仅约10元，大草坪、湖边步道平坦开阔，孩子可以跑跳野餐，预算极低又能待一整天，无行动障碍者绕湖步行毫无压力。
Recommended 低价亲子动物园 landmark (上海动物园): 门票约40元且儿童有优惠，看熊猫、大象的性价比远高于商业乐园，园区树荫多、道路平坦，适合旺季早上开园就进。

raw_name: 南京路步行街—人民公园（含人民广场）
surface_name: 南京路步行街—人民公园（含人民广场）
reason: Recommended 免费逛街城市空间 landmark (南京路步行街—人民公园（含人民广场）): 不花门票钱就能逛街看景、进公园喂鸽子，累了随时钻商场吹空调，对带娃低预算家庭是最灵活的免费中转站。

raw_name: 豫园商城与城隍庙老街（不进收费园林）
surface_name: 豫园商城与城隍庙老街（不进收费园林）
reason: Recommended 免费老街美食区 landmark (豫园商城与城隍庙老街（不进收费园林）): 只逛老街不买豫园门票也能看九曲桥和明清建筑，小吃按份买花费可控，孩子有得吃有得看，旺季建议一早就去避开人潮。
Recommended 免费近郊古镇 landmark (七宝老街): 地铁直达、无需门票，一条街就能吃到汤圆、海棠糕等便宜小吃，比远郊水乡省时省钱，带娃半日往返不折腾。

surface_name: 上海图书馆东馆（少儿馆）
