reason: Recommended 免费室内亲子阅读空间 landmark (上海图书馆东馆（少儿馆）): 完全免费且空调充足，少儿馆有绘本与亲子共读区，是旺季高温天或午后雷雨时的零成本备用方案，电梯与无障碍通道齐全。

Recommended Zoo landmark (Ueno Zoo & Ueno Park): entry is only a few hundred yen with elementary-age children free, and the adjoining park gives a low-cost, stroller-friendly full day that starts early to dodge peak-season crowds.

raw_name: National Museum of Nature and Science
surface_name: National Museum of Nature and Science
reason: Recommended Science Museum landmark (National Museum of Nature and Science): high-school-age entry is under a few hundred yen and younger children go free, making it the best-value air-conditioned refuge when peak-season heat and rain hit Ueno.

raw_name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observation Deck
surface_name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observation Deck
reason: Recommended Observation Deck landmark (Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observation Deck): the panorama costs nothing at all, so a family on a tight budget gets the skyline view without paying Skytree prices, and a weekday-morning slot keeps the queue short in peak season.

Recommended Temple landmark (Senso-ji & Nakamise-dori): admission is free and the approach street lets kids graze on cheap snacks and souvenirs, while an early-morning visit beats the crushing midday peak-season crowds.
Recommended Shrine landmark (Meiji Jingu & Yoyogi Park): both are free, the forested approach is shaded and flat for young legs, and the open lawns give children room to run after the shrine visit.

Recommended Garden landmark (Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden): adult tickets are around 500 yen with children free, and its lawns and ponds make an affordable half-day picnic spot with plenty of shade during the hottest peak-season weeks.

Recommended Waterfront landmark (Odaiba Seaside Park): the beach, promenade and Rainbow Bridge views are entirely free, and paddling plus the adjacent free play areas keep kids busy without a single paid ticket.

Recommended Market landmark (Ameyoko Shopping Street): street-stall pricing means a family can eat and snack for very little, and the covered arcade shelters everyone from peak-season sun or sudden rain.

Recommended Park landmark (Inokashira Park & Inokashira Park Zoo): the park is free and the small zoo charges only a few hundred yen with children free, offering a relaxed, low-cost alternative to the crowded headline sights.

Recommended Museum landmark (Tokyo Fire Museum): admission is free, the retired fire engines and helicopters are a hit with children, and it doubles as a cool indoor bolthole on a sweltering peak-season afternoon.

Recommended Basilica landmark (Basílica de la Sagrada Família): the whole visit is step-free with lifts to the nave and tower levels, children under 11 get in free, and booking the first morning slot in peak season keeps a pushchair or wheelchair visit cool and uncrowded.

Recommended Urban park landmark (Parc de la Ciutadella): it is free, the paths are wide and level, and shaded lawns plus an accessible playground and toilets make it the simplest low-cost escape from peak-season heat with a child.

Recommended Aquarium landmark (L'Aquàrium de Barcelona): it is step-free throughout with lifts between floors and air-conditioned galleries, giving a wheelchair-using child a full afternoon out of the summer sun for a modest ticket.

Recommended Fountain show landmark (Font Màgica de Montjuïc): the evening shows cost nothing and are watched from a flat paved esplanade with reserved wheelchair space, an easy end to a hot peak-season day.

Recommended Science museum landmark (CosmoCaixa): it is fully step-free with lifts and an accessible tactile route, and its hands-on exhibits plus air conditioning suit a child perfectly on a crowded summer afternoon.

Recommended Maritime museum landmark (Museu Marítim de Barcelona): the Royal Shipyards halls are flat and lift-served, entry is free on Sunday afternoons, and there is ample room for a wheelchair-using child to move around freely.

Recommended Cable car landmark (Telefèric de Montjuïc): cabins are boarded from a level platform with staff assistance and take wheelchairs, offering a cheap short ride and big views instead of a hilly climb.

Recommended Beach landmark (Platja de la Nova Icària): wooden access walkways, an accessible shower and amphibious beach chairs get a wheelchair-using child to the water for free, and it is noticeably calmer than Barceloneta in peak season.

raw_name: Rambla de Mar i Port Vell
surface_name: Rambla de Mar i Port Vell
reason: Recommended Waterfront promenade landmark (Rambla de Mar i Port Vell): level boardwalks, ramps and lifts run the length of the marina, making a free breezy evening stroll easy while giving room to sidestep peak-season crowds.

Recommended Art museum landmark (Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya): step-free entrances and lifts reach every floor, admission is free on Sunday afternoons, and family activities keep a child engaged without stretching a low budget.
Recommended national museum landmark (中国国家博物馆): 免费预约入场，全程无障碍电梯与轮椅通道，室内恒温可避开旺季高温与人流暴晒，孩子也能在青铜器、瓷器展厅里看得懂、待得住。
Recommended city history museum landmark (首都博物馆): 免费、人少、冷气足，轮椅可直达各层展厅，老少皆宜的民俗与老北京展陈适合亲子慢逛，是旺季午间最好的避暑落脚点。
Recommended imperial temple park landmark (天坛公园): 门票仅十几元、1.2米以下儿童免票，东西南北门内都是平坦柏油与石板大道，轮椅和婴儿车可一路推到祈年殿，园内古柏成荫适合旺季清早出行。
Recommended imperial garden landmark (颐和园): 新建宫门至东宫门沿昆明湖一线地势平坦、无台阶，可全程轮椅通行，旺季票价亲民且湖边树荫多，坐船看景对孩子也省脚力。
Recommended zoo landmark (北京动物园): 门票十五元、儿童半价，主环路平整无台阶、熊猫馆与海洋馆均有坡道，是低预算亲子行程里性价比最高的一站，建议开园即入避开旺客人潮。
Recommended science museum landmark (中国科学技术馆): 门票三十元、儿童馆另设低价票，全馆无障碍电梯与轮椅租借齐备，儿童科学乐园可玩上半天，室内场馆在旺季高温暴雨天都是稳妥备选。
Recommended urban forest park landmark (奥林匹克森林公园): 免费开放，主园路宽阔平坦、坡度极缓，轮椅与推车通行毫无压力，空间大人流分散，孩子可以跑跳而家长不必在旺季人堆里挤。
Recommended classical lakeside park landmark (北海公园): 门票十元、儿童免票，环湖一圈为平整步道且多处缓坡，可推轮椅直达白塔脚下，划船与喂鱼是小朋友的最爱，傍晚时段人少凉快。
Recommended imperial palace heritage site landmark (故宫博物院): 未成年人免票、成人旺季六十元，官方设有绕开门槛与台阶的无障碍参观路线并可免费借用轮椅，建议提前预约并走午门—太和殿中轴缓坡段，避开正午高峰。

surface_name: Odaiba Seaside Park and Statue of Liberty Viewpoint
reason: Recommended waterfront promenade landmark (Odaiba Seaside Park and Statue of Liberty Viewpoint): the whole seafront walk is a flat, kerb-free boardwalk with lifts at every station and mall, it is free to stroll, and the beach, rainbow bridge views and nearby air-conditioned malls give children space to run while keeping a wheelchair route simple.

Recommended park landmark (Parc de la Ciutadella): Its wide, level tarmac paths, ramped entrances, accessible toilets and free entry make it the easiest full morning or afternoon out for a pushchair or wheelchair, with a playground, a shallow boating lake and deep shade for the hottest peak-season hours.

raw_name: Platja de la Nova Icària and the Passeig Marítim
surface_name: Platja de la Nova Icària and the Passeig Marítim
reason: Recommended beach landmark (Platja de la Nova Icària and the Passeig Marítim): The seafront promenade is completely flat and paved for kilometres, this beach has wooden boardwalks running to the water's edge plus amphibious beach chairs and adapted showers in summer, and it costs nothing for a family on a budget.

Recommended museum landmark (Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya (MNAC)): Entry is free on Saturday afternoons and the first Sunday of the month, the whole building is served by lifts and step-free routes, and its cool halls with family activity sheets are a reliable escape from peak-season heat and crowds.

Recommended museum landmark (Museu Marítim de Barcelona): Free on Sunday afternoons, fully step-free with lifts between its vast former shipyard halls, and a hit with children thanks to the full-size replica galley they can walk around, all at the foot of La Rambla.

surface_name: Font Màgica de Montjuïc evening show

raw_name: La Boqueria market and La Rambla
surface_name: La Boqueria market and La Rambla
reason: Recommended market landmark (La Boqueria market and La Rambla): Both are broad, flat and free to wander, with level entry into the market's central aisle, and an early-morning visit keeps the pushchair-friendly space before the peak-season crowds build.

Recommended museum landmark (CosmoCaixa science museum): A low ticket price relative to big-ticket Barcelona sights, complete step-free access throughout, and a hands-on Clik area plus a flooded Amazonian forest that keep children absorbed for hours indoors away from the July and August sun.

Recommended museum landmark (Museu Picasso): Free on Thursday afternoons and the first Sunday of the month, with lifts and level access between its five medieval palaces, making a short, cheap, culturally rich stop that suits young attention spans.

raw_name: Port Vell and the Rambla de Mar
surface_name: Port Vell and the Rambla de Mar
reason: Recommended waterfront landmark (Port Vell and the Rambla de Mar): Free wooden boardwalks and level quays let you roll right along the water past the yachts and fishing boats, with benches, shade and toilets at hand for a low-cost break between other sights.

Recommended fortress landmark (Castell de Montjuïc): Free on Sunday afternoons, reached by a low-floor accessible bus, and its flat outdoor ramparts, lawns and picnic tables give children room to run while offering the best free harbour views in the city.
Recommended 科技馆 landmark (中国科学技术馆): 全馆有电梯和无障碍坡道，轮椅可以直达每一层的儿童科学乐园，票价低（儿童免费、成人约30元），在旺季也以室内活动为主，最适合亲子一起玩一整天。
Recommended 动物园 landmark (北京动物园): 园区地势平坦、主路全为硬化铺装，轮椅和婴儿车都能通行，门票旺季仅十几元，熊猫馆和大象馆对孩子吸引力极强。
Recommended 皇家祭坛 landmark (天坛公园): 东门到祈年殿为无障碍坡道和无台阶的平路，轮椅能走完主线，门票便宜、园内开阔，孩子可以跑动，旺季早点入园即可避开人流。
Recommended 皇家园林 landmark (颐和园): 从东宫门沿昆明湖东岸是官方无障碍线路，全程平缓无台阶，旺季门票约30元，坐轮椅也能轻松游览长廊和十七孔桥。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (中国国家博物馆): 免费预约、入口有无障碍通道和电梯，室内恒温又遮阳避雨，对孩子来说是旺季避暑、看青铜器和古代中国展的好去处。
Recommended 皇家园林 landmark (北海公园): 环湖主路平坦无台阶，轮椅和推车都能顺畅绕行，门票旺季仅十元，还可以坐脚踏船，孩子玩得开心、花费也很少。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (首都博物馆): 免费参观、全馆电梯加无障碍卫生间，老北京民俗展有大量实物和互动，室内空间宽敞，适合带轮椅和孩子在旺季慢慢逛半天。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (奥林匹克森林公园): 完全免费，成片的塑胶跑道和林间平路没有任何台阶，轮椅推行十分轻松，树荫多、空间开阔，是旺季带孩子躲避人群、野餐泄力的好地方。
Recommended 自然博物馆 landmark (北京自然博物馆): 门票便宜、凭预约即可，馆内有无障碍电梯可到达各展厅，恐龙化石和动物标本对孩子来说最能吸引他们，一个上午就能看完，不累。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (朝阳公园): 免门票，园内环路平整、坡道完善，推轮椅毫无压力，还有儿童游乐区和大草坪，旺季人多时也比热门景点更舒缓，适合安排在行程的最后一天。

Recommended Park landmark (Nong Buak Haad Public Park): Free to enter with level paved loop paths, shade, benches, drinking water and a playground, it is the cheapest way to give a child a proper run-around in the cool of the morning while a wheelchair rolls the entire circuit without a single kerb.

Recommended Temple landmark (Wat Chedi Luang): At roughly 50 baht a head and sitting right in the old city centre, its main courtyard is wide, level paving with generous space around the ruined chedi, so a chair or stroller moves freely while kids get the big dramatic-stupa moment that makes a temple visit stick.

Recommended Temple landmark (Wat Phra Singh Woramahawihan): A low entry fee buys a flat, fully paved compound with shaded seating and the famous Lai Kham chapel seen easily from ground level, making it the gentlest temple stop for a family managing wheels and a tired child in peak-season crowds.

raw_name: Three Kings Monument Plaza and Lanna Folklife Museum
surface_name: Three Kings Monument Plaza and Lanna Folklife Museum
reason: Recommended Museum landmark (Three Kings Monument Plaza and Lanna Folklife Museum): The monument square is free, flat and open for a snack-and-photo break, and the museum beside it charges a small admission, runs a lift to every floor and is air-conditioned, giving you a cool step-free hour when the peak-season heat or smoke closes in.

raw_name: Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Center
surface_name: Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Center
reason: Recommended Museum landmark (Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Center): Housed in the old provincial hall with lift access, ramps and air-conditioning throughout, its modest ticket price and short, child-sized exhibits make it an easy indoor fallback that never traps a wheelchair at a staircase.

Recommended Museum landmark (Chiang Mai National Museum): A level forecourt, ramped entrance and cool galleries keep the whole visit step-free for around 100 baht, and the low-key displays plus a cheap onsite cafe suit a family that needs a calm, unhurried half-day out of the sun.

Recommended Garden landmark (Royal Park Rajapruek): Everything is on flat, wide, sealed walkways with a free tram and buggy service that spares whoever is pushing, and discounted child tickets plus open lawns and shade tents make it the best-value green day out for a low-budget family in peak season.

Recommended Zoo landmark (Chiang Mai Zoo): The site is hilly, but the paid tram and buggy service drops you at each enclosure so almost no pushing uphill is required, and the modest entry fee buys a full day that reliably delights a child without needing any stairs.

raw_name: Tha Phae Gate and Sunday Walking Street
surface_name: Tha Phae Gate and Sunday Walking Street
reason: Recommended Market landmark (Tha Phae Gate and Sunday Walking Street): Completely free, the gate plaza and the broad sealed length of Ratchadamnoen Road are step-free and stroller-friendly, and arriving around 4pm before the peak-season crush lets you sample the cheap street food and let a child see the lantern-lit old city without fighting the crowds.

Recommended Indoor family hub landmark (Central Festival Chiang Mai): Free entry, lifts to every level, spacious accessible toilets, a supervised kids play zone and a cheap food court make it the practical step-free refuge for a low-budget family when peak-season heat, rain or smoke rules out the outdoors.

raw_name: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding
surface_name: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding
reason: Recommended Wildlife landmark (Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding): a once-in-a-childhood panda visit at a modest ticket price, with paved, ramp-linked walkways and shuttle buses that let a wheelchair and stroller roll between enclosures — go at opening time in peak season to beat both the heat and the crowds.

Recommended Museum landmark (Chengdu Museum): free entry with advance booking, lifts to every floor and full air-conditioning make it the ideal step-free, budget-zero refuge during the hottest, busiest midday hours, and the hands-on children's and shadow-puppet exhibits keep kids engaged for hours.

Recommended Park landmark (People's Park): a free, dead-flat paved loop where a wheelchair user can roll straight to the teahouse, the goldfish pond and the open-air dancing, giving a low-budget family a shaded, stroller-friendly half-day in the middle of the city.

Recommended Museum landmark (Sichuan Museum): no admission fee, ramps and lifts throughout, and cool indoor galleries of Bronze Age and Han artefacts that turn a sweltering peak-season afternoon into an easy, step-free cultural stop for children and wheelchair users alike.

Recommended Historic street landmark (Jinli Ancient Street): free to wander, entirely level stone paving with curb-free access from the entrance, and snack stalls and candy-figurine craft demos at pocket-money prices that delight young children while the wheelchair moves without a single step.

Recommended Historic street landmark (Kuanzhai Alley): a free, flat, wide-paved three-lane quarter where a wheelchair rolls easily, with cheap street food and shaded courtyards plus public accessible toilets — best visited early morning in peak season before the crowds thicken.

Recommended Park landmark (Huanhuaxi Park): free admission, smooth level paths along the river and broad lawns where children can run, making it a no-cost, fully step-free rest stop that pairs naturally with nearby Du Fu Thatched Cottage.

Recommended Garden landmark (Du Fu Thatched Cottage): a low-cost garden-museum with gentle, mostly level paved paths, wheelchair loan at the gate and plenty of shaded benches, so the whole family can pace a short, step-free visit around a toddler's or wheelchair user's stamina.

Recommended Temple landmark (Wenshu Monastery): free entry, flat courtyard paving with ramps at the halls, and a cheap vegetarian canteen and teahouse on site — a calm, budget-friendly, step-free break from peak-season crowds.

Recommended Zoo landmark (Chengdu Zoo): a very cheap child-friendly ticket buys a flat, fully paved loop past pandas, monkeys and a small amusement area, with accessible toilets and stroller-friendly paths that make it an easy low-budget full day for a family with limited mobility.

raw_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）
surface_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）
reason: Recommended lakeside landmark (洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）): 全线是无台阶的平坦木栈道和骑行道，轮椅与婴儿车可全程通行，免费开放且沿途有树荫与休息亭，旺季清晨出发即可避开人流。

raw_name: 大理古城（复兴路—五华楼）
surface_name: 大理古城（复兴路—五华楼）
reason: Recommended historic town landmark (大理古城（复兴路—五华楼）): 主街平整、路口多设缓坡，古城免门票，孩子可以边走边吃边看，低预算家庭住城内步行即可往返，旺季建议早晚出行避开正午拥挤。
Recommended historic town landmark (喜洲古镇): 四方街一带地势平坦、巷道短，进出古镇费用很低，稻田边有开阔平地让孩子跑动，几块钱的喜洲粑粑就能解决一顿，适合低预算亲子半日游。
Recommended temple landmark (崇圣寺三塔): 景区主游线是平整柏油路并有电瓶车接驳，轮椅可一路推到三塔脚下与倒影池，儿童有优惠票，是低预算家庭看标志性景观最省力的一段。
Recommended scenic park landmark (三塔倒影公园): 门票只有几元、园内全为平地，是拍三塔全景最省钱的机位，轮椅可绕池一周，旺季人比主景区少得多，孩子也有空间活动。
Recommended museum landmark (大理市博物馆): 免费开放且设有无障碍坡道，馆内凉爽可避雨避晒，碑刻与陶俑展品配合讲解对孩子友好，正是旺季正午带娃歇脚的好去处。

raw_name: 大理白族自治州博物馆
surface_name: 大理白族自治州博物馆
reason: Recommended museum landmark (大理白族自治州博物馆): 免费参观、新馆有电梯和宽展厅，轮椅通行顺畅，白族民俗与青铜器陈列能吸引孩子，下雨或暴晒时是零花费的室内备选。
Recommended park landmark (洱海公园): 免费入园、湖畔步道平坦无台阶，有草坪、树荫和大片休息座椅，孩子有地方玩、家长推轮椅也不费力，适合低预算家庭消磨半天。
Recommended lakeside landmark (龙龛码头): 木栈道平缓直通湖边、没有台阶，免费看日出，清晨人少光好，轮椅和婴儿车都能推到水边，是旺季避开人潮的轻松一站。
Recommended cultural site landmark (大理文庙): 院落基本处在同一平面、主要通道平缓，门票低甚至免费，空间安静开阔，孩子可在殿前空地活动，旺季也相对不拥挤。

Recommended Waterfront landmark (Cais da Ribeira riverside promenade): the lower quay level is a continuous flat, cobble-free stretch with no steps or kerbs, so a wheelchair or pushchair can roll the full length while the child watches the rabelo boats, with free public benches and shade stops that make peak-season heat manageable.

Recommended Garden landmark (Jardins do Palácio de Cristal): free entry, wide smoothly paved main paths with gentle gradients between the terraces, toilets and a playground, plus the best free Douro view in the city and enough lawn and peacock-spotting to fill a whole morning without spending anything.

Recommended Park landmark (Parque da Cidade): Porto's largest green space is essentially flat, fully paved on its main circuit, free, and equipped with accessible toilets, shaded picnic areas and several playgrounds, making it the best low-cost escape from peak-season crowds on a hot afternoon.

raw_name: Foz do Douro and Praia dos Ingleses promenade
surface_name: Foz do Douro and Praia dos Ingleses promenade
reason: Recommended Beach landmark (Foz do Douro and Praia dos Ingleses promenade): the seafront walkway runs step-free from the Castelo do Queijo to the river mouth with ramped access points and wooden beach boardwalks, so the child gets sand and Atlantic waves while the wheelchair user stays on a firm, level surface.

Recommended Market landmark (Mercado do Bolhão): the renovated 2022 building has lifts, ramps and wide aisles throughout its two levels, entry is free, and a family can graze cheaply on bifanas, fruit and pastries while the child watches the fishmongers — a compact indoor option when peak-season sun gets too much.

Recommended Viewpoint landmark (Jardim do Morro): reachable step-free via the lifts at Jardim do Morro metro station, this free grassy terrace looks straight back at Ribeira and the Dom Luís I bridge, with level paths, benches and space for the child to run while you rest in the shade.

Recommended Cable car landmark (Teleférico de Gaia cable car): cabins are boarded at platform level with staff slowing the ride for wheelchair users, giving a genuinely step-free aerial crossing of the Douro that is the single biggest thrill for a child and replaces the inaccessible historic trams and bridge walkways.

Recommended Aquarium landmark (Sea Life Porto): fully step-free with lifts and wide viewing galleries, sited beside the flat Foz coastal path, and the best rainy-day or heatwave fallback for a family — book online in advance during peak season for the cheapest timed tickets and quieter early slots.

Recommended Museum landmark (Museu Nacional Soares dos Reis): lift access to every floor, accessible toilets, and free admission on Sunday mornings, with sculpture and painting galleries compact enough for a short child-friendly visit and a courtyard café for a cheap break.

Recommended Library landmark (Biblioteca Municipal Almeida Garrett): free, fully accessible with lifts and level entrances, and set inside the Palácio de Cristal gardens, it offers air-conditioned children's reading rooms, clean accessible toilets and a quiet low-cost rest stop in the middle of a peak-season day.

Recommended garden landmark (Jardin du Luxembourg): Wide, level gravel paths and free entry make it an easy step-free base where children burn off energy at the playground and puppet theatre while parents rest in the shaded chairs.

raw_name: Jardin des Plantes & Grande Galerie de l'Évolution
surface_name: Jardin des Plantes & Grande Galerie de l'Évolution
reason: Recommended natural-history landmark (Jardin des Plantes & Grande Galerie de l'Évolution): The garden is flat and free, the evolution gallery is lift-served throughout, and the whole ensemble gives a low-cost, stroller- and wheelchair-friendly animal fix that also works on a rainy day.

Recommended art museum landmark (Musée du Louvre): Entry is free for under-18s, every wing is served by lifts, and an earliest-slot booking keeps a wheelchair clear of the peak-season crush that clogs the pyramid hall by mid-morning.

Recommended art museum landmark (Musée d'Orsay): Free for children, fully lift-served and small enough to finish before tiredness sets in, with impressionist galleries that hold a child's attention far better than endless corridors.

Recommended cathedral landmark (Notre-Dame de Paris): Free entry plus a level forecourt and accessible side entrance make this the cheapest big-name sight on the itinerary, best visited at opening time before the peak-season queues build.

raw_name: Champ de Mars & Eiffel Tower esplanade
surface_name: Champ de Mars & Eiffel Tower esplanade
reason: Recommended park landmark (Champ de Mars & Eiffel Tower esplanade): The flat lawns deliver the classic Eiffel Tower view for nothing, and viewing from ground level instead of climbing avoids the long, hot queues while still giving children the photo they came for.

Recommended garden landmark (Jardin des Tuileries): Smooth, step-free alleys link the Louvre to Concorde with no stairs, plus free playgrounds, trampolines and chairs by the ponds for a cheap mid-morning break.
Recommended fine-arts museum landmark (Petit Palais): The permanent collection is free, the building is step-free with lifts, and its compact size and garden café suit a short, unhurried family stop.

raw_name: Parc de la Villette & Cité des Sciences
surface_name: Parc de la Villette & Cité des Sciences
reason: Recommended science landmark (Parc de la Villette & Cité des Sciences): The park is free and flat with accessible paths, and the science museum's hands-on galleries and lifts provide an indoor escape when peak-season heat or rain arrives.

Recommended history museum landmark (Musée Carnavalet): Free permanent collections, full lift access and a Marais location let you pair a short, cool, step-free museum visit with a level walk through the old streets outside.

raw_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
surface_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
reason: Recommended 博物馆 landmark (泉州海外交通史博物馆): 免费开放且有电梯、无障碍卫生间和坡道,空调展厅正好躲开旺季正午的高温,馆内的宋代古船和石刻船模型对小孩极有吸引力。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (中国闽台缘博物馆): 免票入场,大厅到各层展馆全程电梯直达、地面平整,室内凉爽宽敞,推轮椅带孩子逛两小时不费力,是旺季避暑避雨的首选。
Recommended 古迹 landmark (开元寺): 门票免费,中轴线院落地面平坦、殿前有缓坡,东西塔间古榕成荫,正适合旺季带孩子慢走纳凉;建议开门即入以避开人流。
Recommended 古迹 landmark (泉州府文庙): 免费开放,泮池前广场与大成殿前庭均为平整石板地、无台阶阻隔,树荫与廊下座椅多,孩子可在开阔广场活动,轮椅通行顺畅。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (中山路骑楼老街): 全程无车的步行街、路面平整,连绵骑楼在雨季和烈日下都能遮阳挡雨,逛街不花钱,推车带娃可随时进店歇脚。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (西街): 平坦的步行老街,小吃单价低、孩子边走边尝花费很少,沿街骑楼与店面可遮阴;旺季建议清晨前往,人流少时轮椅更好通行。
Recommended 寺庙 landmark (天后宫): 免费参观,山门到正殿为平缓地面、仅少量低台阶可由侧边缓坡绕行,院内有遮蔽与座椅,适合带孩子短时游览后转往隔壁德济门遗址。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (泉州西湖公园): 免费入园,环湖主道为平整铺装的缓坡步道,树荫和休息亭密集,孩子有开阔草地可跑动,是旺季傍晚避开人潮、推轮椅散步的好去处。
Recommended 古迹 landmark (清净寺): 门票仅几元、停留时间短,门内庭院基本平坦、范围小不易走散,带小孩看异域风格石构遗迹很新鲜;入口有少量台阶,可请工作人员协助从侧门进入。

raw_name: 泉州非物质文化遗产馆
surface_name: 泉州非物质文化遗产馆
reason: Recommended 博物馆 landmark (泉州非物质文化遗产馆): 免费开放、室内有电梯与无障碍通道,空调环境适合旺季午后,木偶、南音、花灯等活态展演对孩子吸引力强且不必额外消费。

Recommended Public Park & Square landmark (People's Square): This free, fully flat open space is perfect for families with children during peak season, offering step-free access throughout and easy connections to multiple metro lines.

Recommended Iconic Waterfront landmark (The Bund): A completely flat, wide riverside promenade that is free to walk, wheelchair-friendly, and provides spectacular skyline views that delight children and adults alike.

Recommended City Park landmark (Century Park): One of Shanghai's largest parks with paved, step-free pathways throughout, low-cost entry, and wide open green spaces ideal for families with young children during peak travel season.

raw_name: Shanghai Science and Technology Museum (上海科技馆)
surface_name: Shanghai Science and Technology Museum (上海科技馆)
reason: Recommended Educational Museum landmark (Shanghai Science and Technology Museum): Fully wheelchair-accessible with elevators and ramps on every floor, offering highly interactive and affordable exhibits that captivate children of all ages.

Recommended Cultural & Shopping District landmark (Xintiandi): A pedestrian-friendly, step-free heritage district where families can stroll freely at no entry cost, enjoy street performances, and find budget-friendly food options during busy holiday periods.

Recommended City Park landmark (Zhongshan Park): A well-maintained, flat urban park with free admission, children's play areas, and smooth paved paths fully accessible for wheelchairs, conveniently located near a major metro hub.

raw_name: Shanghai Natural History Museum (上海自然博物馆)
surface_name: Shanghai Natural History Museum (上海自然博物馆)
reason: Recommended Natural History Museum landmark (Shanghai Natural History Museum): Features complete step-free access with ramps and lifts, very affordable ticket prices, and dinosaur and wildlife exhibits that are a huge hit with young children.

raw_name: Yuyuan Garden Area (豫园商城周边)
surface_name: Yuyuan Garden Area (豫园商城周边)
reason: Recommended Historic Garden & Bazaar landmark (Yuyuan Garden Area): The surrounding pedestrian bazaar is free to explore, largely flat and accessible, and filled with traditional snacks and souvenirs that make it a budget-friendly family cultural experience.

raw_name: Lujiazui Riverside Green Space (陆家嘴滨江绿地)
surface_name: Lujiazui Riverside Green Space (陆家嘴滨江绿地)
reason: Recommended Riverside Park landmark (Lujiazui Riverside Green Space): A completely free, flat, and wheelchair-accessible riverside lawn offering close-up views of the iconic Shanghai Tower skyline, ideal for a relaxed family outing during peak season.

raw_name: Shanghai Children's Museum (上海儿童博物馆)
surface_name: Shanghai Children's Museum (上海儿童博物馆)
reason: Recommended Children's Museum landmark (Shanghai Children's Museum): Designed specifically for young visitors with step-free, barrier-free access throughout, very low admission fees, and hands-on interactive exhibits perfectly tailored for families traveling with children.

Recommended zoo landmark (Ueno Zoo): Tickets are among Tokyo's cheapest at around ¥600 with children of junior-high age and younger free, and the whole loop is flat, paved and step-free with wheelchair loans at the gate — arrive at the 9:30 opening during peak season to beat the stroller-and-tour-group crush.

raw_name: National Museum of Nature and Science (Kahaku), Ueno
surface_name: National Museum of Nature and Science (Kahaku), Ueno
reason: Recommended museum landmark (National Museum of Nature and Science): At roughly ¥630 with school-age children free, it is a fully lift-serviced, air-conditioned indoor option where a child can touch dinosaur skeletons and hands-on exhibits, making it the ideal heat-or-rain fallback when peak-season queues at outdoor sights balloon.

Recommended museum landmark (Tokyo National Museum): Admission is about ¥1,000 with children free, every gallery is reached by elevator or ramped corridor, and loaner wheelchairs plus accessible toilets are on site, giving a low-cost, weather-proof half-day that suits a wheelchair user and a child equally.

Recommended garden landmark (Shinjuku Gyoen): At ¥500 with children free, its main promenades are broad, paved and step-free (unlike the gravel paths at Meiji Jingu), and entering via the Sendagaya or Okido gate on a weekday morning avoids the peak-season cherry-blossom and autumn-foliage crowds at the main Shinjuku gate.

raw_name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building South Observatory, Shinjuku
surface_name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building South Observatory, Shinjuku
reason: Recommended observatory landmark (Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building South Observatory): It is completely free, reached by direct lift from the ground-floor entrance with level floors throughout, and gives a child a genuine skyscraper-view thrill without the ¥2,000-plus Skytree ticket — go at opening time to dodge the peak-season security queue.

raw_name: Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation), Odaiba
surface_name: Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation), Odaiba
reason: Recommended museum landmark (Miraikan): Roughly ¥630 for adults with preschoolers free, it is entirely step-free with lifts to every floor, wide aisles for a wheelchair, and indoor interactive robots and displays that keep a child engaged for hours regardless of peak-season heat or rain.

raw_name: Tokyo Sea Life Park (Kasai Rinkai Suisan-en)
surface_name: Tokyo Sea Life Park (Kasai Rinkai Suisan-en)
reason: Recommended aquarium landmark (Tokyo Sea Life Park): Entry is a modest ~¥700 with younger children free, the entire route is a continuous step-free ramp around the central tank with accessible toilets, and it pairs with the free adjacent Kasai Rinkai Park for a full low-budget day away from the most congested peak-season districts.

raw_name: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa, via Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center
surface_name: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa, via Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center
reason: Recommended temple landmark (Senso-ji Temple): The temple grounds are free, flat and paved with an accessible toilet block and a step-free route around the side of the crowded Nakamise shopping street, and the nearby tourist information centre has a free lift-served observation deck — visit before 9am in peak season when the crush is manageable for a wheelchair.

raw_name: Tokyo Fire Museum (Tokyo Fire Department Museum), Yotsuya
surface_name: Tokyo Fire Museum (Tokyo Fire Department Museum), Yotsuya
reason: Recommended museum landmark (Tokyo Fire Museum): Admission is entirely free, the building is lift-served and step-free from the Yotsuya Sanchome exit, and the fire engines, helicopters and hands-on firefighter gear are exactly the kind of free indoor stop that rescues a peak-season afternoon with a child on a tight budget.

raw_name: Odaiba Seaside Park and Rainbow Promenade
surface_name: Odaiba Seaside Park and Rainbow Promenade
reason: Recommended park landmark (Odaiba Seaside Park and Rainbow Promenade): It costs nothing, the whole waterfront boardwalk and beach frontage is level, wide and step-free with accessible facilities, and the Yurikamome line to get there is fully accessible — an easy evening of sand, boats and Rainbow Bridge views that a child will remember longer than any paid attraction.

Recommended public park landmark (Parc de la Ciutadella): free entry with wide, level paved paths, accessible toilets and a shaded playground beside the fountain, so a wheelchair user and a child can spend a whole peak-season morning there without a single stair or ticket queue.

raw_name: Rambla de Mar and Port Vell waterfront
surface_name: Rambla de Mar and Port Vell waterfront
reason: Recommended waterfront promenade landmark (Rambla de Mar and Port Vell waterfront): continuous wooden boardwalks, ramps and lifts link the Columbus monument to Maremagnum, letting a wheelchair roll right to the water's edge while kids watch the boats for nothing — go before 10am to beat the peak-season crowds.

Recommended architectural landmark (Sagrada Família): pre-book a timed slot and enter via the step-free access with interior lifts serving the ground-floor route and museum, which keeps the peak-season queue manageable and avoids the stairs and tower climbs that are not wheelchair usable.

Recommended science museum landmark (CosmoCaixa): fully step-free with lifts throughout, hands-on exhibits a child can actually touch, and at roughly 8 euros per adult with under-16s free it doubles as air-conditioned shelter during the hottest peak-season afternoons.

Recommended market hall landmark (Mercat de la Boqueria): free to enter and level along the wide central aisle, with fruit pyramids and fish counters that fascinate children — arrive before 10am so the wheelchair moves freely before the peak-season crush builds.

Recommended maritime museum landmark (Museu Marítim de Barcelona): ramps and lifts cover the full route, including the full-size replica galley a child can climb aboard, and entry is free on Sunday afternoons, which keeps a low budget intact.

Recommended historic fortress landmark (Castell de Montjuïc): reachable by the wheelchair-accessible Montjuïc cable car or bus 150 and then flat along the ramparts, with free entry on Sunday afternoons and open space where a child can run off energy.

Recommended art museum landmark (Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya (MNAC)): step-free entrances and lifts reach every floor, and free entry on Saturday afternoons and the first Sunday of the month plus family activity spaces make a heatwave or rainy peak-season afternoon cheap and easy.

raw_name: Museu Blau and Parc del Fòrum
surface_name: Museu Blau and Parc del Fòrum
reason: Recommended natural science museum landmark (Museu Blau and Parc del Fòrum): fully accessible with lifts and low-cost admission, its natural-science displays hold a child's attention, and the adjoining flat Fòrum park gives free outdoor space for a picnic afterwards.

Recommended art museum landmark (Museu Picasso): lifts connect all floors on a step-free route through the medieval palaces, and free admission on the first Sunday of each month (book the free ticket online in advance) makes one of the city's best-value rainy-afternoon options for a family on a low budget.
Recommended 历史公园 landmark (天坛公园): 旺季门票仅15元、联票34元，全园主路为平整石板与无障碍坡道，轮椅可从东门或南门直达祈年殿、回音壁等核心景点，古柏林荫浓密适合带娃避暑，早间入园还能避开旅行团高峰。
Recommended 科技馆 landmark (中国科学技术馆): 成人票30元且有儿童科学乐园，全馆电梯、无障碍卫生间与坡道齐备，室内恒温空调正好躲避旺季高温，寓教于乐能让低预算家庭轻松消磨半天。
Recommended 动物园 landmark (北京动物园): 门票仅15元、儿童有优惠，园区道路平坦并设无障碍通道，熊猫馆、水禽湖等主要场馆轮椅可直达，是低预算亲子行程里性价比最高的选择，旺季建议开园即入避开人流。
Recommended 皇家园林 landmark (颐和园): 旺季门票30元，从东宫门进园沿长廊至石舫是一条全程平坦、无台阶的轮椅友好路线，昆明湖边树荫多可遮阳，只要避开万寿山台阶，带娃推车也能从容游览。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (中国国家博物馆): 免费预约参观，全馆电梯、无障碍卫生间与轮椅借用服务完善，恒温展厅是旺季高温与雷雨天的理想去处，孩子可在免费展陈中直观接触历史。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (奥林匹克森林公园): 完全免费开放，环湖主路宽阔平整、坡道连续，轮椅与婴儿车都毫无压力，大面积草坪适合孩子跑跳，且园区体量大、旺季人流相对分散。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (朝阳公园): 门票极低甚至免费，园内主路无台阶、提供轮椅租借，儿童游乐设施集中成片，适合低预算家庭安排半天轻松行程，周边餐饮也便宜方便。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (首都博物馆): 免费预约，馆内无障碍电梯、坡道与轮椅借用一应俱全，室内凉爽可作为旺季午后的避暑备选，少儿互动区内容适龄且不额外收费。
Recommended 步行商业街 landmark (前门大街): 免门票，整条街为平整石板路面、无台阶，轮椅可全程畅行，老字号小吃集中且单价亲民，孩子边走边吃很有兴致，傍晚后气温回落、人流也稍缓。
Recommended 艺术街区 landmark (798艺术区): 免费开放，主街平坦可直接推轮椅通行，夏季众多画廊可随时进室内纳凉，街头雕塑与涂鸦对孩子有天然吸引力，适合作为旺季行程的弹性补充。

Recommended botanical garden landmark (Royal Park Rajapruek): its entire grounds are flat, paved and stroller-smooth with ramps at every pavilion and a shuttle tram for tired legs, entry is only a couple of hundred baht, and the cool-season flower beds are at their best during peak months.

raw_name: Buak Hard Public Park (Nong Buak Haad)
surface_name: Buak Hard Public Park (Nong Buak Haad)
reason: Recommended public park landmark (Buak Hard Public Park): a free, fully level paved loop with shaded benches, a playground your child can run at while you push the chair alongside, and it is the easiest green breathing space in the old city during crowded high season.

raw_name: Ang Kaew Reservoir, Chiang Mai University
surface_name: Ang Kaew Reservoir, Chiang Mai University
reason: Recommended lakeside walking route landmark (Ang Kaew Reservoir): a flat, traffic-free 2 km paved path round the water that suits both a wheelchair and a scooter-free small child, costs nothing, and is coolest and quietest if you go before 8am in peak season.

Recommended zoo landmark (Chiang Mai Zoo): the hillside layout is worked around by the park tram and paved service roads so you can ride between enclosures rather than push uphill, child tickets are cheap, and the pandas and aquarium give a full half-day of low-cost entertainment.

raw_name: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center
surface_name: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center
reason: Recommended history museum landmark (Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center): a lift and level galleries make the whole exhibition wheelchair-usable, it is air-conditioned and cheap (children often free), which makes it a reliable refuge on a hot or hazy peak-season afternoon.

Recommended indoor family attraction landmark (Art in Paradise Chiang Mai): single-level, air-conditioned halls with lift access let a wheelchair roll right into the 3D photo scenes, and it is the rare Chiang Mai attraction where a young child can touch everything for an hour or two at modest cost.

Recommended art museum landmark (MAIIAM Contemporary Art Museum): ramps at the entrance, a lift to both floors and wide open galleries make it genuinely step-free, the cafe and garden give a calm break, and children's workshops run at weekends.

Recommended night market landmark (Chiang Mai Night Bazaar): the whole strip along Chang Klan Road is flat pavement with kerb cuts, so you can roll or push a stroller straight through, and cheap street food plus the free evening stage shows keep costs and a child's attention in check.

Recommended traditional market landmark (Warorot Market): the ground floor aisles are level and wide enough for a chair, everything from fruit to souvenirs is at local prices, and going early in the morning avoids both the peak-season crush and the midday heat.

Recommended Buddhist temple landmark (Wat Phra That Doi Suthep): a dedicated lift carries wheelchair users and strollers from the car park up to the upper terrace, so the iconic golden chedi is reachable without the 300 steps, though the summit plaza itself is uneven and best visited at opening time before peak-season crowds build.

raw_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
surface_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
reason: Recommended wildlife conservation base landmark (成都大熊猫繁育研究基地): 全园主路为平缓柏油与木栈道，轮椅和婴儿车可全程通行，孩子近距离看熊猫的兴趣也最高；旺季务必早上7:30开园即入，避开人流与高温，门票约55元且1.3米以下儿童免票，符合低预算。
Recommended free municipal museum landmark (成都博物馆): 免费预约入场，电梯直达各层、有无障碍卫生间与轮椅借用，皮影戏和民俗展对孩子吸引力强，是天府广场地铁站直达的空调室内点，旺季雨天或午后暴晒时的最佳避峰选择。
Recommended interactive science museum landmark (四川科技馆): 免费或低价预约制，全馆电梯与无障碍坡道完善、地面无台阶，儿童可动手体验的展项多，一次能玩半天，低预算家庭在天府广场一带可与此馆和成都博物馆连成一条零交通成本的路线。
Recommended historic public park landmark (人民公园): 完全免费，园内主干道平整宽敞、坡度极小，鹤鸣茶社可推轮椅入座，还有小型儿童游乐区，旺季人多时可分散在开阔园区内，是低预算家庭随时歇脚补给的落脚点。
Recommended classical garden museum landmark (杜甫草堂博物馆): 园区为环形平路与缓坡，主要展线无台阶、可借轮椅，园林树荫多适合推车慢走，门票约50元且儿童有优惠，建议旺季一开园就进以避开团队客流。
Recommended free riverside park landmark (浣花溪公园): 免费开放，紧邻杜甫草堂且入口无台阶，全园步道平坦宽阔、树荫与水景多，孩子可跑动、家长可推车休息，是把草堂行程延长半天而不增加预算的理想补充。
Recommended city zoo landmark (成都动物园): 门票低廉、儿童票更便宜，主游览道为平地环线、坡道替代台阶，看动物对低龄儿童性价比最高，地铁3号线直达免去换乘搬运轮椅的麻烦，旺季建议开门即入以避开正午人群。
Recommended folk culture street landmark (锦里古街): 免费进入，主街为平整石板路、轮椅可通行，小吃与手工艺摊位密集，孩子边走边吃花费可控；旺季人流极大，建议选择人流较少的上午或傍晚并从无台阶的主入口进入。
Recommended historic alley district landmark (宽窄巷子): 免费街区，三条主巷地面平整、无台阶，宽巷子一带坡道与无障碍通道较完善，孩子可看糖画、掏耳朵等民俗表演；旺季请避开午后人流高峰，并优先走宽巷子主轴线以规避院落门槛。
Recommended provincial museum landmark (四川博物院): 免费预约，入口坡道、电梯与无障碍卫生间齐全，展厅宽敞可推车通行，馆内的巴蜀青铜与民族服饰展对孩子有故事性，是浣花溪一带行程中免费且凉爽的室内备选。
Recommended historic-town landmark (大理古城): 免费开放，复兴路与人民路主街全是平坦石板路、无台阶，推婴儿车或轮椅可以一路走到底，旺季人多时也能随时拐进茶馆或客栈院子坐下休息，对低预算家庭最省心。

raw_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）
surface_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）
reason: Recommended lakeside-promenade landmark (洱海生态廊道): 全程免费的无台阶柏油慢行道，坡度极缓，可租带儿童座椅的自行车或推轮椅通行，沿途有观景平台、树荫和公厕，是孩子放风又不花门票的首选。
Recommended museum landmark (大理州博物馆): 免费参观，馆内有电梯和坡道、全程无障碍，白族服饰与民俗展对孩子有吸引力，旺季正午暴晒或下雨时可以整段躲进空调展厅，零花费又舒适。

raw_name: 崇圣寺三塔文化旅游区
surface_name: 崇圣寺三塔文化旅游区
reason: Recommended Buddhist temple landmark (崇圣寺三塔): 中轴线为缓坡与电瓶车通道，可坐景区观光车直达高处减少步行，儿童按身高免票或半票，旺季请一开门就入园避开团队人流，是拍照打卡的必看地标。
Recommended Bai-village landmark (喜洲古镇): 进镇不收门票，主街平整无台阶，大青树广场空地开阔适合孩子跑动，几块钱一个的喜洲粑粑就能解决一顿加餐，预算压力极小。
Recommended wetland-park landmark (海舌生态公园): 木栈道平坦贯通、直伸入洱海，轮椅和婴儿车都能推到底，门票很低甚至免费，视野开阔、人流比古镇主街分散，适合旺季清晨去避开拥挤。

raw_name: 周城璞真白族扎染博物馆
surface_name: 周城璞真白族扎染博物馆
reason: Recommended craft-workshop landmark (周城璞真扎染博物馆): 院落平坦、进门无台阶，参观免费或仅收很少费用，孩子可以花二三十元自己动手扎一块布，是全程最便宜也最难忘的亲子体验，还能躲太阳。
Recommended Confucian-temple landmark (大理文庙): 免费开放的平地院落，入口有坡道、院内无台阶，古树遮荫且几乎没有旅行团，是古城逛累后推车休息、让孩子安静走走的清净角落。
Recommended city-park landmark (洱海公园): 免费入园，湖畔步道宽阔平整，还有儿童游乐设施和长椅，本地人日常遛娃的地方，物价低、餐饮方便，适合作为抵达或返程当天半天的轻量安排。
Recommended lakeside-pier landmark (才村码头): 从古城过来路程短、无需门票，码头平台和岸边步道全平，可推车看日落、坐短程游船，孩子玩水看船的兴致高，旺季傍晚来比白天凉爽也不花钱。

Recommended waterfront landmark (Cais da Ribeira): a completely flat, paved riverside promenade with no steps, free to stroll, and full of shade, buskers and ice-cream stops that keep a child happy during the hot peak-season afternoons.

raw_name: Ponte Dom Luís I — lower deck walkway
surface_name: Ponte Dom Luís I — lower deck walkway
reason: Recommended bridge landmark (Ponte Dom Luís I — lower deck walkway): the lower deck is reached step-free straight from the Ribeira quay and gives a free, flat, railing-protected crossing with river views, without needing the lifts or stairs to the upper deck.

Recommended park landmark (Jardim do Morro): a free, grassy viewpoint park reached by lift from the Jardim do Morro metro station, giving a step-free picnic spot with the best postcard view of Porto and room for a child to run.

Recommended urban park landmark (Parque da Cidade): Porto's largest green space is free, level and fully paved along its main paths, with playgrounds and Atlantic breezes that make it the best low-cost escape from peak-season crowds.

Recommended market landmark (Mercado do Bolhão): the restored 2022 market is free to enter, served by lifts and level floors, and lets a family sample cheap local snacks and fruit while a wheelchair user moves easily between stalls.

Recommended seaside promenade landmark (Foz do Douro promenade): a flat, car-free Atlantic walkway with free access, benches and accessible café terraces, ideal for an early-morning or late-afternoon outing when the peak-season sun is gentler.

Recommended beach landmark (Praia de Matosinhos accessible beach): in peak season Matosinhos runs a free 'praia acessível' service with amphibious wheelchairs and boardwalk access, so a wheelchair user and a child can both reach the water without stairs or soft sand obstacles.

Recommended aquarium landmark (Sea Life Porto): fully step-free with lifts throughout, it is the most reliable indoor rainy-or-too-hot option for a child, and booking a discounted online timed ticket keeps it within a low budget.

raw_name: Museu Nacional de Soares dos Reis
surface_name: Museu Nacional de Soares dos Reis
reason: Recommended museum landmark (Museu Nacional de Soares dos Reis): a lift-served, level-floored national museum with free entry on Sunday mornings, offering shady, quiet galleries and a garden courtyard that suit both a wheelchair and short attention spans.

Recommended cultural venue landmark (Casa da Música): the metro station and building entrances are lift-served and step-free, the striking foyer is free to visit, and free or low-cost daytime concerts give a family a cool, crowd-free break in peak season.

Recommended free public garden landmark (Jardin du Luxembourg): flat, step-free gravel paths throughout with accessible toilets and a fenced playground, so a wheelchair-using parent and a child can spend a whole free morning here, and arriving before 10am in peak season keeps the shaded alleys quiet.

raw_name: Champ de Mars and the Eiffel Tower esplanade
surface_name: Champ de Mars and the Eiffel Tower esplanade
reason: Recommended iconic monument esplanade (Champ de Mars and the Eiffel Tower esplanade): the tower's lift takes wheelchairs to the second floor and the surrounding lawns are free, level and paved, giving a child the landmark moment without paying for summit tickets or climbing stairs.

raw_name: Grande Galerie de l'Évolution, Jardin des Plantes
surface_name: Grande Galerie de l'Évolution, Jardin des Plantes
reason: Recommended natural history museum (Grande Galerie de l'Évolution, Jardin des Plantes): fully lift-served and step-free with free entry for under-18s, its whale hall and dinosaur gallery are the single best rainy-or-heatwave refuge for a child, and the adjoining botanical garden is free to enter afterwards.

Recommended art museum (Musée du Louvre): every wing is reachable by lift from the step-free Pyramid entrance and admission is free for under-18s, so a short, pre-planned two-hour route to the Egyptian rooms and the Mona Lisa costs almost nothing while timed morning slots dodge the peak-season queues.

Recommended urban park landmark (Parc de la Villette): wide, level, step-free paths link free playgrounds, the dragon slide and open lawns, making it an inexpensive full-day outdoor base in the northeast where peak-season crowds are far thinner than in central Paris.

raw_name: Cité des sciences et de l'industrie
surface_name: Cité des sciences et de l'industrie
reason: Recommended science museum (Cité des sciences et de l'industrie): purpose-built for wheelchair access with lifts to every level, a dedicated children's experiment area, and reduced-price family tickets, so a hot or crowded peak-season afternoon becomes hands-on play indoors.

Recommended modern art museum (Centre Pompidou): step-free throughout via the exterior escalators and lifts, free for under-18s, and its rooftop view plus the free outdoor Place Stravinsky mechanical fountain give a child a short, low-cost, stroller- and wheelchair-friendly visit.

Recommended riverside promenade (Parc Rives de Seine): the closed-to-traffic lower quays are completely flat and step-free with ramps at every access point, offering a free shaded walk, picnic benches and boat-watching that suits a wheelchair and a restless child in the evening when peak-season heat eases.

Recommended formal garden landmark (Jardin des Tuileries): hard, level, step-free central alleys, free entry, accessible toilets and a paid trampoline-and-carousel area next to the Louvre make it an easy low-cost add-on between museum visits rather than a destination in itself.

raw_name: Bois de Vincennes and Parc Floral
surface_name: Bois de Vincennes and Parc Floral
reason: Recommended woodland park landmark (Bois de Vincennes and Parc Floral): the Parc Floral's main paths are paved and step-free with cheap entry and free under-7s, giving a child space to run and a wheelchair user reliable surfaces on the hottest peak-season days when central Paris is at its busiest.

surface_name: National Museum of Nature and Science
reason: Recommended barrier-free science museum landmark (National Museum of Nature and Science): admission is about ¥630 with under-18s free, every floor is reached by elevator and the dinosaur halls and hands-on corners give a child hours of engagement in air-conditioned comfort when the peak-season afternoon turns hottest.

Recommended accessible aquarium landmark (Tokyo Sea Life Park): tickets sit around ¥700 with free entry for younger children, the building is fully step-free with wheelchair loans at the desk, and the indoor penguin and tuna tanks make an ideal crowd-free refuge on a peak-season day.

Recommended budget transport museum landmark (Tokyo Metro Museum): admission is around ¥220 with small children free, the whole two-floor hall is lift-served and wheelchair-flat, and the train simulators and retired carriages are exactly the kind of hands-on draw that keeps a child happy inside on a peak-season afternoon.

Recommended free observation deck landmark (Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observatory): there is no admission charge at all, the route from Shinjuku Station to the 45th-floor South Observatory is lift-only and step-free, and the short indoor visit delivers a big-ticket view without the queues or ticket cost of Skytree or Shibuya Sky.

Recommended hands-on children's museum landmark (Tokyo Toy Museum): admission is around ¥800 with infants free, the converted-school building has lift access and wide doorways throughout, and the wooden-toy play rooms let a child play freely indoors during the most crowded and humid part of peak season.

Recommended free indoor museum landmark (Tokyo Fire Museum): entry costs nothing, lifts serve all floors with step-free access from the station, and the fire engines, helicopters and dress-up corner are a reliable free rainy-or-heat backup for a family already visiting the Odaiba and Koto ward sights.

Recommended park landmark (Park Güell): The free public sections and the paid Gaudí monumental zone give a child the mosaic dragon and gingerbread pavilions at a fraction of the cost of Barcelona's big-ticket sights, and off-peak queues are short enough that a family can enter on a whim.

Recommended park landmark (Parc de la Ciutadella): Entry is free, the playgrounds and the giant woolly mammoth sculpture keep a child busy for hours, and renting a rowboat on the lake costs only a few euros, making it the cheapest full afternoon on this list.

Recommended beach landmark (Bogatell and Barceloneta beaches): Barcelona's city beaches are free, flat and stroller-friendly, and in off-peak months a child gets the sand and shallow water without the summer crowds or the need to pay for a beach club.

Recommended market landmark (Mercat de la Boqueria): Wandering the stalls costs nothing, the candy, fruit-juice and jamón counters let a child try new things for pocket change, and off-peak the aisles are calm enough to let a kid actually look rather than be swept along.

reason: Recommended viewpoint landmark (Turó de la Rovira): This hilltop Civil War anti-aircraft platform is completely free, the walk up is short and easy for a child with no mobility limits, and the 360-degree view over the whole city makes a memorable low-cost picnic spot in the quieter months.

Recommended castle landmark (Castell de Montjuïc): A real hilltop fortress with moats and ramparts, free to enter on Sunday afternoons, reached by free or cheap paths through the Montjuïc gardens, so a family gets a castle day out plus a picnic for almost nothing.

Recommended garden landmark (Parc del Laberint d'Horta): Barcelona's oldest garden has a genuine hedge maze that children adore, entry costs only a couple of euros with free days each week, and off-peak it stays quiet enough for a proper game of hide-and-seek.

raw_name: Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie
surface_name: Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie
reason: Recommended science museum landmark (Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie): the Cité des Enfants hands-on zone is built for young children and costs a fraction of the big-name museums, and its indoor halls are ideal on cold, quiet off-peak days.

Recommended history museum landmark (Musée Carnavalet): the permanent collections are free for everyone, so a family on a tight budget can dip in and out, and the model shops, signs and old Paris objects give a child something concrete to look at rather than endless paintings.

Recommended cathedral landmark (Notre-Dame de Paris): entry is free, the queue moves faster outside peak season, and the scale of the interior plus the little wooden model of the building makes it a short, memorable stop that costs nothing.

raw_name: Jardin des Plantes and the Grande Galerie de l'Évolution
surface_name: Jardin des Plantes and the Grande Galerie de l'Évolution
reason: Recommended natural history museum landmark (Jardin des Plantes and the Grande Galerie de l'Évolution): the gardens and playground are free, the gallery ticket is cheap for a child, and the whale skeletons and stampeding elephant herd are the kind of indoor spectacle that carries a cold-weather day.
Recommended park landmark (Parc des Buttes-Chaumont): it is free, full of hills, grottos and bridges to run across, and 19th-arrondissement prices for lunch nearby are among the lowest in the city.

Recommended art museum landmark (Centre Pompidou): under-18s enter free, the escalator ride and rooftop view are entertainment in themselves, and the off-peak calendar keeps the family workshops cheap and uncrowded.

Recommended basilica landmark (Basilique du Sacré-Cœur): the basilica itself is free to enter, the steps and surrounding Montmartre streets are free to wander, and with no mobility limits a child can enjoy the climb and the view as the reward.

Recommended urban promenade landmark (Coulée verte René-Dumont): a free elevated garden walk above the city gives restless legs somewhere to run off energy between paid stops, and off-peak it is quiet enough for a child to lead the way.

Recommended fine arts museum landmark (Petit Palais): the permanent collection and the garden courtyard are free, the building is small enough for a child's attention span, and it makes a warm, no-cost rainy-day substitute for the Louvre.
Recommended 佛教古寺 landmark (开元寺): 免费开放且东西塔、古榕、放生池都在同一片平缓院落里，孩子可以边走边看又不必担心爬坡，淡季人少时慢慢逛一两个小时最舒服。

raw_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
surface_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
reason: Recommended 专题博物馆 landmark (泉州海外交通史博物馆): 免费入馆、室内有空调和座椅，古船模型和石刻宗教碑能让小朋友直观理解泉州为什么是海丝起点，淡季人少时可以慢慢看互动展项。
Recommended 古代石桥 landmark (洛阳桥): 免费、平坦、视野开阔，孩子可以在近千米的宋代石桥上跑动数桥墩、看筏形基础和牡蛎固基，淡季没有拥挤人流时安全又好拍。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (西街—钟楼历史街区): 全天免费，骑楼长廊遮阳避雨，面线糊、润饼、石花膏等小吃单价很低，一家人边走边吃最省预算，淡季不用排队。
Recommended 古建筑群 landmark (泉州府文庙): 门票极低甚至免费，前庭广场开阔平整，适合孩子跑动，大成殿和泮池还能顺带讲一讲读书求学的故事。
Recommended 渔村民俗村 landmark (蟳埔村): 进村免费，蚵壳砌成的老墙对孩子来说像童话房子，花少量钱就能体验簪花围拍张全家福，淡季游客稀少时村里老人也愿意多聊几句。
Recommended 城郊山岳 landmark (清源山): 门票不贵且离市区很近，老君岩石像、摩崖石刻和缓坡步道强度低，孩子有体力走完全程，淡季气温舒适、山林清静。
Recommended 妈祖庙宇 landmark (泉州天后宫): 免费参观，紧邻中山路和城南小吃区，大殿藻井与妈祖故事对孩子有吸引力，行程上可与德济门遗址连着走，几乎不产生交通成本。
Recommended 民国骑楼街区 landmark (中山路骑楼街): 全程免费，连廊贯通、路面平整，下雨或日晒都不影响遛娃，两侧老字号价格亲民，淡季晚上散步人少凉快。
Recommended 禅武寺院 landmark (泉州少林寺): 免费进入，山门到演武场一路平坦，孩子在演武场看武僧练拳最有兴致，淡季偶尔还能近距离看完整场训练。
Recommended 免费滨江地标 landmark (外滩): 全天免费开放、观景步道宽阔平坦，淡季游客少，孩子可以尽情跑动、看船看灯，几乎不花钱也很有看头。
Recommended 亲子科普博物馆 landmark (上海自然博物馆): 门票便宜，室内恐龙与标本展对小朋友吸引力大，淡季不用排长队，下雨也能安排一整天。
Recommended 低价动物园 landmark (上海动物园): 几十元门票就能看熊猫和大象，园区平坦好推车，淡季人少，孩子体力好的话一天能逛完。
Recommended 古典园林与老城街区 landmark (豫园·城隍庙): 园林门票只需几十元，街区可免费漫步，小吃便宜、选择多，还能拿九曲桥和假山给孩子讲老上海的故事。
Recommended 城市大公园 landmark (世纪公园): 门票仅十元左右，草坪开阔、可野餐放风筝，淡季空旷不挤，是低预算家庭半天的放松好去处。
Recommended 水乡古镇 landmark (朱家角): 古镇本身免费进入，地铁直达省交通费，摇橹船花小钱就有大乐趣，淡季河道清静，孩子坐船逛桥最开心。
Recommended 免费艺术场馆 landmark (上海当代艺术博物馆): 常设展免费，空间巨大不怕孩子跑动，淡季有亲子工作坊，是炎热或阴雨天的零成本备选。
Recommended 免费公共文化空间 landmark (上海图书馆东馆): 免费入馆，少儿馆藏书和互动区都很适合孩子，淡季座位充足，安静休息半天不花一分钱。
Recommended 滨江休闲步道 landmark (徐汇滨江): 全程免费，跑道和步道平整，可骑车、看江、看飞机，淡季人少，适合安排一个不赶时间的下午。
Recommended 森林郊野公园 landmark (共青森林公园): 门票十几元，林间小火车和草坪烧烤区对孩子很友好，淡季票价常有优惠、人少好拍，是低预算家庭收尾的一天。

Recommended Zoo landmark (Ueno Zoo): Tokyo's cheapest big-animal day out at 600 yen for adults with children of junior-high age and under free, and its compact loop suits small legs without needing a stroller or any mobility planning.

raw_name: National Museum of Nature and Science
surface_name: National Museum of Nature and Science
reason: Recommended Museum landmark (National Museum of Nature and Science): Hands-on dinosaur halls and a 360-degree theater keep children absorbed for hours at a modest admission with high-school age and under free, making it the best rainy-day value near Ueno Station.

raw_name: Tokyo Sea Life Park (Kasai Rinkai Aquarium)
surface_name: Tokyo Sea Life Park (Kasai Rinkai Aquarium)
reason: Recommended Aquarium landmark (Tokyo Sea Life Park): A 700-yen aquarium with free entry for junior-high age and under, paired with an adjacent free seaside park where kids can run off energy in cooler off-peak weather.

Recommended Park landmark (Showa Kinen Park): A 450-yen sprawling park with a giant trampoline-like bounce dome, bike rentals and vast lawns that gives a family a full low-cost day in the quieter off-peak months.

Recommended Museum landmark (Tokyo Toy Museum): A converted Yotsuya schoolhouse filled with wooden toys children can actually touch, with an 800-yen adult ticket and cheaper child rates that make it a relaxed, unhurried indoor stop.
Recommended Museum landmark (Fire Museum): Free admission, real fire engines and a rescue helicopter to climb around, plus a short walk from Yotsuya that fits a budget day with a child perfectly.

raw_name: Tokyo Metropolitan Children's Hall (Kodomo no Yakata)
surface_name: Tokyo Metropolitan Children's Hall (Kodomo no Yakata)
reason: Recommended Play Center landmark (Tokyo Metropolitan Children's Hall): Free indoor play floors with crafts, a music room and a rooftop area give families a no-cost backup option in Shibuya when off-peak weather turns wet or cold.
Recommended Zoo landmark (Inokashira Park Zoo): A 400-yen small zoo with a guinea-pig petting corner and a boat pond that pairs with a free stroll through Inokashira Park and a cheap Kichijoji lunch.

raw_name: Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation)
surface_name: Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation)
reason: Recommended Science Center landmark (Miraikan): Interactive robots and the Geo-Cosmos globe wow children, and discounted youth pricing plus weekday off-peak calm make it an easy Odaiba outing.
Recommended Temple landmark (Sensoji Temple): Free to enter and endlessly diverting for children, with snack stalls along Nakamise and early-morning off-peak visits that avoid the crowds entirely.

Recommended Park landmark (Park Güell): the terraces and wooded paths outside the ticketed zone cost nothing, giving kids space to climb and run while the off-peak season means short or nonexistent queues if you do pay for the Gaudí monument area.

Recommended Park landmark (Parc de la Ciutadella): a free central park with playgrounds, a boating lake with inexpensive rowboats and the Mammoth statue, ideal for a whole low-cost family afternoon with a picnic when crowds are thin off-peak.

Recommended Viewpoint landmark (Bunkers del Carmel): a free hilltop panorama over the entire city where children can scramble over the old concrete platforms, and the cooler off-peak months make the uphill walk far more comfortable than in summer heat.

Recommended Garden landmark (Parc del Laberint d'Horta): a genuine neoclassical hedge maze that turns a walk into a game for children, with free admission on Wednesdays and Sundays and quiet off-peak paths that suit unhurried family wandering.

Recommended Beach landmark (Barceloneta Beach and Port Vell): sand, shallow water and the free wooden walkway at the port cost nothing at all, and off-peak the promenade is calm enough to let kids roam without the summer crush.

Recommended Market landmark (Mercat de la Boqueria): browsing the stalls is free and cheap fruit cups or a cone of jamón make a low-cost snack stop, with the vivid colours and fish counters keeping children entertained on a short visit.

Recommended Science museum landmark (CosmoCaixa): a hands-on flooded rainforest, geological wall and touch-everything experiment rooms are built for children, entry is discounted for families and under-sixes go free, and being indoors it is a reliable rainy-day anchor in the off-peak season.

Recommended Museum landmark (Museu Marítim de Barcelona): the vast preserved royal galley and shipbuilding halls are awe-inspiring for kids and free on Sunday afternoons, plus the enclosed setting works well when off-peak weather turns.

raw_name: Barcelona Cathedral and the Gothic Quarter
surface_name: Barcelona Cathedral and the Gothic Quarter
reason: Recommended Cathedral landmark (Barcelona Cathedral and the Gothic Quarter): entry to the cathedral is free at set hours with a small donation, and the surrounding medieval lanes, Roman walls and hidden squares make a no-cost treasure-hunt walk that children enjoy.

Recommended Castle landmark (Castell de Montjuïc): free entry on Sunday afternoons, ramparts and cannons to explore and broad lawns for running about, with the optional cable car ride kept as a cheap treat rather than a necessity.

raw_name: 天坛公园 (Temple of Heaven Park)
surface_name: 天坛公园 (Temple of Heaven Park)
reason: Recommended Historical & Cultural landmark (Temple of Heaven Park): The vast open grounds and iconic circular architecture offer children a fun and educational experience at very low entry cost, especially during off-peak season when crowds are minimal.

Recommended Family & Nature landmark (Beijing Zoo): One of the most affordable and child-friendly attractions in Beijing, featuring giant pandas and hundreds of species that delight young visitors year-round.

Recommended Park & Scenic landmark (Jingshan Park): With very low admission fees and a hilltop panoramic view of the Forbidden City, it is a budget-friendly outing that captivates both children and parents.

raw_name: 故宫博物院 (The Palace Museum / Forbidden City)
surface_name: 故宫博物院 (The Palace Museum / Forbidden City)
reason: Recommended Historical & Cultural landmark (The Palace Museum / Forbidden City): Discounted or free tickets are available for children, and the off-peak season means shorter queues, making this iconic site accessible and enjoyable for the whole family.
Recommended Park & Nature landmark (Beihai Park): The affordable entry fee, peaceful lake scenery, and playful pagoda island make it a perfect low-budget half-day outing for families with children.

raw_name: 中国国家博物馆 (National Museum of China)
surface_name: 中国国家博物馆 (National Museum of China)
reason: Recommended Museum & Education landmark (National Museum of China): Free admission for all visitors makes it an ideal budget choice for families, offering child-friendly exhibits on Chinese history and culture during the quieter off-peak season.

Recommended Park & Leisure landmark (Olympic Park): The outdoor areas are free to explore, giving children plenty of space to run and play around the iconic Bird's Nest and Water Cube structures without straining the family budget.

Recommended Cultural & Lifestyle landmark (Nanluoguxiang Hutong): This historic hutong alley is free to walk through and offers inexpensive local snacks and handmade crafts, giving children a vivid taste of traditional Beijing life.

raw_name: 北京自然博物馆 (Beijing Museum of Natural History)
surface_name: 北京自然博物馆 (Beijing Museum of Natural History)
reason: Recommended Museum & Education landmark (Beijing Museum of Natural History): Very low admission fees and impressive dinosaur skeletons and nature exhibits make it a highly engaging and budget-conscious destination for young children.

Recommended Historical & Scenic landmark (Badaling Great Wall): During the off-peak season, ticket prices are lower and crowds are sparse, allowing families with children to comfortably enjoy this world-famous site without the usual hustle.

raw_name: Bua Tong Sticky Waterfalls (Nam Phu Chet Si)
surface_name: Bua Tong Sticky Waterfalls (Nam Phu Chet Si)
reason: Recommended nature landmark (Bua Tong Sticky Waterfalls): free to enter and climbable barefoot thanks to its grippy limestone, it is at its best in the off-peak rainy months when the water flows strong, and children can scramble up the tiers without any mobility barriers.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Chedi Luang): a few dozen baht gets the whole family into Chiang Mai's most dramatic ruined chedi in the middle of the old city, easy to combine with a cheap street-food lunch and short enough for young attention spans.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Phra That Doi Suthep): a shared songthaew up the mountain costs only a few baht each, the 300-step naga staircase is a fun climb for kids with no mobility limits, and off-peak mornings are cool and uncrowded.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Umong): a forest temple with dark brick tunnels and a lake full of fish and pigeons — essentially a free adventure playground for a child that costs next to nothing and stays shaded even in the low season.

raw_name: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center
surface_name: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center
reason: Recommended museum landmark (Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center): low-cost admission buys an air-conditioned, hands-on history of the city that doubles as the perfect rainy-afternoon shelter during off-peak season.

Recommended park landmark (Buak Hard Public Park): free entry, a shaded playground and a lake in the southwest corner of the old city make it the cheapest way to burn off a child's energy between temple visits.

Recommended market landmark (Warorot Market): browsing costs nothing and small portions of sai ua, khao soi and fruit let a low budget stretch to a full family tasting session, with indoor aisles that work in off-peak rain.

Recommended market landmark (Sunday Walking Street): a free-to-wander night market where 20-40 baht snacks and craft stalls keep a family evening cheap, and off-peak crowds mean a stroller and a curious child can move comfortably.

raw_name: Ang Kaew Reservoir, Chiang Mai University
surface_name: Ang Kaew Reservoir, Chiang Mai University
reason: Recommended nature landmark (Ang Kaew Reservoir): free to enter and flat to walk, this campus lake is a favourite local spot for an evening stroll or rented bicycle, giving kids open space and mountain views at zero cost.

Recommended nature landmark (San Kamphaeng Hot Springs): a small entry fee covers landscaped gardens where children can boil eggs in the springs and paddle the cooler channels, an easy half-day outing that stays pleasant in the quieter low season.

raw_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地 (Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding)
surface_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地 (Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding)
reason: Recommended Wildlife landmark (成都大熊猫繁育研究基地): 熊猫是孩子此行的最大期待，淡季清晨游客稀少可以慢慢看幼崽，成人票约55元且低龄儿童免票，园区平坦好走、全程步行即可，是低预算亲子家庭最值的一次付费。
Recommended Museum landmark (成都博物馆): 免费预约入馆，室内恒温正好避开淡季的阴冷雨天，皮影木偶展和互动区能让孩子待上半天，零门票成本最合低预算。

raw_name: 四川科技馆 (Sichuan Science and Technology Museum)
surface_name: 四川科技馆 (Sichuan Science and Technology Museum)
reason: Recommended Science landmark (四川科技馆): 免费开放（需提前网上预约），动手实验和儿童科学乐园够孩子玩大半天，就在天府广场旁不额外花交通钱，是雨天备选的头号方案。
Recommended Zoo landmark (成都动物园): 门票仅约20元、儿童还有优惠，紧邻熊猫基地可一天串起来，园内路线平坦、动物密度高，孩子体力消耗适中而花费极低。
Recommended Park landmark (人民公园): 完全免费，划船、喂鱼加鹤鸣茶社的盖碗茶，孩子有地方跑、大人有地方坐，淡季不用排队抢位，半天花费只有茶钱。
Recommended Historic Street landmark (锦里古街): 无门票，小吃单价低可以边走边吃当一顿饭，孩子走累或闹脾气时随时能出园，淡季灯笼夜景拍照也不用挤。
Recommended Historic Quarter landmark (宽窄巷子): 免费进入，老院落里的糖画、吹糖人和掏耳朵让孩子近距离接触老成都，淡季巷道宽松、推童车也不磕碰。
Recommended Park landmark (浣花溪公园): 免费开放的大片绿地与诗歌长廊，适合带上干粮野餐放风筝，与杜甫草堂相邻可顺路加一站，淡季安静正是遛娃的好时候。
Recommended Cultural District landmark (东郊记忆): 园区免费，老厂房、蒸汽火车头和铁轨对孩子来说就是游乐场，周末常有免费展览和小型演出，零成本也能耗掉一个下午。

raw_name: 金沙遗址博物馆 (Jinsha Site Museum)
surface_name: 金沙遗址博物馆 (Jinsha Site Museum)
reason: Recommended Archaeological Museum landmark (金沙遗址博物馆): 成人票约70元、儿童半价或免票，太阳神鸟金饰和原状遗迹坑足够震撼，室内参观不怕淡季天气，是唯一值得再花一次门票的科普站。
Recommended 免费滨湖绿道 landmark (洱海生态廊道): 全程免费且路面平整，孩子可以骑车、奔跑、看水鸟，淡季人少更安全，一家人不花门票也能玩上大半天。
Recommended 历史古城街区 landmark (大理古城): 进城不收费、巷子平坦好推车，淡季客栈与小吃的价格在全年最低，孩子走累了随时能回住处休息。
Recommended 白族古镇 landmark (喜洲古镇): 古镇免门票，田地在镇边、孩子能跑能看白族老院子，几块钱一个的喜洲粑粑正好贴合低预算。
Recommended 湿地公园 landmark (海舌生态公园): 免费的原生态半岛，步道平缓无台阶，孩子可以近距离看水草和候鸟，淡季几乎等于包场。
Recommended 观景园林 landmark (三塔倒影公园): 门票远低于崇圣寺主景区却能拍到三塔全景，带孩子在聚影池边看倒影玩水，是性价比最高的打卡点。
Recommended 滨湖古镇 landmark (双廊古镇): 逛镇免费，淡季海景客栈价格低很多，孩子在玉几岛边看渔船、喂海鸥，不花大钱也能住得舒坦。
Recommended 湖心小岛 landmark (小普陀): 环海路边免费观赏，天冷时成群海鸥绕着礁石小岛飞，孩子喂鸥最兴奋，停留半小时即可，近乎零花费。
Recommended 室内展馆 landmark (大理州博物馆): 免费开放且室内不晒不淋，南诏大理国文物和民族服饰讲起来像故事，是淡季阴雨天的最佳备选。
Recommended 泉水园林 landmark (蝴蝶泉公园): 门票便宜、园区不大，孩子走完全程不喊累，淡季能安静看蝴蝶标本和清亮泉眼，还可与喜洲顺路串成一天。
Recommended 山地徒步 landmark (苍山清碧溪·感通寺线): 门票不贵且不必坐索道，全家体力充裕时可沿溪徒步看小瀑布与松林，淡季山路清静，孩子有的是地方撒欢。

raw_name: Ribeira District and Cais da Ribeira
surface_name: Ribeira District and Cais da Ribeira
reason: Recommended free waterfront landmark (Ribeira District and Cais da Ribeira): a completely free, car-free riverside promenade where kids can run along the Douro while parents enjoy the tiled facades and cheap snack bars, and off-peak winter means no crush of tour groups.

Recommended free public garden (Jardins do Paládio de Cristal): free entry gardens with roaming peacocks, ducks, lawns and Douro viewpoints give children hours of low-cost outdoor play, with sheltered tree cover that holds up well on damp off-peak days.

Recommended free urban park (Parque da Cidade do Porto): Porto's largest green space offers playgrounds, cycle paths and a beach at its edge at zero cost, and out of season you have the run of it without waiting for swings or picnic tables.

raw_name: Ponte Dom Luís I (upper deck walk)
surface_name: Ponte Dom Luís I (upper deck walk)
reason: Recommended free bridge viewpoint (Ponte Dom Luís I): walking the top deck costs nothing and delivers the city's most thrilling free view for kids, and in low season you can cross without the shoulder-to-shoulder summer crowds.

Recommended free beach (Praia da Foz do Douro): a free Atlantic beach with rock pools, sand and a promenade for scooter rides that suits families on a budget, and off-peak it is quiet enough for children to explore safely.

Recommended covered market (Mercado do Bolhão): browsing the stalls is free and cheap counter snacks or market fruit keep a family lunch inexpensive, while the indoor halls double as a dry refuge on rainy off-peak afternoons.

Recommended historic station (Estação de São Bento): entry is free and the vast azulejo tile panels give children a genuinely absorbing ten minutes of storytelling, making it an ideal zero-cost stop when off-peak weather turns wet.

Recommended transport museum (Museu do Carro Eléctrico): a small, inexpensive museum of vintage trams that lets kids climb aboard historic vehicles, and its low off-peak ticket prices and indoor setting make it a reliable rainy-day option.
