Recommended Wine cellar landmark (Graham's Port Lodge): A guided cellar tour ending in a seated tasting in a cool, quiet room suits a 70-plus traveler perfectly, and the lodge's lift access and mid-range tour fee keep it both comfortable and affordable.

Recommended Museum and garden landmark (Serralves Museum and Gardens): The Art Deco villa, air-conditioned galleries and level, bench-lined park paths offer a calm, uncrowded refuge where you can alternate culture and shade on hot peak-season days.

Recommended Garden landmark (Jardins do Palácio de Cristal): Free to enter and full of mature tree cover, shaded benches and gentle downhill viewpoints over the Douro, it gives a senior companion a restful, unhurried morning away from the crowded centre.

Recommended Palace landmark (Palácio da Bolsa): The 30-minute guided tour is short, indoors, and cool, and its celebrated Arab Room can be admired from a seated position if your companion prefers to rest mid-tour.

Recommended Market landmark (Mercado do Bolhão): A restored two-level market with lifts, wide aisles, café counters and plenty of seating makes for an easy late-morning visit where you can sample local produce at medium-budget prices before the lunchtime crush.

Recommended Heritage tram landmark (Historic Tram Line 1): Riding the vintage tram along the river from Ribeira to Foz means a guaranteed seat with open-window views, sparing a 70-plus companion the long, hot walk while still covering the whole waterfront.

Recommended Seafront promenade landmark (Foz do Douro Promenade): The flat Atlantic-side walkway has ocean breezes, plentiful benches and seafood restaurants at moderate prices, making it a refreshing late-afternoon or early-evening outing even in peak season.

Recommended art museum landmark (Musée du Louvre): Pre-booked timed entry in the early morning or late-afternoon slot keeps the 70+ traveler out of the worst peak-season crush, and the wing-by-wing route with the Denon escalators, benches in every gallery and the café under the pyramid makes a half-day visit comfortable rather than exhausting.

Recommended art museum landmark (Musée d'Orsay): Its compact, clock-lobby layout on five levels means a full Impressionist sweep in around two hours with lifts to every floor, quiet seating in the Seine-side galleries and a skylit café for a mid-visit pause, all for a moderate ticket price.

Recommended Gothic chapel landmark (Sainte-Chapelle): A short, seated-friendly visit under the 1,113 stained-glass panels delivers the single most spectacular interior in Paris in under 45 minutes, and the combined Sainte-Chapelle plus Conciergerie ticket saves money without adding much walking.

Recommended historic garden landmark (Jardin du Luxembourg): Flat gravel paths, hundreds of green metal chairs and deep shade make this the ideal free mid-day refuge during hot peak-season afternoons, with the Medici Fountain and a kiosk for coffee within a couple of minutes' stroll of the gates.

Recommended river cruise landmark (Seine sightseeing cruise): A one-hour, fully seated boat ride from the Port de la Bourdonnais passes Notre-Dame, the Louvre and the Eiffel Tower with commentary, no stairs beyond the gangway and a modest fixed fare — the highest sightseeing yield per step of walking in the city.

Recommended iron landmark landmark (Eiffel Tower): Lifts run straight to the second floor with no climbing, and a reserved summit or second-level ticket in the first hour of opening avoids both queues and midday heat while keeping the cost at the standard medium-budget rate.

Recommended sculpture museum and garden landmark (Musée Rodin): The small indoor collection opens onto a shaded three-hectare sculpture garden with benches facing 'The Thinker', so the 70+ visitor gets world-class art and a genuine rest stop for one low ticket price.

Recommended hilltop district landmark (Montmartre and Sacré-Cœur): The funicular lifts you up the butte without a single stair, leaving an easy loop past Place du Tertre's café terraces and the basilica's free interior, with a seated lunch stop built naturally into the route.

Recommended opera house landmark (Palais Garnier): The guided tour or, better, an evening ballet lets the traveler sit in the gilded auditorium and grand foyer rather than stand in it, with lifts to the public floors and ticket tiers that stay within a medium budget in peak season.

Recommended royal palace and garden landmark (Palace of Versailles): A 40-minute RER C ride reaches a full day out where timed palace entry, the garden's paid little train and the Grand Canal benches reduce walking to manageable stretches, and the moderate combined ticket covers palace plus gardens.

Recommended Buddhist temple landmark (Kaiyuan Temple 开元寺): the whole complex is level ground with stone-paved paths, dense banyan shade and benches between every hall, so a 70-plus companion can rest whenever needed, and the modest ticket plus cheap noodle shops on West Street right outside keep it comfortably within a medium budget.

Recommended ancient bridge landmark (Luoyang Bridge 洛阳桥): a flat 730-metre Song-dynasty stone causeway with no steps or slopes, lined with rest pavilions and breezy over the water, making it an easy early-morning walk before peak-season tour buses arrive.

Recommended historic arcade street landmark (Zhongshan Road 中山路): the continuous qilou colonnade gives full shade and shelter from sun or sudden rain, the surface is flat and pedestrianised, and the many teahouses and snack stalls let you break the walk without spending much.

raw_name: Quanzhou Maritime Museum 泉州海外交通史博物馆
surface_name: Quanzhou Maritime Museum 泉州海外交通史博物馆
reason: Recommended museum landmark (Quanzhou Maritime Museum 泉州海外交通史博物馆): air-conditioned, lift-served, free to enter and full of seating, it is the ideal midday refuge when peak-season heat and crowds peak outside, and it explains the Silk Road port history behind every other site on this list.

Recommended Confucian heritage landmark (Confucius Temple 府文庙): a large, level courtyard with wide stone terraces, old trees and shaded side benches, quiet even in high season and free of charge, so it pairs well with a rest stop in the surrounding old-town lanes.

Recommended Islamic heritage landmark (Qingjing Mosque 清净寺): one of China's oldest mosques, compact and entirely flat with a shaded stone courtyard, it can be seen thoroughly in under an hour with no climbing and a very low ticket, leaving energy for the rest of the day.

Recommended Mazu temple landmark (天后宫 天后宫): ground-level halls, an easy circuit of a few hundred metres, abundant seating under the ancient trees and free admission make it a gentle stop, best visited right at opening to avoid the peak-season devotional crowds.

Recommended ancient bridge landmark (安平桥): at over two kilometres it is the longest surviving stone bridge in China, but it is completely flat with five rest pavilions along the span, so you can walk as much or as little as your companion feels like and turn back at any point.

Recommended scenic mountain landmark (清源山): the cable car lifts you most of the way to the Laozi stone statue so the climbing is optional, and the shaded teahouses at the top give a long sit-down with city views, though it is worth going on a weekday morning in peak season.

Recommended fishing village landmark (蟳埔村): a flat, compact village of oyster-shell houses where the famous flower-crown styling is inexpensive and done sitting down, giving a 70-plus traveller a memorable photo and a genuine local experience without a single stair.
Recommended 历史地标 landmark (外滩): 沿江是一条平坦开阔的步道，沿途有多处长椅和树荫，70多岁的长辈可以随时停下休息；傍晚亮灯后再去，既能避开白天的人潮和日晒，而且免费，符合中等预算；在旺季请避开19:00至20:00的人流高峰。

raw_name: 上海博物馆（人民广场馆）
surface_name: 上海博物馆（人民广场馆）
reason: Recommended 博物馆 landmark (上海博物馆): 免费入场，室内恒温空调，展厅里有休息座位和电梯，在旺季高温或下雨时，这里是最稳妥的半天安排；70多岁长辈可以在青铜、陶瓷展厅慢慢浏览，展牌上都配有中英文说明。
Recommended 古典园林 landmark (豫园): 园内路径平缓，九曲桥和湖心亭一带可以坐着品茶，长辈慢慢走也不费力；旺季人流密集，建议开园后第一小时入场，并在老城隍庙小吃街安排一顿慢节奏的午餐。
Recommended 水乡古镇 landmark (朱家角): 坐地铁17号线可以直达，古镇主街平坦，还能坐摇橹船代步观景，70多岁的长辈无需长时间步行就能看到完整的江南水乡景致；旺季最好在工作日早上出发，避开周末客流。
Recommended 观景台 landmark (上海中心大厦): 高速电梯直达118层，全程几乎不用走路，室内恒温又有座位，体力负担小，最适合长辈安排；旺季请提前在网上买好指定时段票，这样免去排队，门票价格也在中等预算之内。

raw_name: 武康路—衡复历史风貌区
surface_name: 武康路—衡复历史风貌区
reason: Recommended 历史街区 landmark (武康路): 梧桐成荫，路面平坦，沿途老洋房和咖啡馆密集，走累了随时能坐下喝杯咖啡或喝茶；旺季上午9点前光线柔和、人少凉爽，节奏完全由长辈自己掌握。
Recommended 游船 landmark (黄浦江夜游): 全程坐在舱内或甲板座椅上，两岸灯火尽收眼底，几乎零步行强度，非常适合70多岁的长辈；旺季请提前半天在码头或线上购票，并选带空调内舱的航班，以免受暑热影响。
Recommended 寺庙 landmark (静安寺): 位于市中心，地铁直达，寺内空间紧凑、动线短，半小时到一小时就能参拜完，长辈不容易疲惫；旺季可以选清晨香客较少的时段，而且门票价格低，符合中等预算。
Recommended 艺术场馆 landmark (上海当代艺术博物馆): 免费开放，场馆宽敞并配有电梯、休息区和咖啡厅，长辈可以在空调环境里从容看展；旺季把它当下午避暑避雨的备选，比拥挤的户外景点更从容。

raw_name: 南京路步行街与人民广场
surface_name: 南京路步行街与人民广场
reason: Recommended 商业步行街 landmark (南京路步行街): 全程平地无台阶，沿途商场密集，可随时进去歇脚、上洗手间或用餐，对70多岁的长辈十分友好；旺季建议上午逛街、午后进商场休整，购物与就餐选择多，也与中等预算相符。

Recommended Shinto shrine landmark (Meiji Jingu): Its wide, level gravel approach is shaded by a dense forest canopy with frequent benches, making it the easiest big-name sight for a traveler in their seventies, and arriving before 9am keeps the peak-season crush at Harajuku at bay.

Recommended Buddhist temple landmark (Senso-ji): The temple grounds are flat with plenty of seating and tea shops where your companion can rest, and visiting at 7–8am lets you enjoy Nakamise Street's lanterns and snacks before the midday peak-season crowds build.

Recommended Japanese garden landmark (Shinjuku Gyoen): Paved looping paths, ample benches and a sit-down teahouse make a gentle half-day stroll comfortable for a 70-plus companion, and the modest entry fee plus relaxed picnic lunch suit a medium budget.

Recommended Japanese garden landmark (Hamarikyu Gardens): A flat waterside circuit ending at the Nakajima-no-ochaya teahouse for matcha and sweets gives a seated, unhurried break, with the added bonus of arriving by the seated Sumida River boat from Asakusa.

Recommended museum landmark (Tokyo National Museum): Elevators, wheelchairs on request, benches in every gallery and an in-house cafe make the Ueno campus ideal for warm peak-season afternoons, and the samurai armor and screen-painting halls need no stairs at all.

Recommended theatre landmark (Kabukiza): Single-act 'makumi' tickets let you sample grand kabuki for a fraction of a full performance price, with reserved seats, a rental earphone guide in English and escalators to the upper lobby — a genuinely memorable, low-effort evening for an older traveler.

Recommended river cruise landmark (Sumida River Cruise): Forty minutes of fully seated sightseeing past a dozen bridges and the Skytree gives tired legs a rest and provides shade-free views without walking, and the Asakusa-to-Hamarikyu route drops you straight at the garden gate.

Recommended observation deck landmark (Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building Observatories): Free entry, dedicated elevators with staff assistance and a cafe with chairs at the top deliver Mount Fuji and skyline panoramas at zero cost, a smart fit for a medium budget in a season when paid decks sell out fast.

Recommended historic district landmark (Yanaka and Nezu): This flat, low-rise pocket of old Tokyo offers a gentle walk along Yanaka Ginza's shops, a quiet climb-free shrine visit at Nezu and frequent kissaten for coffee breaks, with none of the shoulder-to-shoulder peak-season pressure of the big districts.

Recommended food hall landmark (Nihombashi and Mitsukoshi): The basement depachika of this historic department store is fully air-conditioned, escalator-served and lined with sample counters where your companion can buy a beautifully packed lunch or wagashi without standing in queues at open-air markets.

Recommended architecture landmark (Sagrada Família): Reserve the earliest timed entry in peak season so your 70+ companion tours the nave in cooler, thinner crowds and can use the lifts rather than the spiral stairs.
Recommended modernista landmark (Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau): A flat, lift-served Art Nouveau hospital campus with shaded courtyards, far quieter than the headline Gaudí sites in high season.

Recommended museum landmark (Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya (MNAC)): Escalators carry you up to cool, bench-filled Romanesque galleries, with the Magic Fountain terraces nearby for an easy evening.

Recommended art museum landmark (Picasso Museum): Air-conditioned rooms with seating throughout in the flat Gothic-quarter streets of El Born make it an ideal midday refuge when peak-season heat peaks.
Recommended historic landmark (Barcelona Cathedral and Gothic Quarter): Cool stone interiors, cloister benches and a lift to the roof let your companion enjoy the old city on level, shaded lanes.
Recommended park landmark (Park Güell): Take a taxi to the upper Baixada de la Glòria entrance and book a timed morning slot so the uphill paths and staircases of the site are largely bypassed.
Recommended concert hall landmark (Palau de la Música Catalana): The guided tour is seated, lift-accessible and only an hour long, giving a modernista highlight without the crowds of Casa Batlló.
Recommended modernista house landmark (Casa Milà (La Pedrera)): A lift reaches the roof terraces and attic, and evening visits in peak season avoid both the heat and the worst daytime queues.

raw_name: Fundació Joan Miró and Montjuïc Cable Car
surface_name: Fundació Joan Miró and Montjuïc Cable Car
reason: Recommended art museum landmark (Fundació Joan Miró and Montjuïc Cable Car): The cable car removes the hill climb entirely, and the air-conditioned galleries with terraces suit a relaxed half-day for a senior traveler.

Recommended waterfront landmark (Port Vell and Barceloneta promenade): A flat, bench-lined seafront walk with plentiful cafés and shade makes an unhurried late-afternoon outing that costs nothing beyond a medium-budget meal.
Recommended imperial palace landmark (故宫博物院): 中轴线平坦开阔、沿途座椅与阴凉处多，提前网上预约上午场即可避开旺季正午高温，适合70岁以上长辈按两小时节奏慢慢走。
Recommended imperial altar park landmark (天坛公园): 园内古柏成荫、长椅密集且步道平缓，门票价格亲民，长辈可在祈年殿外围坐着休息看晨练，不必赶行程。
Recommended royal garden landmark (颐和园): 昆明湖东岸长廊一路有顶有座，可只走长廊与十七孔桥短线，旺季上午入园人少风凉，对年长者体力消耗小。
Recommended great wall landmark (慕田峪长城): 有封闭式缆车直达敌楼，免去爬坡之苦却仍能登城远眺，比八达岭旺季人流稀疏，适合想圆长城心愿的七旬长辈。
Recommended national museum landmark (中国国家博物馆): 全程空调室内、电梯与休息区齐备，免费预约即可参观，是旺季午后高温或阵雨时最稳妥的避暑落脚点。
Recommended imperial lake park landmark (北海公园): 环湖平路可坐游船代步，白塔与九龙壁近观即可，园内茶座多、消费不高，适合长辈半日悠闲游。
Recommended hutong waterside district landmark (什刹海历史文化区): 沿湖步道平坦并有大量树荫与长椅，可坐三轮车听讲解省脚力，餐饮选择丰富且价位适中。
Recommended Tibetan Buddhist temple landmark (雍和宫): 院落层层递进但占地不大，参拜动线短、可随时在廊下歇脚，清晨开门的头一小时人流最少，适合体力有限的长辈。
Recommended princely mansion landmark (恭王府): 庭院集中、参观路线不到两公里，室内外穿插不会长时间暴晒，旺季提前订票走早场可避开团队人流。
Recommended city museum landmark (首都博物馆): 免费预约、室内恒温并设有轮椅与休息座椅，讲解与展陈节奏轻松，适合作为旺季高温天或返程前半天的弹性备选。

Recommended Temple landmark (Wat Phra That Doi Suthep): The hilltop golden chedi is Chiang Mai's signature sight, and with the funicular lift bypassing the 306-step naga staircase, a 70-plus traveler gets the full panorama and cool peak-season mountain air without stair fatigue.

Recommended Temple landmark (Wat Chedi Luang): The ruined 15th-century giant chedi sits on flat, shaded ground inside the old city walls, so an unhurried hour of walking and photography needs no climbing and no early start.

Recommended Temple landmark (Wat Phra Singh): Its Lanna-style viharn and revered Phra Singh Buddha make it the old city's most rewarding short visit, with level courtyards, benches, and modest entry fees that suit a medium budget.

raw_name: Chiang Mai Old City Walk & Three Kings Monument
surface_name: Chiang Mai Old City Walk & Three Kings Monument
reason: Recommended Cultural landmark (Chiang Mai Old City Walk & Three Kings Monument): A gentle self-paced loop past the moat, City Arts and Cultural Centre and Lanna lanes delivers the city's history on pavement, with cafes and rest stops every few minutes during the busy cool season.

raw_name: Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden, Mae Rim
surface_name: Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden, Mae Rim
reason: Recommended Garden landmark (Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden, Mae Rim): Paved paths, canopy walkways and an internal tram let a senior visitor see orchids and highland flora at an easy pace, and the elevated Mae Rim setting is pleasantly cool in peak season.

Recommended Wildlife landmark (Elephant Nature Park): This observation-only sanctuary forbids riding and offers shaded viewing platforms and benches, giving a 70-plus animal lover an ethical, low-exertion half day with elephants.

Recommended Market landmark (Sunday Walking Street (Ratchadamnoen Road)): The old city's weekly craft and food market is flat, well lit and full of seating and snack stalls, ideal for browsing Lanna handicrafts at a medium budget without any physical strain.

raw_name: Thai Cooking Class with Market Tour
surface_name: Thai Cooking Class with Market Tour
reason: Recommended Culinary landmark (Thai Cooking Class with Market Tour): Half-day classes are mostly seated prep and tasting with air-conditioned or shaded kitchens, so a 70-plus traveler learns northern Thai dishes comfortably and takes home a skill rather than a sore back.

Recommended Scenic landmark (Bhubing Palace Gardens, Doi Suthep): The royal winter residence opens its manicured rose gardens exactly during the cool peak months, with gentle gravel paths and benches at altitude, making it an easy add-on to the Doi Suthep drive.

Recommended Scenic landmark (Ping River Dinner Cruise): An evening boat with seated dining and live music gives a relaxed, mobility-free way to close the day, and mid-range operators keep the price within a medium budget while avoiding peak-season road traffic.

raw_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
surface_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
reason: Recommended 生态 landmark (成都大熊猫繁育研究基地): 园区步道平缓，并设有观光车与多处座椅，70岁以上长辈可边乘车边看幼年熊猫，赶在开园早场（7:30）入园即可避开旺季午后人流与高温，55元门票也符合中等预算。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (成都博物馆): 免费开放、恒温恒湿，电梯和无障碍通道齐全，每层都有休息区和卫生间，是旺季正午避暑歇脚的最佳室内落脚点，还能顺带看完成都两千年通史。
Recommended 人文园林 landmark (杜甫草堂博物馆): 全园地势平坦、竹木浓荫，随处可见的廊亭与茶座让长辈每走十来分钟就能坐下歇脚，50元门票加上园内喝茶的花费，中等预算内即可从容逛上半天。
Recommended 历史古迹 landmark (武侯祠博物馆): 主轴线都是平路与低台阶，红墙竹影一段阴凉好走，对膝关节友好的同时又能满足长辈对三国文化的兴趣；旺季建议早上8点开门即入，避团客高峰。
Recommended 市井休闲 landmark (人民公园（鹤鸣茶社）): 园内全平路、树荫成片，二十几元一碗的盖碗茶可以坐上整个上午，看本地老人掏耳朵、摆龙门阵，节奏完全由自己掌控，是旺季走累了最省力的补血站。
Recommended 考古博物馆 landmark (金沙遗址博物馆): 遗迹馆与陈列馆之间为平缓连廊，室内有空调与电梯，太阳神鸟金饰等展品集中在同一层，长辈不必久站久走，70元门票含园林区，性价比适合中等预算。
Recommended 世界遗产水利 landmark (都江堰景区): 从成都东站乘动车约半小时直达，沿内江堤岸全程平路缓行，看鱼嘴、飞沙堰无需爬山，80元门票配一日往返节奏，对腿脚无碍的70岁长辈是旺季最值得的一次近郊出城。
Recommended 佛教寺院 landmark (文殊院): 免费入院、院落平坦，殿宇间都有石凳与遮阴，自带素斋与老茶馆，人流比宽窄巷子温和得多，适合旺季清晨安静地走一圈再吃顿清淡午饭。
Recommended 文化演出 landmark (蜀风雅韵川剧变脸): 全程坐席观演约90分钟、室内有空调，不必走动排队，一次看齐变脸、吐火、手影戏，晚上消遣不耗体力，中档票价对中等预算的长辈来说观感与舒适度兼顾。
Recommended 竹林园林 landmark (望江楼公园): 薛涛井一带竹荫密布、地势全平，长椅密集且游客稀少，旺季里难得的清静去处，20元文物区门票加上免费园林区，半天慢逛花费极低。

raw_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）
surface_name: 洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）
reason: Recommended 生态景观 landmark (洱海生态廊道（才村—龙龛段）): 全程为平缓的木栈道和柏油路，沿途有很多休息点与阴凉处，70多岁的同伴可以按自己的节奏走走停停，不必爬坡。洱海骑行和电瓶车加步行的组合单价低，中预算也能玩得从容。

Recommended cable-car landmark (Teleférico de Gaia Cable Car): Cabins are boarded from level platforms and staff slow or stop the gondola for wheelchair users, so a companion in their seventies gets the panorama of both banks and the bridge from a seated cabin instead of climbing the Luís I Bridge decks.

reason: Recommended Landmark landmark (Tokyo Tower Main Deck & Shiba Park): The Main Deck is reached by elevator with wide viewing aisles and seating, and the level paths through Shiba Park and the neighbouring Zojo-ji grounds let a 70-plus companion combine a classic view with a gentle, step-free walk that can be timed for late afternoon when the crowds and temperature ease.

Recommended Historical & Cultural landmark (Temple of Heaven): Its wide, flat pathways and serene morning atmosphere make it ideal for senior travelers who enjoy leisurely walks and observing locals practicing tai chi during the off-peak season.

Recommended Imperial Heritage landmark (Forbidden City): The off-peak season means smaller crowds and cooler temperatures, allowing seniors without mobility restrictions to explore the vast imperial complex at a comfortable pace with medium-budget entry fees.

Recommended Royal Garden landmark (Summer Palace): The tranquil lakeside scenery and well-maintained flat garden paths offer a relaxing and visually stunning experience perfectly suited for seniors visiting during the quieter off-peak season.

Recommended Iconic Landmark (Mutianyu Great Wall): With cable car access and fewer tourists in the off-peak season, this well-restored section is the most senior-friendly stretch of the Great Wall, accessible on a medium budget.

Recommended Religious & Spiritual landmark (Lama Temple): This beautifully preserved Tibetan Buddhist temple offers a calm, spiritually enriching atmosphere that resonates deeply with senior travelers seeking cultural reflection during the off-peak season.

raw_name: National Museum of China (中国国家博物馆)
surface_name: National Museum of China (中国国家博物馆)
reason: Recommended Museum landmark (National Museum of China): Free admission fits a medium budget perfectly, and the indoor setting with ample seating makes it an excellent choice for seniors wanting to explore 5,000 years of Chinese history comfortably regardless of weather.

Recommended Cultural Neighborhood landmark (Shichahai & Houhai Area): This flat, walkable historic hutong lakeside district offers authentic Beijing street life, affordable local dining, and a relaxed pace ideal for seniors exploring off the beaten path during off-peak season.

Recommended Imperial Garden landmark (Beihai Park): One of Beijing's oldest imperial gardens with flat, accessible paths and scenic lake views, this affordable park is especially peaceful in the off-peak season and perfect for a leisurely senior stroll.

Recommended National Symbol landmark (Tiananmen Square): Free to visit and centrally located, this iconic open square is easy to navigate for seniors with no mobility restrictions and is far less crowded during the off-peak season.

Recommended Nature & Leisure landmark (Beijing Botanical Garden): With gentle pathways, seasonal blooms, and a tranquil environment, this affordable garden retreat offers seniors a refreshing and low-stress natural escape during the off-peak season.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Phra That Doi Suthep): The 3,000-foot climb is done by car or songthaew with a lift and paved ramps at the top, so a 70-plus traveler gets the region's defining views and gilded chedi without stair climbing, and off-peak mornings mean cool air, thin crowds and easy bench breaks.

Recommended historic temple landmark (Wat Chedi Luang): Sitting flat on the ground inside the Old City walls, its 600-year-old ruined chedi and ordination hall can be circled at a slow pace in under an hour, making a low-effort, high-payoff half-day for a senior traveler at a modest entry fee.

Recommended national park landmark (Doi Inthanon National Park): Thailand's highest peak is reached entirely by paved road with a short boardwalk to the summit and the twin royal chedis, so a 70-plus visitor gets cloud-forest scenery and cool highland air in a comfortable, chauffeur-driven day trip that costs far less in the green season.

Recommended botanical garden landmark (Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden): Shaded walkways, glasshouses and a tram through the Mae Rim valley let a senior traveler enjoy orchids and canopy views at their own tempo, with benches, cafes and toilets throughout and off-peak rates making it an easy, unhurried half day.

Recommended wildlife sanctuary landmark (Elephant Nature Park): Observation-only visits with seated viewing platforms and gentle feeding stations suit a 70-plus guest who wants an ethical elephant encounter without trekking, and booking a single day in the low season keeps the cost moderate and the groups small.

Recommended art museum landmark (MAIIAM Contemporary Art Museum): A compact, fully air-conditioned and lift-served gallery with seating and a calm cafe gives a senior traveler a comfortable indoor option for the hotter or wetter off-peak afternoons, at a modest ticket price.

Recommended night market landmark (Chiang Mai Night Bazaar): A flat, brightly lit pedestrian strip with abundant food stalls, seating and taxis at hand lets a 70-plus visitor sample northern Thai food and crafts in the cooler evening hours without long walks or early starts.

Recommended walking street landmark (Sunday Walking Street): The Old City's weekly market runs on level closed-off streets past temple courtyards with plenty of rest stops and cheap street food, and the off-peak season means a noticeably gentler crowd than the December crush.

Recommended hot spring landmark (San Kamphaeng Hot Springs): Private mineral baths and shaded garden pools about 40 minutes from the city offer a restorative, low-exertion half day well suited to a 70-plus traveler, with mid-range pricing that leaves room in a medium budget.

Recommended river cruise landmark (Mae Ping River): A seated evening boat with dinner and live music glides past riverside temples and stilt houses with no walking required, giving a senior traveler a relaxed, well-priced way to see the city from the water during the greener off-peak months.

raw_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
surface_name: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
reason: Recommended 生态 landmark (成都大熊猫繁育研究基地): 园区主路平坦、有观光车代步，淡季上午游客稀少，七十多岁长者不必挤人群即可从容观赏熊猫，是此行程最不可替代的一站。
Recommended 人文园林 landmark (杜甫草堂博物馆): 园内竹木成荫、步道平缓且茶座与长椅密集，淡季门票常有优惠，长者可在诗意景致中走走歇歇而不觉疲惫。
Recommended 历史古迹 landmark (武侯祠): 祠内院落紧凑、绿荫遮蔽且处处可坐，三国故事对七十岁以上长辈有天然的亲切感，淡季游览半小时一轮不晒不累。
Recommended 世界遗产 landmark (都江堰景区): 观景电瓶车与缓坡栈道覆盖主要看点，两千年的水利工程既震撼又无需攀爬，淡季一日往返从容、人均花费可控。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (金沙遗址博物馆): 室内恒温、有无障碍电梯与充足休息区，太阳神鸟金饰对长者是极好的谈资，淡季人少、也更适合避开阴雨天。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (成都人民公园): 鹤鸣茶社一杯盖碗茶坐一下午，平地环湖、厕所与座椅齐备，最能体验本地慢生活，且几乎不花钱。
Recommended 山岳道教 landmark (青城山（前山）): 前山有索道与渡船接驳，长者只需缓步短程即可进入幽深林道，淡季清静少排队，正合七十岁长辈想要的养生气息。
Recommended 宗教场所 landmark (文殊院): 寺院平地一进进院落、香火茶座与素斋皆在同一区域，免费入院，逛完可坐下吃碗甜水面，节奏完全由长者掌握。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (成都博物馆): 免费预约、空调与电梯齐备，天府通史展可坐着慢慢看，淡季随时能约到票，是体力较松的半天最优选择。
Recommended 园林 landmark (望江楼公园): 竹林夹道、锦江岸边步道全平且游客稀少，薛涛遗迹与茶馆兼备，淡季午后陪长者散步闲坐，安静又实惠。
Recommended 高原湖泊风光 landmark (洱海): 湖岸步道和生态廊道平整开阔，可乘游船或观光车环湖，70岁以上长辈不必爬坡就能看尽苍山倒影，淡季游客稀少、船票与湖畔客栈价格也回落到中档预算以内。
Recommended 历史文化 landmark (崇圣寺三塔): 景区内电瓶车直达各殿，路面铺设平整、休息座椅密集，长辈可慢节奏参访千年塔寺，淡季免去排队与人潮拥挤之苦。
Recommended 古城人文 landmark (大理古城): 城内主街平坦、坡度轻微，茶馆与小吃店随处可见，适合傍晚缓步闲逛并在老院子歇脚，淡季住宿价格实惠且街道清静。
Recommended 白族古镇 landmark (喜洲古镇): 古镇街巷短而平、白族民居集中，可坐着品尝喜洲粑粑、看扎染与三道茶，步行强度低，淡季能安静地看清建筑细节。
Recommended 山岳景观 landmark (苍山感通索道): 乘索道直上清碧溪一带，几乎不需徒步即可赏苍山云雾与洱海全景，适合不想吃力爬山的长辈，淡季索道无需久候。
Recommended 湖畔古镇 landmark (双廊古镇): 沿湖小街平缓通畅，客栈与观景平台临水而设，可整日坐着看日落，淡季湖景房价格明显下降、拍照也无人遮挡。
Recommended 历史古城 landmark (巍山古城): 古城以一条笔直主街贯穿、几乎无台阶，南诏发祥地的老建筑与耙肉饵丝小馆近在咫尺，淡季更为清净从容。
Recommended 民俗工艺 landmark (周城村): 可进扎染作坊坐着看白族老人手工扎花、亲手体验染布，活动量小又有互动趣味，淡季作坊里能从容请教工艺细节。
Recommended 茶马古道古镇 landmark (沙溪古镇): 寺登街与古戏台一带平整紧凑，半日即可走完，节奏极慢、适合长者休养式旅行，淡季客栈价格在中档预算内且格外安静。
Recommended 佛教名山 landmark (鸡足山): 有索道与滑竿代步可直达金顶，长辈也能轻松完成礼佛与观云海，淡季香客较少、缆车与山间住宿更为宽裕实惠。

Recommended Riverside historic landmark (Ribeira District & Cais da Ribeira): A flat, bench-lined promenade with cafes every few metres lets your 70+ companion stroll at an easy pace and rest whenever needed, and off-peak it is quiet enough to enjoy the river views without crowds.

Recommended Azulejo-tiled architectural landmark (São Bento Railway Station): Free to enter, step-free and sheltered from off-peak rain, its famous blue-and-white tile panels can be admired from seating inside the hall — a perfect low-cost, low-effort stop for a senior traveler.

Recommended Neoclassical interiors landmark (Palácio da Bolsa): Guided tours are short, entirely indoors and include seats in the grand halls, making the Arabian Room and glass courtyard comfortably accessible at a medium-budget ticket price that off-peak visitors often get without queues.

Recommended Romanesque religious landmark (Porto Cathedral): With no mobility restrictions the terrace and cloister are manageable at an unhurried pace, offering one of the city's best viewpoints and shaded benches for a 70+ companion to pause between short flights of steps.

Recommended Scenic river landmark (Douro River six-bridges cruise): A fully seated, hour-long boat ride with no walking required is ideal for an older traveler, and off-peak departures are cheaper and uncrowded, with indoor saloons available if the weather turns.

surface_name: Vila Nova de Gaia port wine lodge (e.g. Sandeman or Graham's)
reason: Recommended Cellar and tasting landmark (Vila Nova de Gaia port wine lodge): Tours are seated and gently paced with warm indoor cellars, and off-peak rates plus modest tasting fees fit a medium budget while giving your companion a comfortable, cultural afternoon.

Recommended Indoor food market landmark (Mercado do Bolhão): Newly restored, level-floored and weatherproof, it lets a senior visitor sample local produce and sit down for a light meal at everyday prices, and off-peak mornings are calm rather than packed.

Recommended Contemporary art and garden landmark (Serralves Museum and Park): Paved, bench-dotted paths and a lift-served museum building suit a 70+ visitor with no mobility limits, and off-peak season brings discounted entry and tranquil galleries.

Recommended Historic transport landmark (Porto Tram Line 1): The vintage tram is entirely seated and runs along the river to the coast, giving your companion a scenic low-effort outing, with off-peak tickets and empty carriages making boarding relaxed.

Recommended Panoramic garden landmark (Jardins do Palácio de Cristal): Free to enter with gentle shaded walkways, plenty of benches and river-mouth views, it is a restful off-peak afternoon for a senior traveler who wants beauty without cost or exertion.

Recommended museum landmark (Musée du Louvre): Off-peak weekday mornings mean short security lines and near-empty galleries, and the Denon wing's lifts and benches let a 70-plus companion cover the essentials without ever standing for long.

Recommended museum landmark (Musée d'Orsay): Its compact Impressionist floors, plentiful seating in the great hall and a calm café make it the gentlest major museum in Paris for a senior companion, and off-peak tickets are easy to secure on the day.

Recommended church landmark (Sainte-Chapelle): A single short nave with chairs throughout and the finest stained glass in Europe makes this a 45-minute visit that delivers enormous impact with almost no walking.

Recommended gallery landmark (Musée de l'Orangerie): Two oval Monet rooms with central benches mean your companion can sit and take in the Water Lilies at eye level, all indoors and warm on a cold off-peak day.

Recommended opera house landmark (Palais Garnier): The guided tour is largely seated or gently paced through heated salons and the auditorium, offering grand-opera atmosphere without the cost or late night of an actual performance.

Recommended landmark landmark (Eiffel Tower): Booking a lift ticket to the second floor in low season means minimal queuing and a warm, glassed viewing level, so the ascent stays comfortable and memorable rather than strenuous.

Recommended cruise landmark (Seine river cruise): A heated, fully seated one-hour boat ride past every major monument is the single best low-effort orientation for an older traveler, and off-peak departures are quiet and often discounted.

Recommended museum landmark (Musée Rodin): The intimate mansion galleries open onto a sculpture garden with shady benches, giving a relaxed half-day of art and fresh air at a medium-budget ticket price.

Recommended historic district landmark (Covered passages of Paris): A sheltered, level stroll through Galerie Vivienne and Passage des Panoramas keeps you warm and dry off-peak, with historic tea rooms and bookshops providing natural rest stops every few minutes.

Recommended palace landmark (Palace of Versailles): Off-peak is the only sane time to visit, and the direct RER C train, on-site shuttle and audio-guided indoor route make this bucket-list day trip genuinely manageable for a senior traveler.
Recommended 佛教寺庙 landmark (开元寺): 寺内庭院平坦、古榕成荫且处处有石凳可歇脚，非旺季香客稀少，七十岁以上长者慢走参拜一两小时也不觉累，且免门票，正合中等预算。

raw_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
surface_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
reason: Recommended 博物馆 landmark (泉州海外交通史博物馆): 全程室内、有空调、电梯与休息座椅，免费开放，日晒或下雨天都是长者最稳妥的去处，一趟就能把泉州海丝脉络听明白。
Recommended 历史街区 landmark (西街): 一条平缓老街直通开元寺，边走边尝面线糊、润饼花费不高，非旺季不必挤人流，走累了几步就有茶馆可坐下歇息。
Recommended 骑楼商业街 landmark (中山路): 连片骑楼可遮阳避雨、路面平整无台阶，最适合长者饭后慢走消食，两旁老字号物价亲民，符合中等预算。
Recommended 古桥 landmark (洛阳桥): 桥面平缓、海风凉爽，往返约一公里且免费，长者无需登高即可漫步千年石桥，非旺季桥上看不到几个人，走走停停很自在。
Recommended 山岳景区 landmark (清源山): 有盘山车道可乘车直达老君岩一带，长者不必爬台阶就能近观宋代石像，门票不贵、非旺季景交车不排队，体力负担远小于想象。
Recommended 妈祖庙 landmark (天后宫): 坐落在老城平地上，殿前广场宽敞、香客不拥，免费参观后可顺路慢逛德济门遗址，适合长者安排成半日的轻松行程。
Recommended 文庙 landmark (泉州府文庙): 院落开阔平坦、廊下长凳多荫凉，长者随时可坐下休息，还能坐着听一段南音，免费入场且非旺季几乎包场。
Recommended 渔村文化村落 landmark (蟳埔村): 村内步道平坦，长者可以坐着让当地阿姨梳一次簪花围、在蚝壳厝前拍照，参与感强而花费不高，非旺季不用排队等候。
Recommended 滨海古城 landmark (崇武古城): 城墙下滨海步道平缓，长者只看海听涛、不登城墙也不吃力，建议包车或打车一日往返以免久候公交，海鲜价位适中正好合中等预算。
Recommended 滨江景观 landmark (外滩): 观景步道全程平坦无台阶、长椅与休息点密集，七十岁以上的同行者走累随时可坐下看江景，错峰季清晨与傍晚人流稀少，且完全免费，契合中等预算与无行动限制的轻松节奏。
Recommended 古典园林 landmark (豫园): 园区不大可分段慢逛，九曲桥、湖心亭一带随处可倚栏小憩，错峰季避开人潮后能从容看砖雕与假山，门票价格适中，七十岁以上长者持证件通常还能享受优惠。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (上海博物馆东馆): 室内恒温、电梯直达各展厅、休息座椅充足，无需担心错峰季的寒风或阴雨，免费预约入场，对七十岁以上同行者而言是体力消耗最低而文化密度最高的半日行程。

Recommended 江上观光 landmark (黄浦江游船（浦江游览）): 全程坐船观景、体力消耗近乎为零，甲板与舱内都有座位，错峰季船票常有折扣且不拥挤，适合七十岁以上同行者把两岸夜景一次看完。
Recommended 水乡古镇 landmark (朱家角古镇): 市区出发约一小时车程，老街沿河地势平坦，走累了就进临河茶馆坐一坐或改乘摇橹船，错峰季河道安静、住宿与餐饮价格回落，很适合长者慢节奏过一天。
Recommended 宗教古迹 landmark (静安寺): 寺院建在平地上、台阶极少，殿内可缓步参拜，出寺即是静安公园，有长椅和树荫供七十岁以上同行者歇脚，香花券花费不高，错峰日香客不多、氛围清净。

raw_name: 武康路—衡山路历史街区
surface_name: 武康路—衡山路历史街区
reason: Recommended 历史街区 landmark (武康路—衡山路历史街区): 梧桐树下人行道平缓宽阔，每隔一段就有咖啡馆与路边长椅，武康大楼等打卡点在步行可达范围内，错峰季街道安静、光线柔和，适合长者不赶时间地散步拍照。
Recommended 城市规划 landmark (上海城市规划展示馆): 全室内观展、电梯上下、每层都设休息区，巨大的城市模型对七十岁以上、熟悉老上海的同行者格外有共鸣，门票低廉且错峰日人少，两小时即可从容看完。
Recommended 自然科学博物馆 landmark (上海自然博物馆): 馆内电梯与座椅齐备、动线平缓，标本与沉浸展区边走边看可自行掌握节奏，错峰的工作日午后几乎不拥挤，票价不高，是雨天或降温时的稳妥备选。

Recommended Buddhist temple landmark (Senso-ji Temple): In off-peak months the Nakamise approach is calm enough for an unhurried stroll with your senior companion, entry is free, and the flat Asakusa lanes have plenty of benches and tea shops for rests.

Recommended Shinto shrine landmark (Meiji Jingu): The wide, level gravel paths through the shrine's forest give a quiet, shaded walk that suits a 70-plus traveler, with no admission fee and easy access from Harajuku Station.

Recommended museum landmark (Tokyo National Museum): Ueno's galleries are fully indoor, lift-served and seat-rich, making them ideal for cooler or rainy off-peak days, and the modest ticket price fits a medium budget.

Recommended garden landmark (Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden): Paved, mostly flat loops and numerous pavilions let your senior companion enjoy seasonal planting at a gentle pace, and off-peak entry is inexpensive and uncrowded.

Recommended garden landmark (Hama-rikyu Gardens): A low-cost, wheelchair-friendly tidal garden with a teahouse where you can sit over matcha by the pond, a restful half-day that pairs well with a Sumida River boat arrival.

Recommended historic site landmark (Imperial Palace East Gardens): Free admission, broad gravel paths and open lawns make this an easy morning walk for a fit 70-plus traveler, and off-peak weekdays are pleasantly quiet.

Recommended observation tower landmark (Tokyo Skytree): Lift access straight to the deck means no climbing, and on clear off-peak days queues are short, so your companion gets the full city panorama with minimal standing.

Recommended art museum landmark (Nezu Museum): A compact, lift-served collection plus a serene strolling garden, sized so a 70-plus visitor can see it all in about two hours without fatigue, at a reasonable ticket price.

Recommended performing arts landmark (Kabukiza Theatre): Single-act 'makumi' tickets let your senior companion sample kabuki affordably in a comfortable, air-conditioned seat, with English earphone guides and a Ginza location that is easy to reach.

Recommended river cruise landmark (Sumida River Cruise): A seated, enclosed boat from Asakusa to Hama-rikyu covers major sights with zero walking, an ideal low-effort option between garden visits and a good value on a medium budget.

Recommended architectural landmark (Sagrada Família): Off-peak mornings mean shorter queues and space to sit and absorb the interior, and the lift plus lift-accessible tower option lets a 70-plus traveller enjoy Gaudí's masterpiece without exhausting stair climbs, with timed tickets keeping the visit to a comfortable 90 minutes.

Recommended modernist heritage landmark (Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau): This former hospital complex is flat, uncrowded and dotted with benches and a courtyard café, making it an unhurried, wheelchair-easy half-day that suits a senior companion far better than a packed headline site, at a modest ticket price.

Recommended park landmark (Park Güell): Booking the early off-peak slot avoids the midday tour groups and heat, and the Monumental Zone's paved paths with frequent viewpoints and shaded benches let you enjoy Gaudí's terraces at a gentle pace, while the free outer park offers a low-cost alternative if legs tire.

Recommended 博物馆 landmark (中国国家博物馆): 免费预约参观、电梯直达各展厅、馆内提供轮椅借用和无障碍卫生间，作为室内场馆在淡季寒冷多风时最舒适，且有大量座椅可分段休息。
Recommended 城市广场 landmark (天安门广场): 广场为全平地面、无台阶，视野开阔且有安保人员协助，淡季提前网上预约后安检排队短，建议从附近地铁或出租车落客点近端进入以缩短步行距离。
Recommended 城市公园 landmark (北京奥林匹克公园): 中轴景观大道完全平坦宽阔、全程无障碍，可远观鸟巢与水立方而无需登高爬楼，园内电瓶车和休息区多，淡季空旷清静、适合轮椅长距离平稳推行。
Recommended 博物馆 landmark (首都博物馆): 入口设无障碍坡道、馆内电梯与轮椅借用齐备，展厅动线短、座椅密集，淡季观众少可慢慢看，票价低廉且交通便利，符合中等预算与少走路的要求。

Recommended art museum landmark (Serralves Museum and Park): Lifts to every gallery floor, ramps, benches throughout and wheelchairs available on request make it the most comfortable rainy-season indoor option, with off-peak tickets and quiet galleries.

Recommended concert hall landmark (Casa da Música): Step-free entry, lifts to all levels and dedicated accessible seating on guided tours, plus low-season ticket prices for daytime concerts that suit an early-finishing day.

Recommended garden landmark (Jardins do Palácio de Cristal): The main paved paths and terrace near the entrance are step-free and bench-lined with Douro views, and the steeper side trails can simply be skipped without losing the visit.

Recommended museum landmark (Museu Nacional Soares dos Reis): A compact, lift-served museum with a level courtyard entrance, seating in every room and a quiet off-peak atmosphere, ideal as a sheltered, unhurried afternoon at moderate cost.

Recommended art museum landmark (Musée d'Orsay): Step-free entry at 1 rue de la Légion d'Honneur, lifts to every floor and plentiful benches let a 70+ wheelchair user enjoy the Impressionist galleries at a relaxed pace, and off-peak weekdays are blissfully quiet.

Recommended art museum landmark (Musée du Louvre): The Pyramid entrance has lifts straight to all wings, wheelchair loan and companion tickets are free, and a medium budget stretches far when you pre-book a timed slot to avoid the queues.

Recommended art museum landmark (Musée de l'Orangerie): Two oval rooms of Monet's Water Lilies sit on one level floor reached by lift, making it the most compact, low-effort major museum in Paris and ideal for a short off-peak visit.

Recommended iconic monument landmark (Eiffel Tower): Dedicated lifts reach the first and second floors without a single stair, priority access for wheelchair users skips the line, and the second-floor views are more than enough without tackling the summit.

Recommended art museum landmark (Musée Rodin): The mansion's main galleries and the sculpture garden are step-free with lifts and firm, mostly flat paths, offering a gentle half-day of The Thinker and roses with frequent garden seating.

Recommended cathedral landmark (Cathédrale Notre-Dame de Paris): Since reopening, the nave is entered at ground level with no steps and free admission, giving a wheelchair user a grand, warm indoor stop in the off-peak season at almost no cost.

Recommended modern art landmark (Centre Pompidou): Lifts run to every exhibition level, wheelchairs are lent free at reception, and the top-floor panorama is reachable entirely step-free on a medium budget ticket.

Recommended royal palace landmark (Palace of Versailles): The state apartments are fully step-free with lifts and free entry for disabled visitors plus a companion, and off-peak months mean you can roll through the Hall of Mirrors without the summer crush.

Recommended river excursion landmark (Seine river cruise): Boats such as the Bateaux Parisiens and Vedettes de Paris board via ramps with crew assistance and offer heated, seated salons, making an hour of sightseeing the easiest way to see the whole city without walking.

Recommended garden landmark (Jardin du Luxembourg): Wide paved allées, level gravel paths and countless benches make this free garden an effortless, restful afternoon where a wheelchair user and their companion can stop for a crêpe by the basin.

raw_name: Vila Nova de Gaia Wine Cellars
surface_name: Vila Nova de Gaia Wine Cellars
reason: Home to famous Port wine lodges such as Taylor's, Graham's, and Sandeman, offering guided tours and tastings of the world-renowned Port wine produced in the Douro Valley.
An iconic 18th-century Baroque tower and one of Porto's most recognizable symbols, offering panoramic 360-degree views of the city from its bell tower summit.
A world-class contemporary art museum set within a stunning Art Deco villa and 18-hectare park, hosting major international exhibitions and beautiful landscaped gardens.
A scenic coastal area where the Douro River meets the Atlantic Ocean, featuring beautiful beaches, fresh seafood restaurants, and relaxing seaside promenades perfect for day trips.

The iron tower built for the 1889 World's Fair was meant to be temporary and is now the emblem of the city; ride to the second or summit level for the layout of the Seine, or return after dark when it sparkles on the hour.

Home to the Mona Lisa, the Winged Victory of Samothrace and the Venus de Milo, but also to 35,000+ works spanning Mesopotamia to the 19th century — pick two wings in advance rather than trying to see it all.

A Beaux-Arts railway station converted in 1986, with the world's richest collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist painting — Monet, Degas, Van Gogh and Manet in a space you can actually finish in an afternoon.
The Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité reopened in December 2024 after the 2019 fire, so the cleaned stonework and rebuilt roof and spire are newly visible for the first time in decades.

The white travertine basilica crowns the city's highest hill, and the lanes below — Place du Tertre, the vineyard, the Bateau-Lavoir — preserve the artist quarter where Picasso and Toulouse-Lautrec worked.

raw_name: Arc de Triomphe and the Champs-Élysées
surface_name: Arc de Triomphe and the Champs-Élysées
reason: Climb the 284 steps for the best view down the twelve radiating avenues of Haussmann's plan, then walk the Champs-Élysées toward the Tuileries; the tomb of the Unknown Soldier is beneath the arch.

Louis IX's 13th-century palace chapel holds fifteen windows of stained glass so complete that the walls seem made of light — smaller and far less crowded than Notre-Dame, and best on a bright morning.

Two oval rooms built to Monet's own specification hold his eight-panel Water Lilies cycle, with the Paul Guillaume collection of Renoir, Cézanne and Modigliani downstairs — a compact, calm counterpoint to the big museums.

The 23-hectare garden of the Luxembourg Palace mixes formal French parterres, the Medici Fountain and a boating pond where children sail wooden boats — the clearest picture of how Parisians actually use their city.

A one-hour boat ride between the Île de la Cité and the Eiffel Tower passes the bridges, the Musée d'Orsay facade and the Louvre in sequence, which makes the city's geography click into place — go at dusk for the lit monuments.
泉州最著名的佛教寺庙，始建于唐代，拥有东西两座宋代石塔，是泉州海上丝绸之路的重要见证，2021年列入世界文化遗产。
中国现存最古老的伊斯兰教清真寺之一，建于北宋时期，体现了泉州作为古代海上丝绸之路起点的多元宗教文化，世界遗产之一。
中国现存最早的跨海梁式大石桥，建于北宋，与赵州桥并称中国古代四大名桥，是古代桥梁建筑技术的杰作，世界遗产之一。
泉州保存最完整的古街区，汇聚闽南传统建筑、特色小吃与民俗文化，紧邻开元寺，是感受泉州千年市井生活的最佳场所。
始建于唐代的孔庙，是福建规模最大的文庙建筑群，保存有宋代大成殿，展现了泉州深厚的儒学文化传统，世界遗产之一。
中国现存最完整的明代花岗岩滨海石城，是重要的海防遗址，周边海岸线风景优美，惠安女传统服饰文化独具特色。
中国现存规模最大、年代最早的妈祖庙之一，是海上丝绸之路信仰文化的重要载体，世界遗产之一，香火鼎盛。
保留着独特蟳埔女习俗的渔村，以头戴鲜花簪花围为标志性文化，近年成为热门打卡地，可体验正宗闽南渔村生活与非遗文化。
宋代雕凿的全国最大天然花岗岩老子石像，高5.1米，是泉州道教文化的象征，位于清源山风景区内，山景与人文兼备。

raw_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
surface_name: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
reason: 专门展示泉州海上丝绸之路历史的专题博物馆，馆藏宋代古船及大量珍贵文物，是深入了解泉州作为'东方第一大港'历史的最佳场所。
黄浦江西岸约1.5公里的万国建筑群，与对岸陆家嘴天际线形成上海最具代表性的对景，清晨可看本地人晨练，夜晚可赏灯光夜景，建议傍晚从外白渡桥走到延安东路，一次看完白天、日落与亮灯三种面貌。
明代私家园林，玉玲珑、九曲桥、湖心亭都在其中，周边老城厢小吃集中，可一并尝南翔小笼、蟹壳黄；园内布局紧凑，建议开园即入，避开午后人流。

raw_name: 陆家嘴（上海中心、东方明珠、滨江步道）
surface_name: 陆家嘴（上海中心、东方明珠、滨江步道）
reason: 中国最密集的超高层建筑群，上海中心观光层可俯瞰外滩与整座城市的江湾格局，滨江大道适合散步与骑行，比登塔更从容地感受城市尺度。

raw_name: 武康路—衡复历史风貌区
surface_name: 武康路—衡复历史风貌区
reason: 梧桐树、老公寓与名人旧居连成一片，武康大楼是必到打卡点，周边安福路、五原路、复兴西路咖啡馆与小店密集，是理解上海日常城市气质最好的步行区。
由石库门弄堂改造的创意园区，巷道狭窄、店铺密集，保留了上海里弄的居住肌理，适合淘手作与拍照，工作日白天人少时逛感最好。
以上海石库门建筑为基础的改造商业区，中共一大会址就在旁边，可把近代史参观与餐饮购物串成半日行程，夜晚氛围尤其好。

raw_name: 上海博物馆（人民广场馆）
surface_name: 上海博物馆（人民广场馆）
reason: 青铜器、瓷器、书画三大馆藏在国内属第一梯队，免费预约即可参观，是雨天或高温天最值得安排的室内行程；东馆开放后可看更完整的展陈体系。
距市区约一小时地铁加公交可达，放生桥、北大街、漕河港水道构成典型江南水乡景观，比周庄、乌镇近，适合一日往返，清晨或傍晚游客最少。
中国内地规模最大的迪士尼乐园，创极速光轮、加勒比海盗等项目为全球独有或顶配版本，适合亲子与主题乐园爱好者，建议避开周末与节假日并提前购买早享卡。
原上海工部局宰牲场，钢筋混凝土伞形柱与迷宫式坡道极具空间感，是上海工业遗产改造中最有建筑本体看头的一处，摄影与建筑爱好者不应错过。

Tokyo's oldest temple, founded in 628, reached through the Kaminarimon gate and Nakamise shopping street. Best early morning before the crowds, and it's the clearest place to see how Edo-era religious life still sits inside a modern city.

The world's busiest pedestrian crossing, with up to ~3,000 people per green light. Nearby Shibuya Sky observation deck and the Hachiko statue make it a compact half-day stop that explains Tokyo's density better than any single sight.

A forested shrine precinct of ~100,000 donated trees in the middle of the city, dedicated to Emperor Meiji. Walk in from Harajuku station and the noise drops away within minutes — plus it borders Yoyogi Park and Takeshita Street for contrast.
At 634 m, the tallest structure in Japan, with observation decks at 350 m and 450 m. Clear-day views reach Mt. Fuji; the attached Solamachi complex covers shopping and food if the weather turns.

A 58-hectare garden blending French formal, English landscape and traditional Japanese styles. It's the best cherry-blossom spot in central Tokyo in spring and a genuinely calm picnic ground the rest of the year.

The wholesale fish market moved to Toyosu in 2018, but the outer market's stalls remain — tamagoyaki, uni, grilled seafood, knives and ceramics. Go before 10 a.m. for the freshest selection and shorter lines.
A barefoot, walk-through immersive installation of water, mirror and light rooms. It's the most photographed contemporary art experience in the city and works well with a Toyosu or Odaiba afternoon.

Japan's oldest and largest museum, holding over 100,000 objects including national treasures, swords, ukiyo-e and Buddhist sculpture. Ueno Park itself adds a zoo, several smaller museums and a pond worth an extra hour.

The former grounds of Edo Castle, open free to the public, with surviving moats, stone walls and the foundation of the castle keep. A short walk from Tokyo Station and a good counterpoint to the neon districts.

The densest concentration of electronics, anime, manga and arcade culture anywhere — multi-floor shops like Yodobashi and Mandarake, retro game stores, and maid cafés. Best on a weekday afternoon when the streets aren't shoulder-to-shoulder.

Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece and the one sight in Barcelona that genuinely lives up to the hype. Book a timed ticket online with a tower access slot — the interior forest of stone columns and the stained-glass colour gradients are the point, and walk-ins can mean two-hour queues.

Gaudí's hillside garden city, with the mosaic serpent bench and the gingerbread gatehouses. Entry to the monumental zone is ticketed and capped per half-hour, so reserve ahead; go early morning for cooler air and softer light on the tilework.

The most theatrical of Gaudí's residential commissions — a dragon-backed roof, bone-like balconies and a blue-tiled light well. The immersive visit includes an augmented-reality tablet that explains the structural and natural references you would otherwise miss.

Roman walls, medieval alleys and two cathedral squares layered on top of each other. Best done without a fixed route — wander from Plaça del Rei through the Jewish Quarter to the Roman temple columns on Carrer Paradís, ideally in the evening when the crowds thin.

Gaudí's last civilian building, with the wave-like stone façade and the surreal warrior-chimney rooftop. Night visits with projections on the terrace are a good alternative if daytime slots sell out, and the attic holds a fine Gaudí model exhibition.

Housed in five medieval palaces on Carrer Montcada, it holds the strongest collection of Picasso's formative Barcelona years, including the complete Las Meninas series. Small enough to see properly in 90 minutes and usually far less crowded than the Gaudí sites.

A whole hill of things: the Romanesque frescoes at MNAC, Miró's foundation, the Olympic ring, and the cable car up from the port. The fountain light shows on summer evenings are free and worth timing your descent around.

Barcelona's great iron-roofed market off La Rambla — jamón, fruit cups, fresh seafood and a handful of busy counter bars where you can eat lunch standing up. Go before 11am to see it working as a market rather than as a tourist corridor.

A proper city beach within walking distance of the old town, with the long promenade running to Bogatell and the chiringuitos behind it. Gets extremely busy in July and August; early morning or late afternoon is much better, and the seafood restaurants in the Barceloneta grid are worth the detour inland.

The best panoramic view of the city, from the 19th-century amusement park and Sagrat Cor church at the top of Tibidabo, or for free from the old anti-aircraft bunkers on Turó de la Rovira at sunset. Take the Tramvia Blau and funicular rather than driving.

raw_category: 世界文化遗产 / 历史宫殿
reason: 明清两代皇宫，现存世界上规模最大、保存最完整的木结构宫殿建筑群；中轴线由午门、太和殿到御花园层层递进，还能看珍宝馆、钟表馆。建议在网上提前实名预约，留出半天以上，从午门进、神武门出。

raw_category: 世界文化遗产 / 古代军事工程
reason: 最经典的长城段落，城墙沿山脊起伏，气势最足，交通也最方便（可以坐S2线或高铁到八达岭）。需要体力的游客可以选慕田峪长城，人少一些，还可以坐索道，视野同样出色。

raw_category: 世界文化遗产 / 祭祀建筑
reason: 明清皇帝祭天祈谷的地方，祈年殿三层蓝琉璃圆顶是北京最有代表性的建筑轮廓之一；回音壁、圜丘的声学设计也很精巧。清早去能同时看到本地人打太极、唱戏、抖空竹的生活场景。

raw_category: 世界文化遗产 / 皇家园林
reason: 以昆明湖、万寿山为骨架的大型皇家园林，长廊彩画、佛香阁、十七孔桥、苏州街各具特色。最推荐的走法是坐游船看湖上视角，再沿西堤慢慢走一圈。

raw_category: 城市地标 / 近现代史迹
reason: 国家象征性的中心广场，四周有人民大会堂、国家博物馆、人民英雄纪念碑。看降旗仪式或者起早看升旗都很震撼；进广场需要安检，纪念堂等场所另有开放时间限制。
馆藏140余万件，从后母戊鼎、四羊方尊到近现代革命文物，一馆就能串起整个中国通史脉络。免费预约，展厅极大，最好提前想好重点看哪几个馆，别走得太散。

raw_category: 历史建筑 / 府邸园林
reason: 清代规模最大的一座王府，曾是和珅宅邸，后为恭亲王奕䜣府邸；前府后园，萃锦园里的西洋门、大戏楼、福字碑都很有看头，是了解北京王府生活的必去之地。

raw_category: 宗教场所 / 藏传佛教寺院
reason: 清代皇家寺院，也是全国规格最高的藏传佛教寺庙之一；万福阁内26米高的白檀木弥勒大佛为镇寺之宝。香火极盛，建筑汉藏风格交融，也顺路可以去旁边的国子监、孔庙。

raw_category: 历史街区 / 胡同漫步
reason: 前海、后海连成一片水面，周边保存着成片的胡同四合院、王府与名人故居（如宋庆龄故居、梅兰芳纪念馆）。冬天可以滑冰，夏天可以坐船，傍晚在银锭桥一带看夕阳、吃小吃最合适。
由原国营798厂等老厂房改造而成，包豪斯式锯齿形厂房与画廊、雕塑、书店混在一起，是国内当代艺术最集中的地标之一，适合拍照，也适合看展，和上面的古迹形成明显反差。

Chiang Mai's signature temple, perched on a mountain ~15 km from the city with a gilded chedi, ornate naga staircase and sweeping views over the valley; a must for first-time visitors and easily combined with Doi Pui viewpoint.

raw_name: Chiang Mai Old City (moat, walls and temple cluster)
surface_name: Chiang Mai Old City (moat, walls and temple cluster)
reason: The square moated old town is walkable and dense with temples — Wat Chedi Luang's massive ruined chedi, Wat Phra Singh, Wat Chiang Man — plus cafes and guesthouses, making it the natural base for exploring on foot or by bicycle.

The best weekly night market in northern Thailand: a long stretch of handmade crafts, textiles and northern-style snacks such as sai ua and khao soi, with temple courtyards doubling as food courts. Arrive early evening for the monk alms and atmosphere.

Thailand's highest peak (~2,565 m), roughly two hours from the city, with cool cloud-forest trails, the twin Royal Chedis, Wachirathan and Sirithan waterfalls, and hill-tribe villages — a full-day trip that delivers the region's best mountain scenery.

A well-known rescue sanctuary for elephants saved from logging and tourism work; visitors observe and feed rather than ride. A responsible way to see elephants, but book well ahead as day visits fill up.

A 14th-century forest temple with dark brick tunnels, a weathered stupa and a leafy, meditation-oriented grounds with fish ponds — far quieter than the mountain temples and a favourite for a slow, contemplative morning.

Chiang Mai's modern quarter: design shops, indie cafes, galleries, co-working spaces and good restaurants, plus One Nimman's market hall. Ideal for evening eating and people-watching, especially with MAYA mall nearby.

raw_name: Bua Tong Sticky Waterfalls (Nam Phu Chet Si)
surface_name: Bua Tong Sticky Waterfalls (Nam Phu Chet Si)
reason: Porous limestone falls you can literally walk up thanks to its grippy, non-slip surface — a rare hands-on natural experience about 60 km north of the city, best in the wet season when the water flows strongly.

raw_name: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar (Chang Klan Road)
surface_name: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar (Chang Klan Road)
reason: The nightly counterpart to the walking streets: clothing, souvenirs and electronics stalls plus seafood and barbecue food halls, open every evening — useful if your trip doesn't line up with a weekend.

raw_name: Mae Sa Valley (Mae Sa Waterfall, Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden, Mae Sa Elephant Camp area)
surface_name: Mae Sa Valley (Mae Sa Waterfall, Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden, Mae Sa Elephant Camp area)
reason: A cluster of attractions along Route 1096 about 45 minutes north — tiered waterfalls with pools for swimming, the glasshouse-and-canopy-walkway botanic garden, and orchid farms — easy to combine into one relaxed half- or full-day loop.

raw_name: 大熊猫繁育研究基地 (Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding)
surface_name: 大熊猫繁育研究基地 (Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding)
reason: 世界上最著名的大熊猫保护基地，可近距离观察大熊猫及红熊猫，是成都最具代表性的标志性景点，每年吸引数百万游客。

raw_name: 宽窄巷子 (Wide and Narrow Alleys)
surface_name: 宽窄巷子 (Wide and Narrow Alleys)
reason: 清代古街保护区，融合传统川西建筑与现代餐饮、茶馆、文创店铺，是体验成都慢生活与老成都文化的绝佳场所。
中国唯一君臣合祀祠庙，纪念三国时期蜀汉丞相诸葛亮与刘备，拥有1800年历史，是了解三国文化的重要圣地。
紧邻武侯祠的仿古商业街，汇聚四川特色小吃、民间手工艺品与传统表演，夜晚灯笼璀璨，氛围极为热闹。
建于公元前256年的水利工程奇迹，至今仍在运作，被列为世界文化遗产，同时周边青城山风景秀丽，可一日游完成。
道教发源地之一，山林幽静、古观众多，被誉为'青城天下幽'，与都江堰同列世界遗产，适合登山与感受道家文化。
西南地区规模最大的城市博物馆，馆藏丰富，系统展示成都从古蜀文明至近现代的历史文化演变，免费开放。

raw_name: 金沙遗址博物馆 (Jinsha Site Museum)
surface_name: 金沙遗址博物馆 (Jinsha Site Museum)
reason: 古蜀国3000年前的皇家祭祀遗址，出土大量金器、玉器与青铜器，太阳神鸟金箔图案已成为中国文化遗产标志。
成都市中心最具市井气息的公园，以鹤鸣茶社闻名，可体验正宗成都茶馆文化、观看民间相亲角与休闲慢生活。

raw_name: 春熙路与太古里 (Chunxi Road & Taikoo Li)
surface_name: 春熙路与太古里 (Chunxi Road & Taikoo Li)
reason: 成都最繁华的商业中心，太古里以开放式街区融合现代时尚与历史建筑，是购物、餐饮、打卡网红地的综合体验区。
大理的标志性高原湖泊，环湖约120公里，沿途有才村、挖色、海舌公园等观景点，骑行或自驾环湖是体验大理最经典的方式，日出日落与苍山倒影尤为出名。
十九峰十八溪横亘洱海西岸，可乘索道上山或徒步玉带云游路，高山杜鹃、冷杉林与俯瞰洱海坝子的视角是核心看点，山上气候多变需备衣物。
明代格局的城池，五华楼、复兴路、洋人街与人民路构成主要动线，白族民居与市井生活集中，住宿餐饮便利，适合作为整个大理行程的落脚点。
南诏大理国时期留存的国家级文物，主塔千寻塔高约69米，三塔鼎立于苍山洱海之间，是大理历史地位最直观的实物见证，也是城市地标。
保存最完整的白族商帮聚落，严家大院等院落可见三坊一照壁、四合五天井的典型形制，周边稻田与破酥粑粑等小吃让古镇兼具建筑与生活气息。
洱海东岸伸入湖中的半岛渔村，客栈与观景台直面苍山十九峰，是拍苍山洱海全景的最佳位置之一，清晨与傍晚光线最好。
剑川县内的茶马古道集市遗存，寺登街与兴教寺、古戏台保存完好，商业化程度低于大理古城，适合安静住两晚感受滇西乡村节奏。
宾川县内的佛教名山，传为迦叶尊者道场，金顶寺可看日出与云海，索道加徒步的组合适合一日或两日行程，是滇西重要的朝山与观景地。
南诏国发祥地，拱辰楼与星拱楼构成十字街格局，古城生活气息浓厚，游客密度远低于大理古城，搭配巍宝山可完整了解南诏历史脉络。
苍山云弄峰下的泉水景观，因白族爱情传说与电影《五朵金花》而广为人知，园内合欢树与蝴蝶文化陈列适合与喜洲、周城一并安排半日游。

The UNESCO-listed medieval waterfront is the emotional center of Porto: narrow lanes of tiled facades dropping to the Douro, café terraces along the quay, and the classic view back up at the bridge. Best at golden hour, when the granite turns amber and the rabelo boats come in.

A two-deck iron arch built by a disciple of Eiffel in 1886, linking Porto to Vila Nova de Gaia. Walking the upper deck at sunset gives you the postcard panorama of both riverbanks and the port cellars — and the lower deck drops you straight into the wine district.

A 1906 Neo-Gothic shop with a sweeping forked staircase and stained-glass skylight, often cited as one of the world's most beautiful bookstores. Entry is ticketed to manage crowds, and the ticket value can be deducted from a book purchase.

A working 1916 station whose vestibule is lined with roughly 20,000 blue-and-white azulejo tiles depicting Portuguese history and rural scenes. It costs nothing to enter and takes only minutes, which makes it the highest reward-per-effort stop in the city.

raw_name: Port Wine Cellars of Vila Nova de Gaia
surface_name: Port Wine Cellars of Vila Nova de Gaia
reason: The lodges across the river age and blend the fortified wine that made the city famous. Guided tours end in tastings of tawny and vintage ports, and the cellars offer the coolest, most informative afternoon in the region on a hot day.

The 76-meter Baroque bell tower is Porto's silhouette on every skyline, and the 240-step climb rewards you with the tightest 360-degree view of the old town. The adjacent church interior is worth a look before or after the ascent.

A fortress-like Romanesque cathedral begun in the 12th century, with a silver altarpiece, a Gothic cloister covered in azulejos, and a terrace that frames the city below. It anchors the oldest part of town and pairs naturally with a walk down to Ribeira.

The former stock exchange, built in the 19th century, whose Arab Room — a gilded Moorish-revival hall — is one of the most ornate interiors in Portugal. Visits are by guided tour only, so plan the timing around the schedule.

Álvaro Siza's minimalist museum holds Portugal's leading contemporary art collection, set inside a 18-hectare estate with a rose garden, a surrealist pink villa, and tree-lined paths. It is the best half-day escape from the tourist core.

Where the Douro meets the Atlantic, with a long promenade, Atlantic-facing beaches, and seafood restaurants that locals actually use. A tram ride out along the river makes the trip part of the experience, and it is ideal for a slower final afternoon.

Gustave Eiffel's 1889 iron tower was built as a temporary fair structure and nearly demolished; today it defines the skyline. Ride to the second or summit level for the city grid, or see it sparkle on the hour after dark from the Trocadéro.

The world's most-visited museum, a former royal palace holding the Mona Lisa, Winged Victory and Venus de Milo alongside Egyptian, Greek and Near Eastern collections. Book a timed slot and pick two wings rather than trying to cover it in one visit.

A Beaux-Arts railway station converted in 1986, and the best single collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist work — Monet, Renoir, Degas, Van Gogh, Cézanne — under the original glass-vaulted ceiling and station clock.

A masterpiece of French Gothic on the Île de la Cité, reopened after the 2019 fire restoration. The façade, rose windows and towers anchor the historic center; the adjacent Sainte-Chapelle with its stained-glass walls is a ten-minute walk.

The white travertine basilica crowns the city's highest hill, with steps and terraces offering the widest free panorama of Paris. The surrounding village of artists' studios, Place du Tertre and steep lanes preserves the atmosphere of the bohemian era.

The climb up Napoleon's triumphal arch (284 steps) puts you at the center of the star of twelve radiating avenues, with the Grande Armée axis running to the Louvre and La Défense. The avenue itself is the city's ceremonial spine.

reason: The inside-out building by Renzo Piano and Richard Rogers houses Europe's largest modern and contemporary collection — Matisse, Kandinsky, Picasso, Duchamp — plus the rooftop view over the Marais and a lively forecourt.

Twenty-three hectares of formal French and English garden laid out for Marie de' Medici, with the Medici Fountain, sailboat pond, chess players, and chairs that invite an entire afternoon. It is the model of a Parisian neighborhood park.

Louis XIV's seat of power, 45 minutes out by RER C: the Hall of Mirrors, the royal apartments and 800 hectares of André Le Nôtre's gardens and fountains. Go early on a weekday and reserve the gardens as much time as the palace.

A hillside of 44 hectares of elaborate 19th-century funerary architecture and cobbled lanes, resting place of Chopin, Oscar Wilde, Molière, Piaf and Morrison. It works as a quiet, free, deeply atmospheric walk away from the museum crowds.
泉州最具标志性的地方，始建于唐垂拱二年（686年），是宋元时期泉州规模最大的佛教寺院。寺内东西双塔（镇国塔、仁寿塔）为南宋石构建筑，历经地震台风仍屹立，是泉州古城的天际线。大雄宝殿内有24尊飞天乐伎斗拱、殿前千年古桑，处处是海上丝绸之路多元文化交汇的实证，1982年即列为全国重点文物保护单位。
开元寺门前的千年老街，是泉州最有烟火气的所在。红砖骑楼、老字号小吃（面线糊、润饼、石花膏）、巷弄里的宗祠与洋楼混杂在一起，商业化程度相对克制，走两步就能拐进裴巷、旧馆驿等安静小巷。免费开放，清晨和傍晚光线最好，是把泉州“半城烟火半城仙”气质看明白的地方。
泉州城北的国家5A级景区，山上老君岩是宋代道教石雕，利用天然巨石雕成，高5米多，是中国现存最大、最完整的道教石雕造像。山中还有弥陀岩、碧霄岩、九日山祈风石刻等大量宋元摩崖题刻，其中九日山的祈风石刻直接记录了宋代官员为海舶祈风的历史。登顶可俯瞰整个泉州城区与晋江入海口。
北宋皇祐五年至嘉祐四年（1053—1059年）由时任泉州知州蔡襄主持修建，是中国现存最早的跨海梁式石桥。桥工采用“种蛎固基”法，在桥墩上养殖牡蛎让石缝胶结，是全球生物技术与桥梁工程结合的最早案例之一。桥上石将军、石塔、月光菩萨塔保存完好，傍晚在桥上散步看潮汐最有味道。
始建于北宋大中祥符二年（1009年），是中国现存最古老的伊斯兰教清真寺之一，也是泉州作为“宋元中国的世界海洋商贸中心”最直接的物证。留存至今的尖拱形花岗岩门楼、奉天坛残柱与明善堂，融合了阿拉伯与中式做法，门票便宜、游客不多，安静得能听见风穿过石缝的声音。
南宋庆元二年（1196年）始建，是现存建筑规模最大、规格最高的妈祖庙之一，妈祖信仰正是随着泉州港的海运贸易向外传播的。大殿的明代木构、蟠龙石柱和寝殿里的元代石构件都值得细看。庙前就是德济门遗址，旁边是城南老商业区，妈祖诞辰前后香火与民俗活动极为热闹。
明洪武二十年（1387年）为抗倭而建的石头城，是中国现存较完整的明代海防城池之一。城墙全部用花岗岩砌筑，城外就是礁石海岸与沙滩，城内还有老街和居民生活其中。惠安女的服饰与民俗在这里最容易遇到，搭配崇武海岸的日落，是泉州最出片的一站（属惠安县，距市区约一小时车程）。
晋江入海口北岸的渔村，以“蚵壳厝”闻名——用海蛎壳拌泥沙砌墙，据传壳料来自宋元时期远洋商船压舱的非洲、东南亚海蛎壳，是海上贸易留下的活化石。近年因簪花围民俗体验走红，能把渔村信仰（妈祖、顺济宫）、闽南建筑与市井生活一次看全，建议清晨或黄昏去，避开人流高峰。
泉州香火最盛的庙宇，主祀关公，因同时配祀岳飞而得名。庙不大，但终年香烟缭绕，信众抽签、问事、演戏酬神，是观察闽南民间信仰日常运作最好的窗口。与清净寺、府文庙同在一条百米内的街上，伊斯兰教、儒家、道教神明比邻而居，这条街本身就是泉州“世界宗教博物馆”的缩影。

Recommended Boulevard landmark (Passeig de Gràcia): Walking this elegant avenue to admire Gaudí's Casa Batlló and Casa Milà façades from outside is free and offers world-class architectural beauty for budget travelers.

Recommended Architecture landmark (Palau de la Música Catalana (exterior)): The ornate Modernista façade can be admired for free, giving couples a breathtaking glimpse of UNESCO-listed craftsmanship without the interior ticket cost.

Recommended Neighborhood landmark (El Born Neighborhood): This trendy, walkable district offers free street exploration, affordable pintxos bars, and a lively peak-season atmosphere that couples can enjoy on a low budget.

Recommended architectural landmark (Sagrada Família): One splurge-worthy ticket for two, and booking the first morning slot online in peak season beats the queues and the midday heat while Gaudí's interior light is at its best.

Recommended park landmark (Park Güell): The free green zones and city views cost nothing, so a couple on a budget can walk up early, enjoy the mosaic terraces from outside the ticketed core, and picnic instead of paying for lunch.

Recommended coastal landmark (Barceloneta and Bogatell beaches): Free all day, ideal for a couple in peak season who want a swim and a sunset stroll, with Bogatell noticeably calmer than the packed central sand.

Recommended historic landmark (Gothic Quarter): A self-guided wander through the Roman walls, cathedral square and hidden plazas costs nothing, and the narrow shaded lanes stay cool even in August afternoons.

Recommended viewpoint landmark (Montjuïc and the Magic Fountain): The evening fountain show is free and genuinely romantic for a couple, and you can reach it on foot or with a single cheap metro fare rather than a cable-car splurge.

Recommended viewpoint landmark (Bunkers del Carmel): A free 360-degree sunset spot above the city that suits a couple with no mobility limits willing to take the uphill walk with a bottle of wine from a local shop.

Recommended park landmark (Parc de la Ciutadella): Free to enter, with the Gaudí-designed fountain, a boating lake and plenty of grass for a cheap picnic after visiting the adjacent Gothic Quarter and El Born.

Recommended museum landmark (Museu Picasso in El Born): Free entry on the first Sunday of the month and Sunday afternoons makes it the best-value culture stop for a budget couple, combined with a free stroll through El Born's medieval streets.

Recommended historic landmark (Shichahai): free to stroll, its lakeside lanes and bridges are made for an evening walk as a couple, and you can eat cheaply at the hutong snack stalls instead of the pricey waterfront bars.

Recommended 城市观景 landmark (景山公园): 门票只要2元，是全程最省钱的浪漫性价比之选；傍晚登万春亭俯瞰紫禁城金色屋顶看日落，人少风凉，最适合旺季白天太热时的错峰约会。

Recommended 当代艺术街区 landmark (798艺术区): 园区免费、多数画廊免费，付费展览也可按需挑选；旺季室外太晒时钻进厂房展馆吹空调看展，是预算低又想有文化感的情侣刚需。

reason: Recommended 现代地标 landmark (奥林匹克公园): 园区免费开放，只看夜景不花一分钱；旺季白天酷热，晚上八点后来看鸟巢水立方亮灯、沿湖散步，是零成本又体面的收尾项目。
Recommended 传统商业街 landmark (前门大街—杨梅竹斜街): 逛街免费，小吃与老字号可以两个人分着吃来控制预算；旺季傍晚从大栅栏拐进杨梅竹斜街，咖啡馆与小书店安静凉爽，适合给一天行程收个尾。

Recommended Temple landmark (Wat Phra That Doi Suthep): The 30-baht songthaew ride up the mountain plus a tiny entry fee gives a low-budget couple the city's most iconic golden chedi and panoramic views, and the cool, clear November-to-February skies of peak season make the 300-step climb genuinely pleasant.

Recommended Temple landmark (Wat Phra Singh): At roughly 50-100 baht for two, this is the finest classical Lanna temple inside the moat, so it delivers the Old City's headline sightseeing at a fraction of what comparable attractions cost elsewhere.

Recommended Temple landmark (Wat Chedi Luang): The ruined 14th-century chedi is a five-minute stroll from your guesthouse and pairs beautifully with dusk lighting, letting a budget couple tick off a major monument without a taxi or a tour booking.

raw_name: Tha Phae Gate and Old City Moat
surface_name: Tha Phae Gate and Old City Moat
reason: Recommended Historic Landmark landmark (Tha Phae Gate and Old City Moat): Completely free and best in the dry, cooler peak season, it is the perfect anchor point for a self-guided walking loop that links the temples, markets and cafés on foot.

Recommended Market landmark (Sunday Walking Street): Handicrafts, street food and live music run for a kilometre through the illuminated Old City for the price of whatever you choose to snack on, making it the single cheapest evening of entertainment on the trip.

Recommended Market landmark (Warorot Market): Local-priced northern sausages, sticky rice and Thai sweets mean a couple can eat a full, authentic lunch for under 100 baht, and the cool peak-season weather is ideal for grazing the open-air food stalls.

Recommended Temple landmark (Wat Umong): Free entry, shaded woodland paths and eerie brick meditation tunnels give a low-budget couple a quiet, atmospheric half-day escape that costs nothing beyond the short songthaew fare.

Recommended Temple landmark (Wat Suan Dok): The forest of white royal chedi against the Suthep hills is one of the city's best free photo stops, and the temple hosts inexpensive evening meditation sessions that suit couples looking for a low-cost cultural activity.

raw_name: Ang Kaew Reservoir, Chiang Mai University
surface_name: Ang Kaew Reservoir, Chiang Mai University
reason: Recommended Park landmark (Ang Kaew Reservoir): Free to enter and popular with local students, the reservoir's sunset walk and mountain backdrop is a romantic, zero-cost way to end the day after sightseeing, with cheap campus food courts nearby.

Recommended Market landmark (Chiang Mai Night Bazaar): Browsing is free and the open-air food court allows a couple to split a few dishes for a cheap dinner, while the peak-season evening crowds and cooler air make it a lively final stop on a walking-based day.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Phra That Doi Suthep): The golden chedi on the mountain ridge is Chiang Mai's signature sight, and in peak season's cool, clear mornings a couple can share a songthaew up for a few dozen baht, getting postcard valley views for the price of a street-food lunch.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Chedi Luang): The ruined 15th-century chedi sits right in the old town, so couples on a tight budget can walk to it and pair the modest entry fee with free wandering among the surrounding lanes, and peak-season evenings give it a warm, uncrowded glow.

Recommended market landmark (Sunday Walking Street (Ratchadamnoen Road)): One long street of handicrafts and cheap grilled snacks lets a couple eat dinner, browse, and people-watch for the cost of a few hundred baht, and it only runs at full strength in the dry high season when the old town is at its liveliest.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Umong): The forest temple's walk-through brick tunnels and wooded ponds make a quiet, low-cost half-day that suits couples wanting shade and stillness, and entry is by donation, so it fits a budget trip without feeling like a compromise.

Recommended market landmark (Warorot Market (Kad Luang)): A working local market rather than a tourist one, it lets a couple assemble a full picnic of northern sausage, sticky rice, and fruit for very little, and peak-season mornings are comfortably cool for browsing the food stalls.

Recommended park landmark (Nong Buak Haad Public Park): Free, walkable from the old town's southwest corner, and full of locals doing aerobics at dusk, it is the cheapest possible couple's break between temple stops, and peak season is the one time of year the lawns are green and the air is dry enough to linger.

raw_name: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center
surface_name: Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center
reason: Recommended museum landmark (Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center): A small, inexpensive museum in the old provincial hall gives context to everything else you will see, making it a smart rainy-afternoon or rest-day stop for a couple who would rather spend their budget on food than on tours.

Recommended market landmark (Chiang Mai Night Bazaar): Open every evening, it is the reliable free-to-enter fallback after a day of sightseeing, with cheap eats and no pressure to buy, and peak-season crowds make it feel festive rather than empty.

Recommended temple landmark (Wat Suan Dok (monk chat)): The whitewashed royal cemetery and the free evening monk-chat sessions offer something genuinely memorable for a couple at almost no cost, and the peak-season sunset behind the chedi is the best free photo opportunity in the city.

Recommended Historical & Cultural landmark (Wuhou Shrine): A free or low-cost iconic Three Kingdoms heritage site perfect for couples to explore Chengdu's deep history together during peak season without breaking the budget.

Recommended Cultural & Street Food landmark (Jinli Ancient Street): Adjacent to Wuhou Shrine, this lively pedestrian street offers couples affordable Sichuan snacks and traditional crafts, ideal for a romantic stroll even in peak season crowds.

raw_name: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding (成都大熊猫繁育研究基地)
surface_name: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding (成都大熊猫繁育研究基地)
reason: Recommended Wildlife & Nature landmark (Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding): A must-visit for couples seeking a memorable shared experience with giant pandas; arriving early in peak season ensures the best viewing before crowds build up.

Recommended Cultural & Lifestyle landmark (Kuanzhai Alley): This well-preserved Qing Dynasty alley complex is free to enter and offers couples a charming, budget-friendly atmosphere of teahouses, street art, and local snacks.

Recommended Urban Landmark (Tianfu Square): The symbolic heart of Chengdu is completely free to visit, giving budget-conscious couples a great central starting point and photo opportunity during their one-day tour.

Recommended Park & Leisure landmark (People's Park): Admission is free and the park's famous teahouse culture and tranquil lake offer couples an authentic, relaxing Chengdu experience even during the busy peak travel season.

Recommended Modern Culture & Architecture landmark (Taikoo Li Chengdu): Located next to Chunxi Road, this stylish open-air complex is free to roam and offers couples a striking contrast of contemporary design beside the ancient Daci Temple.

Recommended Religious & Historical landmark (Daci Temple): Nestled within Taikoo Li, this Tang Dynasty Buddhist temple has a minimal entry fee and provides couples a peaceful cultural retreat amid the peak-season buzz of central Chengdu.

surface_name: Sichuan Opera Face-Changing Show (川剧变脸表演)
reason: Recommended Performing Arts & Culture landmark (Sichuan Opera Face-Changing Show): Affordable evening teahouse performances offer couples an unforgettable and uniquely Chengdu cultural finale to their one-day itinerary without exceeding a low budget.

surface_name: 北京国家博物馆 (National Museum of China)

surface_name: 王府井步行街 (Wangfujing Pedestrian Street)
